questions.testName: SSC CGL Tier I: Full Test - 5
questions.question: Aman's average score in a series of tests was ‘y’. He appeared in one more test and obtained score ‘z’. If Aman appeared in total ‘n’ tests, then which one of the following expression shows his average score for all the tests?
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Total number of tests taken by Aman = n.
Number of initial tests before the last one = n - 1.
Sum of scores in the first (n - 1) tests = Average × Count = y(n - 1).
Total sum of all n tests = Initial sum + Score of last test = y(n - 1) + z.
New Average = Total Sum ÷ Total Tests = [y(n - 1) + z] / n.
∴ The correct answer is [y(n - 1) + z] / n.

Alternate Method
Given:
Total number of tests appeared = n
Average score in the series before the last test = y
Score obtained in the last test = z

Formula Used:
Average = Sum of Observations ÷ Number of Observations
Sum of Observations = Average × Number of Observations

First (n - 1) tests
Sum = y(n - 1)
Last 1 test
Score = z
Total n tests
Total Sum = y(n - 1) + z

Calculations:
⇒ Number of tests taken before the final test = Total tests - 1 = n - 1
⇒ Sum of scores in the initial (n - 1) tests = y × (n - 1)
⇒ Total score for all n tests = Sum of (n - 1) tests + Score in the last test
⇒ Total score = y(n - 1) + z
⇒ Required Average = Total score ÷ Total number of tests
⇒ Required Average = [y(n - 1) + z] / n
∴ The correct answer is [y(n - 1) + z] / n.

Additional Information
Average (Arithmetic Mean)

Average is defined as the sum of all values divided by the total number of values. Formula: Average = Sum of all terms ÷ Number of terms.

Combined Average

If group 1 has n1 items with average A1 and group 2 has n2 items with average A2, then the combined average is (n1A1 + n2A2) ÷ (n1 + n2).

Net Change in Average

When a new observation is added, the new average can also be calculated as: Old Average + (Difference between new value and old average ÷ Total new number of items).

questions.testName: SSC CGL Tier I: Full Test - 5
questions.question: What is the area (in square units) of the triangle formed by the graphs of the equations: 2x - y + 8 = 0 and 8x + 3y - 24 = 0, and y = 0?
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Put y = 0 to find the base points on the X-axis: 2x + 8 = 0 ⇒ x = -4 and 8x - 24 = 0 ⇒ x = 3.
The length of the base = 3 - (-4) = 7 units.

To find the height, find the y-coordinate of the intersection of 2x - y + 8 = 0 and 8x + 3y - 24 = 0.

Multiply the first equation by 4 to get 8x - 4y + 32 = 0, and subtract it from the second: 7y - 56 = 0 ⇒ y = 8.
Area = 1/2 × Base × Height = 1/2 × 7 × 8 = 28 sq units.
∴ The correct answer is 28 sq units.

Alternate Method
Given:
Equation 1: 2x - y + 8 = 0
Equation 2: 8x + 3y - 24 = 0
Equation 3: y = 0 (This is the X-axis)

A(-4, 0)
B(3, 0)
C(0, 8)
Height = 8
Base = 7

Calculations:
⇒ To find Vertex A, substitute y = 0 into Equation 1:
⇒ 2x - 0 + 8 = 0 ⇒ 2x = -8 ⇒ x = -4
⇒ Vertex A = (-4, 0)
⇒ To find Vertex B, substitute y = 0 into Equation 2:
⇒ 8x + 3(0) - 24 = 0 ⇒ 8x = 24 ⇒ x = 3
⇒ Vertex B = (3, 0)
⇒ To find Vertex C, find the intersection point of Equation 1 and Equation 2:
⇒ From Equation 1, y = 2x + 8
⇒ Substitute y in Equation 2: 8x + 3(2x + 8) - 24 = 0
⇒ 8x + 6x + 24 - 24 = 0 ⇒ 14x = 0 ⇒ x = 0
⇒ Substitute x = 0 to get y: y = 2(0) + 8 = 8
⇒ Vertex C = (0, 8)
⇒ The distance between A(-4, 0) and B(3, 0) is the base of the triangle.
⇒ Base = 3 - (-4) = 7 units
⇒ The height of the triangle is the perpendicular distance from C(0, 8) to the X-axis.
⇒ Height = 8 units
⇒ Area of triangle = 1/2 × Base × Height
⇒ Area = 1/2 × 7 × 8
⇒ Area = 28 sq units
∴ The correct answer is 28 sq units.

Additional Information
Area of Triangle using Coordinates

Area = 1/2 × |x1(y2 - y3) + x2(y3 - y1) + x3(y1 - y2)|
Distance Formula

The distance between two points (x1, y1) and (x2, y2) is given by √((x2 - x1)² + (y2 - y1)²).

Intercepts of a Line

The x-intercept is found by setting y = 0, and the y-intercept is found by setting x = 0 in the equation of the line.

questions.testName: SSC CGL Tier I: Full Test - 5
questions.question: An electric fan lists at Rs.265.80 and is sold at a discount of 10%. The shopkeeper gives a further discount of 8% for cash payment. The selling price of the fan, when payment is made in cash, is:
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Using the multiplying factor method for successive discounts:

Selling Price = Marked Price × (100 - D1)% × (100 - D2)%
SP = 265.80 × 0.90 × 0.92
SP = 265.80 × 0.828 = 220.0824 ≈ 220.08
∴ The correct answer is Rs. 220.08.

Alternate Method
Given:
Marked Price (MP) = Rs. 265.80
First discount (D1) = 10%
Second cash discount (D2) = 8%

Formula Used:
Selling Price (SP) = MP × [(100 - D1)/100] × [(100 - D2)/100]

Calculations:
⇒ Price after first discount of 10% = 265.80 × (100 - 10) ÷ 100
⇒ Price after 10% discount = 265.80 × 90 ÷ 100 = 239.22
⇒ Final Selling Price after further 8% discount = 239.22 × (100 - 8) ÷ 100
⇒ Final Selling Price = 239.22 × 92 ÷ 100 = 220.0824
⇒ Rounding to two decimal places, SP = Rs. 220.08
∴ The correct answer is Rs. 220.08.

Additional Information
Equivalent Single Discount

For two successive discounts of D1% and D2%, the single equivalent discount percentage is calculated using the formula: D = D1 + D2 - (D1 × D2) ÷ 100.

Marked Price (MP) vs Cost Price (CP)

Marked Price is the list price labeled on an item. All trade and cash discounts are exclusively calculated on the Marked Price, whereas profit or loss is calculated on the Cost Price.

questions.question: In a Maths quiz 10 students scored 20 marks, six students scored 19 marks, five students scored 18 marks, four students scored 17 marks, and two students scored 12 marks. The average marks scored by the class (correct to 2 decimal places) is:
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Use the Net Deviation Method by taking an Assumed Average = 18.
Net deviation = (10 × 2) + (6 × 1) + (5 × 0) + (4 × -1) + (2 × -6)
Net deviation = 20 + 6 + 0 - 4 - 12 = +10 marks
Average change per student = +10 ÷ 27 ≈ +0.37
Actual Average = 18 + 0.37 = 18.37
∴ The correct answer is 18.37 marks.

Alternate Method

Given:
Distribution of students and their marks:

10 students scored 20 marks

6 students scored 19 marks

5 students scored 18 marks

4 students scored 17 marks

2 students scored 12 marks

Formula Used:
Average = Sum of all observations ÷ Total number of observations

Calculations:
⇒ Total students = 10 + 6 + 5 + 4 + 2 = 27
⇒ Total marks = (10 × 20) + (6 × 19) + (5 × 18) + (4 × 17) + (2 × 12)
⇒ Total marks = 200 + 114 + 90 + 68 + 24
⇒ Total marks = 496
⇒ Average marks = 496 ÷ 27
⇒ Average marks ≈ 18.3703...
∴ The correct answer is 18.37 marks.

Additional Information
Weighted Average

When data sets have different frequencies or weights, the weighted average is calculated as Sum(wi × xi) ÷ Sum(wi), where w is the respective frequency and x is the value.

Assumed Mean Deviation Method

A faster way to find averages involves picking an assumed mean (A), calculating total deviation (D) of all items from A, and finding True Average = A + (D ÷ N).

Combined Average

For two groups with sizes n1 and n2 and averages A1 and A2, the combined average is given by the formula (n1A1 + n2A2) ÷ (n1 + n2).

questions.question: To pack a set of books, Gautam got cartons of a certain height that were 48 inches long and 27 inches wide. If the volume of such a carton was 22.5 cubic feet, what was the height of each carton? [Use 1 foot = 12 inches.]
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Convert the given volume directly into cubic inches by multiplying by 123.

Volume in inches = 22.5 × 1728 = 38880 inch3
Since Volume = Length × Width × Height
Height = 38880 ÷ (48 × 27)
Height = 38880 ÷ 1296 = 30 inches
∴ The correct answer is 30 inches.

Alternate Method
Given:
Length (L) = 48 inches
Width (B) = 27 inches
Volume (V) = 22.5 ft3
1 ft = 12 inches

Formula Used:
Volume of a cuboid = L × B × H

Calculations:
⇒ Volume in inch3 = 22.5 × 12 × 12 × 12
⇒ Volume = 22.5 × 1728 = 38880 inch3
⇒ L × B × H = 38880
⇒ 48 × 27 × H = 38880
⇒ 1296 × H = 38880
⇒ H = 38880 ÷ 1296
⇒ H = 30 inches
∴ The correct answer is 30 inches.

Additional Information
Volume of a Cuboid

V = L × B × H, where L, B, and H denote length, breadth, and height respectively.

Surface Area of a Cuboid

Total Surface Area (TSA) = 2(LB + BH + HL). Lateral Surface Area (LSA) = 2H(L + B).

Diagonal of a Cuboid

The length of the longest space diagonal inside a cuboid is √(L2 + B2 + H2).

Unit Conversions

Since 1 foot = 12 inches, calculating volume requires taking the cube of 12. Thus, 1 cubic foot = 123 = 1728 cubic inches.

questions.testName: SSC CGL Tier I: Full Test - 6
questions.question: A hemispherical bowl of diameter 16 cm is full of ice cream. Each student in a class is served exactly 6 scoops of ice cream. If the hemispherical scoop is having a radius of 2 cm, then ice cream is served to approximately how many students?
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Total number of scoops in the bowl = (Radius of bowl ÷ Radius of scoop)3
⇒ Total scoops = (8 ÷ 2)3 = 43 = 64 scoops
Since each student is served exactly 6 scoops:
⇒ Number of students served = 64 ÷ 6 = 10.66

Ice cream can be fully served to a maximum of 10 students with exactly 6 scoops each.

∴ The correct answer is 10 students.

Alternate Method
Given:
Diameter of the hemispherical bowl = 16 cm ⇒ Radius
(R) = 16 ÷ 2 = 8 cm
Radius of the hemispherical scoop (r) = 2 cm
Scoops served per student = 6

Formula Used:
Volume of a hemisphere = (2 ÷ 3) × π × radius3

Calculations:
⇒ Volume of the ice cream in the bowl = (2 ÷ 3) × π × 83 = (2 ÷ 3) × π × 512
⇒ Volume of a single scoop = (2 ÷ 3) × π × 23 = (2 ÷ 3) × π × 8
⇒ Total number of scoops = Volume of bowl ÷ Volume of single scoop
⇒ Total number of scoops = [(2 ÷ 3) × π × 512] ÷ [(2 ÷ 3) × π × 8] = 512 ÷ 8 = 64 scoops
⇒ Since each student receives exactly 6 scoops, the number of students = 64 ÷ 6 = 10.66
⇒ Thus, ice cream is fully served to 10 students, leaving exactly 4 scoops remaining in the bowl.
∴ The correct answer is 10 students.

Additional Information
Volume of a Hemisphere

A hemisphere is exactly half of a complete sphere. Its volume formula is V = (2 ÷ 3) × π × r3.

Total Surface Area (TSA) of a Hemisphere

The TSA encompasses the curved surface along with the flat circular base. The formula is TSA = 3 × π × r2.

Volume Proportionality Rule

For any pair of 3D shapes featuring identical proportions (like two spheres or hemispheres), the ratio of their total volumes equals the cube of the ratio of their corresponding linear dimensions.

questions.testName: SSC CGL Tier I: Full Test - 6
questions.question: In a bag, the number of ₹5 coins is 8 more than the number of ₹10 coins but 20% less than the number of ₹2 coins. If the total amount in the bag is ₹270, what is the number of ₹5 coins?
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Let the number of ₹2 coins be 5y. Then ₹5 coins (20% less) = 4y, and ₹10 coins = 4y - 8.

Total value = 2(5y) + 5(4y) + 10(4y - 8) = 270.
10y + 20y + 40y - 80 = 270 ⇒ 70y = 350 ⇒ y = 5.
Number of ₹5 coins = 4 × 5 = 20.
∴ The correct answer is 20.

Alternate Method
Given:
Number of ₹5 coins is 8 more than the number of ₹10 coins.

Number of ₹5 coins is 20% less than the number of ₹2 coins.

Total amount in the bag = ₹270.

Formula Used:
Total Value = (Value of ₹2 coins) + (Value of ₹5 coins) + (Value of ₹10 coins)

Calculation:
⇒ Let the number of ₹2 coins be 5y.
⇒ Number of ₹5 coins is 20% less = 5y × (80 ÷ 100) = 4y
⇒ Number of ₹10 coins is 8 less than ₹5 coins = 4y - 8
⇒ Total value = (2 × 5y) + (5 × 4y) + 10 × (4y - 8) = 270
⇒ 10y + 20y + 40y - 80 = 270
⇒ 70y = 350
⇒ y = 350 ÷ 70 = 5
⇒ Number of ₹5 coins = 4 × 5 = 20
∴ The correct answer is 20.

Additional Information
Coins and Denominations

The total value of any denomination is calculated by multiplying the face value of the coin with the number of coins (Value = Denomination × Count).

Percentage Relationships

If quantity A is R% less than quantity B, then A = B × (100 - R) ÷ 100. This relationship is often used to find the ratio between multiple quantities quickly.

Linear Equations

Word problems often translate into linear equations format ax + b = c, where solving for the common ratio variable 'y' or 'x' gives the exact values for each parameter.

questions.question: The base of a triangular field is three times its altitude. If the cost of cultivating the field at Rs. 24.4/hect is Rs. 448.35, find its height. (in metres)
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Total Area = Total Cost ÷ Rate per hectare
Area = 448.35 ÷ 24.4 = 18.375 hectares = 183750 m2
Area of a triangle = 1⁄2 × Base × Height
1⁄2 × 3h × h = 183750 ⇒ h2 = 122500
h = √122500 = 350 m
∴ The correct answer is 350 m.

Alternate Method
Given:
Base (b) = 3 × Height (h)
Total cost of cultivating = ₹448.35
Rate of cultivating = ₹24.4 per hectare
1 hectare = 10,000 m2

Formula Used:
Area of field = Total Cost ÷ Rate per hectare
Area of triangle = 1⁄2 × Base × Height

Calculations:
⇒ Area = 448.35 ÷ 24.4
⇒ Area = 18.375 hectares
⇒ Area in m2 = 18.375 × 10,000 = 183,750 m2
⇒ 1⁄2 × Base × Height = 183,750
⇒ 1⁄2 × 3h × h = 183,750
⇒ 1.5h2 = 183,750
⇒ h2 = 183,750 ÷ 1.5
⇒ h2 = 122,500
⇒ h = √122500
⇒ h = 350 m
∴ The correct answer is 350 m.

Additional Information
Area of Equilateral Triangle

The area is given by (√3 ÷ 4) × a2, and the height is (√3 ÷ 2) × a, where a is the side length.

Heron's Formula

For a scalene triangle with sides a, b, and c, Area = √[s(s-a)(s-b)(s-c)], where the semi-perimeter s = (a + b + c) ÷ 2.

Hectare Conversion

1 hectare is widely used in land measurement and is equal to exactly 10,000 square meters (m2).

Middle diameter = (12 + 20)/2 = 16 m

Runs scored in the last 4 innings = 42, 56, 72, and 40

Average = Total Sum of Observations ÷ Number of Observations

Calculations:
⇒ Total runs in 5 innings = Average × Number of innings
⇒ Total runs in 5 innings = 58 × 5 = 290
⇒ Sum of runs in the last 4 innings = 42 + 56 + 72 + 40 = 210
⇒ Runs in the 1st inning = Total runs in 5 innings - Sum of runs in the last 4 innings
⇒ Runs in the 1st inning = 290 - 210 = 80
∴ The correct answer is 80 runs.

Additional Information
Average

Average represents the central value of a dataset. It is calculated by dividing the sum of all values by the total number of values.

Net Deviation Method

The sum of deviations of all observations from their arithmetic mean is always zero. This property helps in finding a missing observation efficiently without calculating large sums.

Weighted Average

When combining groups of varying sizes, the combined average is calculated as: (n1x1 + n2x2) ÷ (n1 + n2).

questions.testName: SSC CGL Tier I: Full Test - 7
questions.question: ABCD is a rhombus in which ∠ADB = 25°. Then, the value of (2 ∠BAD- ∠ABC) is :
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
In a rhombus, adjacent sides are equal (AD = AB), making ΔABD an isosceles triangle.
⇒ ∠ABD = ∠ADB = 25°
⇒ ∠BAD = 180° - (25° + 25°) = 130°
⇒ ∠ABC = 2 × ∠ABD = 50° (Since the diagonal bisects the angle)
⇒ 2 × ∠BAD - ∠ABC = 2 × 130° - 50° = 210°
∴ The correct answer is 210°.

Alternate Method
Given:
ABCD is a rhombus.

∠ADB = 25°

Calculations:
In a rhombus, all four sides are of equal length, so AD = AB.
⇒ In ΔABD, sides AD and AB are equal, which means the angles opposite to them are also equal.
⇒ ∠ABD = ∠ADB = 25°

The sum of all interior angles in a triangle is 180°.

⇒ ∠BAD + ∠ABD + ∠ADB = 180°
⇒ ∠BAD + 25° + 25° = 180°
⇒ ∠BAD = 180° - 50° = 130°

We know that the diagonal of a rhombus acts as an angle bisector for the interior angles.

⇒ ∠ABC = 2 × ∠ABD
⇒ ∠ABC = 2 × 25° = 50°
Now, substitute these values into the required expression (2 × ∠BAD - ∠ABC):
⇒ 2 × 130° - 50°
⇒ 260° - 50° = 210°
∴ The correct answer is 210°.

Additional Information
Properties of a Rhombus

All four sides are of equal length. Opposite angles are equal, and any two adjacent angles are supplementary (their sum is 180°).

Diagonals of a Rhombus

The diagonals bisect each other at right angles (90°) and completely bisect the interior angles at the vertices they connect.

Area of a Rhombus

The area can be calculated using the lengths of the diagonals: Area = (d1 × d2) ÷ 2, or by using the base and height: Area = Base × Height.

questions.testName: SSC CGL Tier I: Full Test - 7
questions.question: Three solid iron cubes of edges 8 cm, 10 cm and 12 cm are melted together to make a new cube. It is observed that 496 cm3 of the melted material is lost due to improper handling. The area (in cm2) of the whole surface of the newly formed cube is:
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Total volume of given cubes = 83 + 103 + 123 = 512 + 1000 + 1728 = 3240 cm3
Volume of the new cube = 3240 - 496 = 2744 cm3
Side of the new cube (a) = 3√2744 = 14 cm
Total Surface Area = 6a2 = 6 × 142 = 6 × 196 = 1176 cm2
∴ The correct answer is 1176 cm2.

Alternate Method
Given:
Edges of the three solid iron cubes = 8 cm, 10 cm, and 12 cm
Melted material lost due to improper handling = 496 cm3

Formula Used:
Volume of a cube = a3
Total surface area of a cube = 6a2

Calculations:
⇒ Total volume of the three smaller cubes = (83 + 103 + 123) cm3
⇒ Total volume = 512 + 1000 + 1728 = 3240 cm3
⇒ Volume of the newly formed cube = Total Initial Volume - Material Lost
⇒ Volume of the new cube = 3240 - 496 = 2744 cm3
⇒ Let the edge length of the new cube be 'a' cm.
⇒ a3 = 2744
⇒ a = 3√2744 = 14 cm
⇒ Area of the whole surface of the new cube = 6a2
⇒ Surface Area = 6 × (14)²
⇒ Surface Area = 6 × 196 = 1176 cm2
∴ The correct answer is 1176 cm2.

Additional Information
Total Surface Area of a Cube

The total surface area of a cube is the combined area of its 6 identical square faces. Formula: TSA = 6a2.

Lateral Surface Area of a Cube

The lateral surface area includes only the 4 vertical faces, excluding the top and bottom faces. Formula: LSA = 4a2.

Volume of a Cube

The volume of a cube represents the 3D space occupied by it. Formula: Volume = a3.

Diagonal of a Cube

The length of the longest line segment connecting two opposite interior corners of a cube. Formula: Diagonal = a√3.

questions.testName: SSC CGL Tier I: Full Test - 7
questions.question: A girl cycles from A to B, a distance of 25 km in 2 hours 20 minutes. The road from A is a levelled road for 15 km and then it slopes down to B. The average speed of the girl on the levelled road is 10 km/h. Her average downhill speed (in km/h) is:
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Total time = 2 hr 20 min = 7/3 hours
Time spent on levelled road = 15 ÷ 10 = 3/2 hours
Remaining time for downhill = 7/3 - 3/2 = 5/6 hours
Downhill distance = 25 - 15 = 10 km
Downhill speed = 10 ÷ (5/6) = 12 km/h
∴ The correct answer is 12 km/h.

Alternate Method
Given:
Total distance = 25 km
Total time = 2 hours 20 minutes = 2 + 20/60 = 7/3 hours
Distance of levelled road = 15 km
Speed on levelled road = 10 km/h

Formula Used:
Time = Distance ÷ Speed
Speed = Distance ÷ Time

Calculations:
⇒ Time taken to cover the levelled road = 15 ÷ 10 = 1.5 hours = 3/2 hours
⇒ Remaining distance (downhill) = Total distance - Distance of levelled road
⇒ Remaining distance = 25 - 15 = 10 km
⇒ Remaining time = Total time - Time on levelled road
⇒ Remaining time = 7/3 - 3/2 = (14 - 9) / 6 = 5/6 hours
⇒ Average downhill speed = Remaining distance ÷ Remaining time
⇒ Average downhill speed = 10 ÷ (5/6) = (10 × 6) / 5 = 12 km/h
∴ The correct answer is 12 km/h.

Additional Information
Average Speed

Average speed is the total distance covered divided by the total time taken. Formula: Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time.

Average Speed (Equal Distances)

If two equal distances are covered at speeds x and y, the average speed for the whole journey is given by 2xy ÷ (x + y).

Relative Speed

When two bodies move in the same direction, relative speed = |S1 - S2|. When moving in opposite directions, relative speed = S1 + S2.

questions.testName: SSC CGL Tier I: Full Test - 7
questions.question: A cylindrical vessel 60 cm in diameter is partially filled with water. A sphere 30 cm in diameter is gently dropped into the vessel and is completely immersed. To what further height will the water in the cylinder rise?
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
When an object is immersed, the volume of water displaced equals the volume of the immersed object.

Volume of Cylinder part (Rise) = Volume of Sphere
π × R2 × h = (4 ÷ 3) × π × r3
h = (4 ÷ 3) × (r ÷ R)2 × r
Given R = 30 cm and r = 15 cm. Ratio (r ÷ R) = 1/2.
h = (4 ÷ 3) × (1/2)² × 15 = (4 ÷ 3) × (1 ÷ 4) × 15 = 5 cm
∴ The correct answer is 5 cm.

Alternate Method
Given:
Diameter of the cylindrical vessel = 60 cm
Radius of the cylinder (R) = 60 ÷ 2 = 30 cm
Diameter of the sphere = 30 cm
Radius of the sphere (r) = 30 ÷ 2 = 15 cm

Formula Used:
Volume of Cylinder = π × R2 × h
Volume of Sphere = (4 ÷ 3) × π × r3

Calculations:
When the sphere is completely immersed, the volume of water displaced is exactly equal to the volume of the sphere.

Let the rise in the water level be h cm.
⇒ Volume of water raised = Volume of sphere
⇒ π × R2 × h = (4 ÷ 3) × π × r3
⇒ π × (30)² × h = (4 ÷ 3) × π × (15)³

Cancel π from both sides:

⇒ 900 × h = (4 ÷ 3) × 3375
⇒ 900 × h = 4 × 1125
⇒ 900 × h = 4500
⇒ h = 4500 ÷ 900
⇒ h = 5 cm
∴ The correct answer is 5 cm.

Additional Information
Archimedes' Principle (Volume Displacement)

When an object is completely submerged in a fluid, it displaces a volume of fluid exactly equal to its own volume regardless of its shape.

Surface Area of Sphere

Total Surface Area (TSA) = 4 × π × r2

Cylinder Area Properties

Curved Surface Area (CSA) = 2 × π × r × h | Total Surface Area (TSA) = 2 × π × r × (r + h)

questions.testName: SSC CGL Tier I: Full Test - 7
questions.question: Sampark Kranti Express left Delhi for Chennai at 14:30 hours, travelling at a speed of 75 km/h, while Rajdhani Express left Delhi for Chennai on the same day at 16:30 hours, travelling at a speed of 90 km/h, travelling on the same route. How far away from Delhi will the two trains meet?
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Direct formula for meeting distance: D = [S1 × S2 × Time Difference] ÷ (S2 - S1)
Here, S1 = 75 km/h, S2 = 90 km/h, and Time Difference = 16:30 - 14:30 = 2 hours.
D = [75 × 90 × 2] ÷ (90 - 75)
D = 13500 ÷ 15
D = 900 km
∴ The correct answer is 900 km.

Alternate Method
Given:
Speed of Sampark Kranti Express = 75 km/h
Departure time of Sampark Kranti = 14:30 hours
Speed of Rajdhani Express = 90 km/h
Departure time of Rajdhani = 16:30 hours

Formula Used:
Distance = Speed × Time
Relative Speed (same direction) = S1 - S2

Calculations:
⇒ Time difference between the departures = 16:30 - 14:30 = 2 hours.
⇒ Distance covered by Sampark Kranti Express in these 2 hours = 75 × 2 = 150 km.
⇒ This 150 km is the head start distance between the two trains.
⇒ Relative speed of Rajdhani Express with respect to Sampark Kranti = 90 - 75 = 15 km/h.
⇒ Time taken by Rajdhani Express to catch up = Distance ÷ Relative speed.
⇒ Catch up time = 150 ÷ 15 = 10 hours.
⇒ The meeting distance from Delhi = Speed of Rajdhani × Time taken.
⇒ Distance = 90 × 10 = 900 km.
∴ The correct answer is 900 km.

Additional Information
Relative Speed

When two objects move in the same direction, their relative speed is the difference of their individual speeds (S1 - S2). When they move in opposite directions, it is the sum of their speeds (S1 + S2).

Catch-up Time Formula

Time to meet = Head start distance ÷ Relative speed. This determines the duration required for the faster object to overtake the slower one.

Average Speed

When a journey covers two equal halves at different speeds S1 and S2, Average Speed = (2 × S1 × S2) ÷ (S1 + S2).

questions.testName: SSC CGL Tier I: Full Test - 7
questions.question: Vineet buys 2 chairs for Rs. 1500. He sold one at 20% profit and the other at 17.5% loss. On the whole, he receives neither loss nor profit. What was the cost of each chair?
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Since the overall transaction results in 0% profit/loss, the profit amount equals the loss amount.

⇒ 20% of CP1 = 17.5% of CP2
⇒ Ratio of CP1 : CP2 = 17.5 : 20 = 7 : 8
⇒ CP1 = (7 ÷ 15) × 1500 = Rs. 700 & CP2 = (8 ÷ 15) × 1500 = Rs. 800
∴ The correct answer is Rs. 700, Rs. 800.

Alternate Method
Given:
Total Cost Price of two chairs = Rs. 1500
Profit on first chair = 20%
Loss on second chair = 17.5%
Net profit or loss = 0%

Formula Used:
When an overall transaction yields neither profit nor loss, the absolute profit earned on one item is exactly equal to the loss incurred on the other item.

Calculations:
⇒ Let the CP of the first chair be x and the second chair be y.
⇒ x + y = 1500
⇒ 20% of x = 17.5% of y
⇒ x ÷ y = 17.5 ÷ 20 = 175 ÷ 200
⇒ x ÷ y = 7 ÷ 8
⇒ Ratio of CP of first chair to second chair = 7 : 8
⇒ Total ratio parts = 7 + 8 = 15
⇒ 15 parts = 1500 ⇒ 1 part = 100
⇒ CP of first chair = 7 × 100 = Rs. 700
⇒ CP of second chair = 8 × 100 = Rs. 800
∴ The correct answer is Rs. 700, Rs. 800.

Additional Information
No Profit No Loss Condition

When a transaction results in no profit and no loss overall, the absolute profit earned on one item is exactly equal to the absolute loss on the other item.

Alligation Cross Method

Used for finding the ratio of base values (like Cost Price) when individual percentages and overall average percentage are given. CP Ratio = (Net % - Loss %) : (Profit % - Net %).

Base of Profit and Loss

Both profit percentage and loss percentage are always calculated on the Cost Price (CP) unless specifically stated otherwise. Profit = SP - CP and Loss = CP - SP.

questions.testName: SSC CGL Tier I: Full Test - 7
questions.question: The denominator of a rational number is greater than the numerator by 10. If the numerator is increased by 1 and the denominator is decreased by 1, then expression for new denominator is _________. (where n is the numerator of the fraction)
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Let the numerator of the rational number be n.

The original denominator is 10 more than the numerator, which is n + 10.

When the denominator is decreased by 1, the new denominator becomes (n + 10) - 1.

Simplifying the expression, we get n + 9.

∴ The correct answer is n + 9.

Alternate Method
n
n + 10
Original Fraction
Num + 1
Den - 1
n + 1
n + 9
New Fraction
New Denominator = n + 10 - 1 = n + 9

Given:
⇒ The denominator of a rational number is greater than the numerator by 10.
⇒ The numerator is increased by 1.
⇒ The denominator is decreased by 1.

Calculation:
⇒ Let the numerator of the original rational number be n.
⇒ Original Denominator = n + 10
⇒ Original Rational Number = n / (n + 10)
⇒ The new denominator is formed by subtracting 1 from the original denominator.
⇒ New Denominator = Original Denominator - 1
⇒ New Denominator = (n + 10) - 1
⇒ New Denominator = n + 9
∴ The correct answer is n + 9.

Additional Information
Rational Numbers

A rational number is any number that can be expressed as a fraction p/q, where p and q are integers and q is not equal to zero.

Fraction Modification

If a fraction is represented as x/y, increasing the numerator by 'a' and decreasing the denominator by 'b' results in a new fraction expressed as (x + a) / (y - b).

Simplification of Algebraic Expressions

Simplifying algebraic expressions involves grouping and combining like terms. For constant numbers, basic arithmetic operations are applied directly, e.g., (n + a) - b = n + (a - b).

questions.testName: SSC CGL Tier I: Full Test - 7
questions.question: There are 12 men on a Basketball team and in a game 5 of them play at any one time. If the game is 1 hour long and if each man plays exactly the same amount of time, how many minutes does each man play?
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Total active playing time on the court = Number of active players × Game duration.
Total playing time = 5 × 60 = 300 minutes.

Since this playing time is exactly equally distributed among all 12 players, we divide the total time by 12.

Time per player = 300 ÷ 12 = 25 minutes.
∴ The correct answer is 25 minutes.

Alternate Method
Given:
Total players on the basketball team = 12
Number of players active on the court at any one time = 5
Duration of the game = 1 hour = 60 minutes

Formula Used:
Total player-minutes = Number of active players × Game duration
Time per player = Total player-minutes ÷ Total number of players

Calculations:
⇒ Total player-minutes = 5 × 60
⇒ Total player-minutes = 300 minutes
⇒ As the total court time is shared equally among 12 players, we divide the total minutes by 12.
⇒ Time per player = 300 ÷ 12
⇒ Time per player = 25 minutes
∴ The correct answer is 25 minutes.

Additional Information
Man-Hours Concept

When an activity requires a constant number of individuals active at all times, the total accumulated effort is the product of the active individuals and the duration: Total Time = Active Members × Duration.

Equal Distribution (Average)

If a total continuous resource must be shared exactly equally among a group, the amount received per individual is calculated as Average = Total Quantity ÷ Total Number of Individuals.

questions.testName: SSC CGL Tier I: Full Test - 7
questions.question: In a group of 260 people, one-fourth are women, two-fifth are men and the rest are children. The average age of women is five-sixth of the average age of men, average age of children is one-third of the average age of men. If the average age of men is 48 years, what is the average age of the group in years?
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
We can find the average directly using fractions without calculating the total number of people.

Fraction of Women = 1/4, Men = 2/5 ⇒ Children = 1 - (1/4 + 2/5) = 1 - 13/20 = 7/20.
Average age of Men = 48 years.
Average age of Women = 5/6 × 48 = 40 years | Average age of Children = 1/3 × 48 = 16 years.
Group Average = (1/4 × 40) + (2/5 × 48) + (7/20 × 16) = 10 + 19.2 + 5.6 = 34.8.
∴ The correct answer is 34.8 years.

Alternate Method
Given:
Total people = 260
Number of Women = 1/4 of 260 = 65
Number of Men = 2/5 of 260 = 104
Number of Children = 260 - (65 + 104) = 91
Average age of Men = 48 years
Total Group (260 people)
Women (1/4)
Avg: 40
Men (2/5)
Avg: 48
Children (7/20)
Avg: 16
Weighted Average Calculation
Group Avg = 34.8 years

Formula Used:
Average = (Sum of all observations) ÷ (Total number of observations)

Calculations:
⇒ Average age of Women = 5/6 × 48 = 40 years
⇒ Average age of Children = 1/3 × 48 = 16 years
⇒ Total age of Women = 65 × 40 = 2600
⇒ Total age of Men = 104 × 48 = 4992
⇒ Total age of Children = 91 × 16 = 1456
⇒ Total age of the group = 2600 + 4992 + 1456 = 9048
⇒ Average age of the group = 9048 ÷ 260
⇒ Average = 34.8 years
∴ The correct answer is 34.8 years.

Additional Information
Weighted Average Method

When different sub-groups have unique averages, the overall combined average is calculated as (N1A1 + N2A2 + ...) ÷ (N1 + N2 + ...).

Independence from Absolute Totals

If the relative ratios or percentage fractions of multiple groups are known along with their respective averages, the overall average remains constant regardless of the actual base population size.

Properties of Averages

If all individual items in a data set are multiplied or divided by a specific constant, the overall average of the data set will also be multiplied or divided by that same constant.

questions.question: While listing N consecutive even numbers for determining their average, the last number, by mistake, got replaced by the next odd number and thereby the average turned out to be more than the desired value by 0.0125. What is the value of N?
questions.solution:
Solution
Shortcut Trick
The next odd number after any even number L is L + 1.

Total Increase in Sum = (L + 1) - L = 1.
Increase in Average = (Total Increase in Sum) ÷ (Number of Terms N).
0.0125 = 1 ÷ N
N = 1 ÷ 0.0125 = 80.
∴ The correct answer is 80.

Alternate Method
Given:
Number of consecutive even numbers = N
Error: Last even number replaced by next odd number
Increase in average = 0.0125

Calculations:
⇒ Let the N consecutive even numbers be E1, E2, ..., EN.
⇒ Let their original sum be S.
⇒ Original Average = S ÷ N.
⇒ The last number EN is replaced by (EN + 1).
⇒ New Sum = S - EN + (EN + 1) = S + 1.
⇒ New Average = (S + 1) ÷ N = (S ÷ N) + (1 ÷ N).
⇒ Change in average = (New Average) - (Original Average) = 1 ÷ N.
⇒ Given that this change is 0.0125.
⇒ 1 ÷ N = 0.0125
⇒ N = 1 ÷ 0.0125
⇒ N = 10000 ÷ 125 = 80.
∴ The correct answer is 80.

Additional Information
Effect of Observation Change on Average

If a single observation in a set of N terms is increased by 'k', the new average increases by exactly k ÷ N compared to the old average.

Consecutive Even Numbers

Consecutive even numbers form an Arithmetic Progression (AP) with a common difference of 2. The average of any N consecutive numbers in an AP is (First term + Last term) ÷ 2.

Decimal to Fraction Conversion

Shortcut for N: Since 0.125 = 1/8, then 0.0125 = 1/80. Therefore, 1 ÷ N = 1 ÷ 80 implies N = 80.

questions.question: In a company, there are only two types of employees, workers, and officers. 35% of the employees are officers and the average monthly salary of an officer is ₹39,000 more than the combined average monthly salary of all employees. What is the difference between the average monthly salaries of an officer and a worker?
questions.solution:
Solution
Shortcut Trick
Ratio of Officers : Workers = 35% : 65% = 7 : 13.
Deviation of Officer's salary from the combined average = +₹39,000.
Applying the net deviation rule: Sum of deviations = 0.
7 × (+39,000) + 13 × (Worker's deviation) = 0.
Worker's deviation = -(7 × 39,000) ÷ 13 = -₹21,000.
Total difference = Officer's surplus + Worker's deficit = 39,000 + 21,000 = ₹60,000.
∴ The correct answer is ₹60,000.

Alternate Method
Given:
Percentage of Officers = 35%
Percentage of Workers = 100% - 35% = 65%
AvgOfficer - AvgTotal = ₹39,000

Formula Used:
Weighted Average: n1(A1 - Aavg) = n2(Aavg - A2)

Calculations:
⇒ Ratio of Officers (nO) to Workers (nW) = 35 : 65 = 7 : 13
⇒ Let AvgTotal be A, then AvgOfficer = A + 39,000
⇒ Let AvgWorker be AW
⇒ 7 × (AvgOfficer - A) = 13 × (A - AvgWorker)
⇒ 7 × (39,000) = 13 × (A - AvgWorker)
⇒ A - AvgWorker = (7 × 39,000) ÷ 13
⇒ A - AvgWorker = 7 × 3,000 = 21,000
⇒ Difference = AvgOfficer - AvgWorker
⇒ Difference = (AvgOfficer - A) + (A - AvgWorker)
⇒ Difference = 39,000 + 21,000 = 60,000
∴ The correct answer is ₹60,000.

Additional Information
Alligation Rule for Averages

The ratio of the quantities of two groups is the inverse ratio of the differences of their individual averages from the combined average: n1/n2 = (A2 - Aavg) / (Aavg - A1).

Net Deviation Method

In any distribution, the sum of the products of the frequency and the deviation of each value from the mean is always zero: ∑ fi(xi - x̄) = 0.

Weighted Average Formula

The combined average of two groups is given by Aavg = (n1A1 + n2A2) / (n1 + n2), where n represents the number of items and A represents the average.

questions.question: In the set of first 100 multiples of 5, P is the average of the multiples on the odd places and Q is the average of the multiples on the even places. By what number, the value of Q is more than P?
questions.solution:
Solution
Shortcut Trick
Each even-placed multiple is exactly 5 more than its preceding odd-placed multiple.

Multiples: (5, 10), (15, 20), (25, 30), ... (495, 500).
Difference between every pair (Even - Odd) = 5.
Therefore, Average of Even (Q) - Average of Odd (P) = Constant difference = 5.
∴ The correct answer is 5.

Alternate Method
Given: First 100 multiples of 5: {5, 10, 15, 20, ..., 500}
Formula Used: Average of an Arithmetic Progression (AP) = (First term + Last term) ÷ 2
⇒ Set P (Odd places): 1st, 3rd, ..., 99th multiples
⇒ P = {5, 15, 25, ..., 495}
⇒ Average P = (5 + 495) ÷ 2 = 500 ÷ 2 = 250
⇒ Set Q (Even places): 2nd, 4th, ..., 100th multiples
⇒ Q = {10, 20, 30, ..., 500}
⇒ Average Q = (10 + 500) ÷ 2 = 510 ÷ 2 = 255
⇒ Difference = Q - P = 255 - 250 = 5
∴ The correct answer is 5.

Additional Information
Average of Arithmetic Progression

For any sequence in AP, the average is always the middle term or the mean of the first and last terms: (a + l) ÷ 2.

Consecutive Terms Difference

If every term of set B is 'k' more than the corresponding term of set A, then Average(B) - Average(A) = k.

Sum of First n Multiples

Sum of first n multiples of 'x' = x × [n(n+1) ÷ 2]. The average is x × (n+1) ÷ 2.

questions.question: If the radius of a right circular cone is 33.33% of the height then what could be the value for radius and height (in cm) respectively if the volume of the Cone is 27\pi?
questions.solution:
Solution
Shortcut Trick
Ratio of Radius (r) to Height (h) = 33.33% = 1 : 3.
Let r = x and h = 3x.
Volume of Cone = (1/3) × π × x2 × 3x = πx3.
Given: πx3 = 27π ⇒ x3 = 27 ⇒ x = 3.
Radius = 3 cm, Height = 3 × 3 = 9 cm.
∴ The correct answer is 3 cm and 9 cm.

Alternate Method
Given:
Volume (V) = 27π cm3
Radius (r) = 33.33% of Height (h)

Formula Used:
Volume of a Right Circular Cone = (1/3) × π × r2 × h

Calculations:
⇒ r = 33.33/100 × h ⇒ r = (1/3)h
⇒ h = 3r
⇒ Volume = (1/3) × π × r2 × (3r)
⇒ 27π = (1/3) × π × r2 × 3r
⇒ 27π = πr3
⇒ r3 = 27
⇒ r = √327 = 3 cm
⇒ h = 3 × 3 = 9 cm
∴ The correct answer is 3 cm and 9 cm.

Additional Information
Curved Surface Area (CSA) of Cone

The formula for CSA of a cone is πrl, where l is the slant height.

Slant Height Formula

The slant height (l) of a cone is given by l = √(r2 + h2).
Total Surface Area (TSA) of Cone
The TSA of a cone is given by the sum of CSA and base area: TSA = πrl + πr2 = πr(l + r).

Volume Relation

The volume of a cone is exactly 1/3rd of the volume of a cylinder with the same radius and height (πr2h).

questions.question: Aman started a business investing 70000 rs. Rakhi joined him after six months with an amount of 105000 rs. and Sagar joined them with 1.4 lakhs rs. after another six months. The amount of profit earned should be distributed in what ratio among Aman, Rakhi and Sagar respectively, 3 years after Aman started the business?
questions.solution:
Solution
Shortcut Trick
Ratio of Capitals: 70,000 : 1,05,000 : 1,40,000 = 2 : 3 : 4
Ratio of Time: 36 months : 30 months : 24 months = 6 : 5 : 4
Profit Ratio = (Capital × Time) Ratio
Profit Ratio = (2 × 6) : (3 × 5) : (4 × 4) = 12 : 15 : 16
∴ The correct answer is 12 : 15 : 16.

Alternate Method
Given:
Aman investment = ₹70,000 | Rakhi investment = ₹1,05,000 | Sagar investment = ₹1,40,000
Aman time = 3 years = 36 months
Rakhi time = 36 - 6 = 30 months
Sagar time = 30 - 6 = 24 months
Formula: Profit Ratio = (Investment1 × Time1) : (Investment2 × Time2) : (Investment3 × Time3)
⇒ Profit Ratio = (70000 × 36) : (105000 × 30) : (140000 × 24)
⇒ Simplifying by 1000: (70 × 36) : (105 × 30) : (140 × 24)
⇒ Dividing by 35: (2 × 36) : (3 × 30) : (4 × 24)
⇒ Dividing by 6: (2 × 6) : (3 × 5) : (4 × 4)
⇒ Profit Ratio = 12 : 15 : 16
∴ The correct answer is 12 : 15 : 16.

Additional Information
Basic Partnership Rule

Profit is always distributed in the ratio of the product of Capital and Time Period (P = C × T).

Working vs. Sleeping Partner

A working partner manages the business and may receive a salary or commission before the remaining profit is shared among all partners.

Variable Investment

If a partner changes their investment amount during the year, total profit share is calculated as Σ(Capitaln × Timen).

questions.question: In 100m race, A runs at 6 kmph. If A gives B a start of 4m and still beats him by 12 seconds, what is the speed of B?
questions.solution:
Solution
Shortcut Trick
Time taken by A = (Distance ÷ Speed) = 100 ÷ (6 × 5/18) = 60 seconds.

B takes 12 seconds more to cover 4m less distance.

Time taken by B = 60 + 12 = 72 seconds.
Distance covered by B = 100 - 4 = 96 m.
Speed of B = (96 ÷ 72) × (18/5) = 4.8 km/hr.
∴ The correct answer is 4.8 km/hr.

Alternate Method
Given:
Total Race Distance = 100 m
Speed of A = 6 km/hRs. tart given to B = 4 m
Time lag (A beats B) = 12 seconds

Calculations:
⇒ Speed of A in m/s = 6 × (5/18) = 5/3 m/s
⇒ Time taken by A to finish 100m = 100 ÷ (5/3) = 60 seconds
⇒ Since A beats B by 12 seconds, B takes (60 + 12) = 72 seconds
⇒ Distance covered by B = Total Distance - Start = 100 - 4 = 96 m
⇒ Speed of B = Distance ÷ Time = 96 ÷ 72 = 4/3 m/s
⇒ Speed of B in km/hr = (4/3) × (18/5)
⇒ Speed of B = 24/5 = 4.8 km/hr
∴ The correct answer is 4.8 km/hr.

Additional Information
Race Terminology

'A gives B a start of x meters' means B starts x meters ahead of A. 'A beats B by t seconds' means A finishes the race t seconds before B.

Unit Conversion

To convert km/hr to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/hr, multiply by 18/5.

Dead Heat

A dead heat occurs when all participants finish the race at the exact same time, meaning the time taken by each is equal.

questions.question: During a storm, a tree broke at a point 5 m above the ground in such a way that the top of the tree touched the ground 12 m away from where it originally stood. What was the height of the tree before it broke?
questions.solution:
Solution
Shortcut Trick
Recognize the Pythagorean triplet: (5, 12, 13).
Stump height (Perpendicular) = 5 m, Distance (Base) = 12 m.
Broken part (Hypotenuse) = 13 m.
Total tree height = Stump height + Broken part = 5 + 13 = 18 m.
∴ The correct answer is 18 m.

Alternate Method
Given: Height of the stump (p) = 5 m
Distance from base to the top on ground (b) = 12 m
Formula: h2 = p2 + b2
⇒ Let the length of the broken part be AC.
⇒ AC2 = (5)² + (12)²
⇒ AC2 = 25 + 144 = 169
⇒ AC = √169 = 13 m
⇒ Total height of the tree = Height of the stump + Length of the broken part
⇒ Total height = 5 m + 13 m = 18 m
∴ The correct answer is 18 m.

Additional Information
Pythagoras Theorem

In any right-angled triangle, the square of the hypotenuse is equal to the sum of the squares of the other two sides: a2 + b2 = c2.

Common Pythagorean Triples

Standard integer sets that satisfy the theorem include (3, 4, 5), (5, 12, 13), (8, 15, 17), and (7, 24, 25). Multiples of these also form triples.

Right-Angled Triangle Properties

The hypotenuse is always the longest side, and it is the side opposite to the 90° angle.

questions.question: If the radii of two circular ends of a bucket are 15 cm and 7 cm and the curved surface area of the bucket is 374π cm^2, find the volume of the bucket.
questions.solution:
Solution
Shortcut Trick
Slant height l = CSA ÷ [π × (R + r)] = 374π ÷ (22π) = 17 cm.
Height h = √(l2 - (R - r)²) = √(172 - 82) = √(289 - 64) = 15 cm.
Volume = (π × h ÷ 3) × (R2 + r2 + R × r) = 5π × (225 + 49 + 105).
Volume = 5π × 379 = 1895π cm3.
∴ The correct answer is 1895π cm3.

Alternate Method
Given:
Radius of larger end (R) = 15 cm
Radius of smaller end (r) = 7 cm
Curved Surface Area (CSA) = 374π cm2

Formula Used:
CSA of frustum = π(R + r)l

Calculations:
⇒ CSA = π(R + r)l
⇒ 374π = π(15 + 7) × l
⇒ 374 = 22 × l
⇒ l = 374 ÷ 22 = 17 cm
⇒ l2 = h2 + (R - r)²
⇒ 172 = h2 + (15 - 7)²
⇒ 289 = h2 + 82
⇒ 289 = h2 + 64
⇒ h2 = 225
⇒ h = 15 cm
⇒ Volume = (1 ÷ 3) × π × 15 × (152 + 72 + 15 × 7)
⇒ Volume = 5π × (225 + 49 + 105)
⇒ Volume = 5π × 379
⇒ Volume = 1895π cm3
∴ The correct answer is 1895π cm3.

Additional Information
Total Surface Area of Frustum

The total surface area includes the curved area and the area of both circular bases: TSA = πl(R + r) + πR2 + πr2.

Slant Height Relation

The slant height l of a frustum is the hypotenuse of a right triangle with legs h and (R - r), given by l = √[h2 + (R - r)²].

Volume of a Cone

The volume of a full cone is a special case of a frustum where r = 0, expressed as V = (1/3)πR2h.

questions.question: A sum of Rs. 66,550 is taken on loan. This is to be paid back in two equal instalments. If the rate of interest is 20% compounded annually, find the value of each instalment.
questions.solution:
Solution
Shortcut Trick
Rate = 20% = 1/5 → (Principal : Amount) = 5 : 6
For 2 years, equate instalments: (5 × 6 : 6 × 6) and (52 : 62)
Year 1: 30 : 36 | Year 2: 25 : 36
Total Principal = 30 + 25 = 55 units
55 units = ₹66,550 ⇒ 1 unit = ₹1,210
Each instalment = 36 units = 36 × 1,210 = ₹43,560
∴ The correct answer is ₹43,560.

Alternate Method
Given:
Principal (P) = ₹66,550
Rate of Interest (R) = 20% p.a.
Number of instalments (n) = 2

Formula Used:
P = x / (1 + R/100)1 + x / (1 + R/100)² where x = instalment value.

Calculation:
⇒ 66,550 = x / (1 + 20/100) + x / (1 + 20/100)²
⇒ 66,550 = x / 1.2 + x / 1.44
⇒ 66,550 = (1.2x + x) / 1.44
⇒ 66,550 = 2.2x / 1.44
⇒ x = (66,550 × 1.44) / 2.2
⇒ x = 30,250 × 1.44
⇒ x = 43,560
∴ The correct answer is ₹43,560.

Additional Information
Compound Interest Instalment Formula

For n years, Principal P = x [1/k + 1/k2 + ... + 1/kn], where k = (1 + R/100) and x is the annual instalment.

Simple Interest Instalment

In SI, the instalment x = (100 × A) / [100n + RTn(n-1)/2], where A is the total debt amount to be paid.

Effective Rate of Interest

For CI, the effective rate for 2 years is R + R + (R × R)/100. For 20%, it is 20 + 20 + 4 = 44%.

questions.question: The simple interest on a certain sum of money at the rate of 5% per annum for 9 years is ₹1,260. At what rate of interest can the same amount of interest be received on the same sum after 6 years?
questions.solution:
Solution
Shortcut Trick
Since the Principal (P) and Simple Interest (I) are the same in both cases, the product of Rate (R) and Time (T) must be constant.

⇒ R1 × T1 = R2 × T2
⇒ 5 × 9 = R2 × 6
⇒ 45 = 6 × R2
⇒ R2 = 45 ÷ 6 = 7.5%
∴ The correct answer is 7.5%.

Alternate Method
Given:
Case 1: Interest (I) = ₹1,260, Rate (R1) = 5%, Time (T1) = 9 years
Case 2: Interest (I) = ₹1,260, Time (T2) = 6 years, Principal (P) is same as Case 1.

Formula Used:
Simple Interest (I) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

Calculations:
⇒ 1,260 = (P × 5 × 9) ÷ 100
⇒ 1,260 = (P × 45) ÷ 100
⇒ P = (1,260 × 100) ÷ 45
⇒ P = 28 × 100 = ₹2,800
Now, using this Principal for the second case:
⇒ 1,260 = (2,800 × R2 × 6) ÷ 100
⇒ 1,260 = 28 × R2 × 6
⇒ 1,260 = 168 × R2
⇒ R2 = 1,260 ÷ 168
⇒ R2 = 7.5%
∴ The correct answer is 7.5%.

Additional Information
Simple Interest Property

If the simple interest and principal remain constant, the rate of interest is inversely proportional to the time period (R ∝ 1/T).

Total Amount in SI
The total amount (A) is the sum of Principal and Interest: A = P + (P × R × T)/100 = P(1 + RT/100).

SI vs CI Difference

Simple interest is calculated only on the principal, whereas compound interest is calculated on the principal plus the accumulated interest of previous periods.

questions.question: Johnson borrows ₹30,000 at 5% compound interest per annum. He wants to pay this amount back by the end of 2 years in two equal yearly installments. How much does he have to pay approximately at the end of each year?
questions.solution:
Solution
Shortcut Trick
Rate (R) = 5% = 1/20 → Installment Factor = 21/20.
For 2 installments: Principal (P) = x × [ (20/21) + (20/21)² ]
30,000 = x × [ 20/21 + 400/441 ] = x × [ 820 / 441 ]
x = (30,000 × 441) ÷ 820 ≈ 16,134.14
∴ The correct answer is ₹16,134.

Alternate Method
Given: Principal (P) = ₹30,000 | Rate (R) = 5% | Time (n) = 2 years | Equal Installments = x
Formula: Principal = [ x ÷ (1 + R/100)1 ] + [ x ÷ (1 + R/100)² ]
⇒ 30,000 = x ÷ (1.05) + x ÷ (1.05)²
⇒ 30,000 = x × (1 ÷ 1.05 + 1 ÷ 1.1025)
⇒ 30,000 = x × (0.95238 + 0.90703)
⇒ 30,000 = x × 1.85941
⇒ x = 30,000 ÷ 1.85941
⇒ x ≈ 16134.14
∴ The correct answer is ₹16,134.

Additional Information
CI Installment General Formula

For n installments, Principal P = x ÷ k1 + x ÷ k2 + ... + x ÷ kn, where k = (1 + r/100).

Effective Interest Rate

The effective compound rate for 2 years is Reff = 2R + R2/100. For 5%, Reff = 10.25%.

Present Value Concept

Each installment paid in the future is discounted back to the present day using the compound interest rate to equate it with the initial borrowed principal.

questions.question: If $x - y = 4$ and $x^3 - y^3 = 316$, where $y > 0$, then find the value of $x^2 - y^2$:
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Formula: $x^3 - y^3 = (x - y)[(x - y)^2 + 3xy]$
$\Rightarrow 316 = 4[4^2 + 3xy]$
$\Rightarrow 79 = 16 + 3xy$
$\Rightarrow 3xy = 63 \Rightarrow xy = 21$

Find two factors of 21 whose difference is 4:
$7 \times 3 = 21$ and $7 - 3 = 4$.
Thus, $x = 7$ and $y = 3$.

Now calculate $x^2 - y^2$:
$\Rightarrow x^2 - y^2 = 7^2 - 3^2 = 49 - 9 = 40$

∴ The correct answer is 40.

questions.question: In an examination 35% candidates failed in one subject and 42% failed in another subject while 15% failed in both subjects. If 2500 candidates had appeared in that exam how many passed in either subject but not in both?
questions.solution:
Solution
Shortcut Trick
Only Failed in Subject 1 = 35% - 15% = 20%
Only Failed in Subject 2 = 42% - 15% = 27%
Passed in either but not both = (Failed only in Subject 1) + (Failed only in Subject 2)
Total Required Percentage = 20% + 27% = 47%
Required Candidates = 47% of 2500 = 1175
∴ The correct answer is 1175.

Alternate Method
Given:
Total Candidates = 2500
Failed in Subject A, n(A) = 35%
Failed in Subject B, n(B) = 42%
Failed in both subjects, n(A ∩ B) = 15%

Concept:

"Passed in either subject but not both" is equivalent to "Failed in exactly one subject". In Venn diagram terms, this is the sum of (A - B) and (B - A).

Calculations:
⇒ Candidates who failed ONLY in Subject A = n(A) - n(A ∩ B) = 35% - 15% = 20%
⇒ Candidates who failed ONLY in Subject B = n(B) - n(A ∩ B) = 42% - 15% = 27%
⇒ Note: Passed in Sub A but failed Sub B = Failed only in Sub B = 27%
⇒ Note: Passed in Sub B but failed Sub A = Failed only in Sub A = 20%
⇒ Percentage of candidates passed in either but not both = 20% + 27% = 47%
⇒ Number of candidates = (47 ÷ 100) × 2500
⇒ Number of candidates = 47 × 25
⇒ Number of candidates = 1175
∴ The correct answer is 1175.

Additional Information
Venn Diagram Formula

For two sets A and B, n(A ∪ B) = n(A) + n(B) - n(A ∩ B). This formula calculates the total elements in at least one set.

Symmetric Difference

The expression "either but not both" refers to (A - B) ∪ (B - A), which is also written as (A ∪ B) - (A ∩ B).

Complementary Sets

If set A represents failures, then the complement A' represents passers. Passing both subjects is represented by (A ∪ B)', which equals 100% - n(A ∪ B).

questions.question: The expression (tan θ + cot θ) (sec θ + tan θ) (1 - sin θ), 0° < θ < 90°, is equal to:
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Use the value substitution method by picking a specific angle, let θ = 30°.

Substitute values: tan 30° = 1/√3, cot 30° = √3, sec 30° = 2/√3, sin 30° = 1/2.
Expression = (1/√3 + √3) × (2/√3 + 1/√3) × (1 - 1/2) = (4/√3) × (3/√3) × (1/2).
Expression = (4/√3) × √3 × 1/2 = 2.
Check options for θ = 30°: cosec 30° = 1/sin 30° = 1/(1/2) = 2.
∴ The correct answer is cosec θ.

Alternate Method
Given: The expression (tan θ + cot θ) (sec θ + tan θ) (1 - sin θ) for 0° < θ < 90°.
Formula Used: tan θ = sin θ/cos θ; cot θ = cos θ/sin θ; sec θ = 1/cos θ; sin²θ + cos²θ = 1.
⇒ Simplifying (tan θ + cot θ) = (sin θ / cos θ + cos θ / sin θ) = (sin²θ + cos²θ) / (sin θ cos θ)
⇒ (tan θ + cot θ) = 1 / (sin θ cos θ)
⇒ Simplifying (sec θ + tan θ)(1 - sin θ) = (1/cos θ + sin θ/cos θ)(1 - sin θ)
⇒ ((1 + sin θ) / cos θ) × (1 - sin θ) = (1 - sin²θ) / cos θ
⇒ cos²θ / cos θ = cos θ
⇒ Multiplying both parts: [1 / (sin θ cos θ)] × cos θ = 1 / sin θ
⇒ 1 / sin θ = cosec θ
∴ The correct answer is cosec θ.

Additional Information
Reciprocal Identities

Trigonometric ratios are related by reciprocals: cosec θ = 1/sin θ, sec θ = 1/cos θ, and cot θ = 1/tan θ.

Pythagorean Identities

Fundamental identities include sin²θ + cos²θ = 1, 1 + tan²θ = sec²θ, and 1 + cot²θ = cosec²θ.

Quotient Identities

The tangent and cotangent functions can be expressed as ratios: tan θ = sin θ/cos θ and cot θ = cos θ/sin θ.

questions.question: A swimming pool is constructed in the shape of a right-angled triangle. One side is five-third of the length of the second side (leaving the longest side). If the management decides to increase the length of one side by 4 m and decrease the second side by 2 m such that the area of the swimming pool remains the same, then what was the length of one side before the alteration happened?
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Ratio of sides (excluding hypotenuse) = 5 : 3.
Let the sides be 5x and 3x. Area = (1/2) × 5x × 3x = 7.5x2.
According to the condition: (5x + 4)(3x - 2) = 15x2 (since area is halved by 2).
⇒ 15x2 - 10x + 12x - 8 = 15x2.
⇒ 2x = 8 ⇒ x = 4.
Sides are: 5 × 4 = 20 m and 3 × 4 = 12 m.
∴ The correct answer is 20 m.

Alternate Method
Given: Side1 = (5/3) × Side2.
Formula: Area of right - angled triangle = (1/2) × Base × Height.
Let the second side be 3x and the first side be 5x.
⇒ Initial Area = (1/2) × 5x × 3x = 7.5x2 m2.
⇒ New sides after alteration = (5x + 4) and (3x - 2).
⇒ New Area = (1/2) × (5x + 4) × (3x - 2).
⇒ Since Area remains same: (1/2) × 5x × 3x = (1/2) × (5x + 4) × (3x - 2).
⇒ 15x2 = 15x2 - 10x + 12x - 8.
⇒ 2x = 8.
⇒ x = 4.
⇒ Length of Side 1 = 5 × 4 = 20 m.
⇒ Length of Side 2 = 3 × 4 = 12 m.
∴ The correct answer is 20 m.

Additional Information
Pythagoras Theorem

In a right - angled triangle, the square of the hypotenuse is equal to the sum of the squares of the other two sides: a2 + b2 = c2.

Heron’s Formula

For any triangle with sides a, b, and c, Area = √[s(s - a)(s - b)(s - c)], where s = (a + b + c)/2.

Triangle Area Property

If the product of the base and height remains constant, the area of the triangle remains unchanged.

questions.question: What is the simplified form of the following expression? \((x - \frac{1}{y})^3 + (x + \frac{1}{y})^3\)
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Use Algebraic Identity: (a - b)³ + (a + b)³ = 2a(a2 + 3b2).
Here, a = x and b = 1/y.
Substitute: 2(x)[(x)² + 3(1/y)²].
Simplified result: 2x(x2 + 3/y2).
∴ The correct answer is 2x(x2 + 3/y2).

Alternate Method
Given: (x - 1/y)³ + (x + 1/y)³
Formula used: (a - b)³ = a3 - 3a2b + 3ab2 - b3 and (a + b)³ = a3 + 3a2b + 3ab2 + b3
⇒ Expansion of (x - 1/y)³ = x3 - 3x2/y + 3x/y2 - 1/y3
⇒ Expansion of (x + 1/y)³ = x3 + 3x2/y + 3x/y2 + 1/y3
⇒ Summing both expressions: (x3 - 3x2/y + 3x/y2 - 1/y3) + (x3 + 3x2/y + 3x/y2 + 1/y3)
⇒ Combining like terms: (x3 + x3) + (-3x2/y + 3x2/y) + (3x/y2 + 3x/y2) + (-1/y3 + 1/y3)
⇒ Result = 2x3 + 6x/y2
⇒ Taking 2x common: 2x(x2 + 3/y2)
∴ The correct answer is 2x(x2 + 3/y2).

Additional Information
Cubic Identity (Difference)

(a + b)³ - (a - b)³ = 2b(3a2 + b2) = 6a2b + 2b3

Algebraic Square Identities

(a + b)² + (a - b)² = 2(a2 + b2) and (a + b)² - (a - b)² = 4ab

Sum and Difference of Cubes

a3 + b3 = (a + b)(a2 - ab + b2) and a3 - b3 = (a - b)(a2 + ab + b2)

questions.question: The average output of n machines is k units per day. If one of the machines is excluded, whose output is 780 units per day, the average output will decrease by 30 units. Instead, if one dead machine is included, the average output will decrease by 90 units. What is the total output of n machines?
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Case 1: Removal of 780 units machine reduces average by 30 ⇒ 780 - k = 30(n - 1)
Case 2: Addition of 0 units machine reduces average by 90 ⇒ k - 0 = 90(n + 1)
Substitute k = 90n + 90 in first equation: 780 - (90n + 90) = 30n - 30
690 - 90n = 30n - 30 ⇒ 120n = 720 ⇒ n = 6
Average k = 90(6 + 1) = 630 units. Total output = 6 × 630 = 3780 units.
∴ The correct answer is 3780 units.

Alternate Method
Given:
Number of machines = n | Average output = k units/day
Value of machine excluded = 780 units | Value of machine included = 0 units

Formula Used:
Total Output = Number of Machines × Average Output

Calculations:
⇒ Total initial output = n × k
⇒ When 780 is excluded: (nk - 780) ÷ (n - 1) = k - 30
⇒ nk - 780 = (n - 1)(k - 30) = nk - 30n - k + 30
⇒ 30n + k = 810 ... (Eq. 1)
⇒ When a dead machine (0 units) is included: (nk + 0) ÷ (n + 1) = k - 90
⇒ nk = (n + 1)(k - 90) = nk - 90n + k - 90
⇒ k - 90n = 90 ⇒ k = 90n + 90 ... (Eq. 2)
⇒ Substituting (Eq. 2) in (Eq. 1): 30n + (90n + 90) = 810
⇒ 120n = 720 ⇒ n = 6
⇒ k = 90(6) + 90 = 630
⇒ Total Output = nk = 6 × 630 = 3780 units
∴ The correct answer is 3780 units.

Additional Information
Net Deviation Principle

In any average problem, the sum of deviations from the average is always zero. If an item is added or removed, the total change in the sum equals the deviation of that item from the original average.

Impact of Adding Zero

When a zero - value item is added to a set, the total sum remains constant, but the average decreases because the denominator (count) increases: New Avg = Old Sum ÷ (n + 1).

Average Property

If every element in a set is increased or decreased by a constant value 'x', the average also increases or decreases by 'x' respectively.

questions.question: Shyam is travelling on his cycle and has calculated to reach point 'A' at 2 PM If he travels at 10 kmph. he will reach there at 12 noon if he travels at 15 kmph. At what speed must he travel to reach 'A' at 1 PM:
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
The target time (1 PM) is the exact midpoint between 12 noon and 2 PM.

When the distance is constant and the required time is the arithmetic mean of two given times, the required speed is the Harmonic Mean of the two speeds.

Required Speed = (2 × S1 × S2) ÷ (S1 + S2)
Required Speed = (2 × 10 × 15) ÷ (10 + 15) = 300 ÷ 25 = 12 kmph.
∴ The correct answer is 12 kmph.

Alternate Method
Given:
Speed 1 (S1) = 10 kmph (Reaches at 2 PM)
Speed 2 (S2) = 15 kmph (Reaches at 12 noon)
Time difference (ΔT) = 2 PM - 12 noon = 2 hours.

Formula Used:
Distance (D) = (S1 × S2 × ΔT) ÷ (S2 - S1)
Speed = Distance ÷ Time

Calculations:
⇒ D = (10 × 15 × 2) ÷ (15 - 10)
⇒ D = 300 ÷ 5 = 60 km.
⇒ Time taken at 10 kmph = 60 ÷ 10 = 6 hours.
⇒ If he reaches at 2 PM after 6 hours, he started at = 2 PM - 6 hours = 8 AM.
⇒ To reach at 1 PM, target duration = 1 PM - 8 AM = 5 hours.
⇒ Required Speed = Total Distance ÷ Target Duration
⇒ Required Speed = 60 ÷ 5 = 12 kmph.
∴ The correct answer is 12 kmph.

Additional Information
Distance - Speed Inverse Relation

When distance is constant, speed is inversely proportional to time (S1/S2 = T2/T1).

Average Speed (Equal Distances)

If a person covers equal distances at speeds x and y, the average speed is 2xy ÷ (x + y).

Speed Units Conversion

To convert kmph to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert m/s to kmph, multiply by 18/5.

questions.question: A vertical cross-section along the middle of a cylinder with a height of 15 cm and a base radius of 7 cm is cut out. Find the area of the cross-section portion in cm^2.
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Vertical cross - section of a cylinder along the middle is a rectangle.

Dimensions of this rectangle: Width = Diameter (2r) and Length = Height (h).
Width = 2 × 7 = 14 cm
Area = Width × Height = 14 × 15
Area = 210 cm2
∴ The correct answer is 210 cm2.

Alternate Method
Given:
Radius of cylinder (r) = 7 cm
Height of cylinder (h) = 15 cm
Formula: Area of vertical cross - section = 2 × r × h
⇒ Diameter of the base (d) = 2 × Radius
⇒ d = 2 × 7 = 14 cm
⇒ The vertical cross - section is a rectangle with length 15 cm and breadth 14 cm.
⇒ Area of the rectangle = Length × Breadth
⇒ Area = 15 × 14
⇒ Area = 210 cm2
∴ The correct answer is 210 cm2.

Additional Information
Horizontal Cross - section

A horizontal cross - section (parallel to the base) of a cylinder is always a circle with area πr2.

Volume of Cylinder

The volume of a cylinder is calculated as V = πr2h, representing the total capacity.
Total Surface Area (TSA)

The TSA of a cylinder includes the curved surface and two circular bases: TSA = 2πrh + 2πr2 = 2πr(h + r).

Diagonal of Vertical Cross - section

The diagonal of the rectangular cross - section can be found using √((2r)² + h2).

questions.question: When asked to divide a number by 6, Rani has divided it by 9 and she got the quotient as 21 and remainder as 3. Realising her mistake, later she divided it by 6. What will be the quotient and remainder?
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Original Number = (Incorrect Divisor × Quotient) + Remainder
Number = (9 × 21) + 3 = 189 + 3 = 192
New Calculation: 192 ÷ 6 = 32
Remainder = 192 - (6 × 32) = 0
∴ The correct answer is Quotient - 32, Remainder - 0.

Alternate Method
Given: Divisor1 = 9, Quotient1 = 21, Remainder1 = 3, Divisor2 = 6
Formula: Dividend = (Divisor × Quotient) + Remainder
⇒ Original Number = (Divisor × Quotient) + Remainder
⇒ Number = (9 × 21) + 3
⇒ Number = 189 + 3 = 192
⇒ New Quotient = 192 ÷ 6 = 32
⇒ New Remainder = 192 - (6 × 32) = 0
∴ The correct answer is Quotient - 32, Remainder - 0.

Additional Information
The Division Algorithm

For any integer (dividend) and a non - zero integer (divisor), the relationship is Dividend = (Divisor × Quotient) + Remainder.

Remainder Condition

The remainder (r) must always satisfy the condition 0 ≤ r < |divisor|. If r = 0, the dividend is exactly divisible by the divisor.

Verification

To verify a division result, multiply the quotient by the divisor and add the remainder; the sum must equal the original dividend.

questions.question: A hollow closed cube of side 10 cm, each weighing 200 gm, is made. This cube is placed in water with a horizontal face. How many cm of its height sinks in water if the density of water is 1 gm per cm3?
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
According to the Law of Flotation, Weight of a floating object = Weight of displaced liquid.

Base Area × Submerged Height × Density of liquid = Weight of object
⇒ (10 × 10) × h × 1 = 200
⇒ 100 × h = 200 ⇒ h = 2 cm
∴ The correct answer is 2 cm.

Alternate Method
Given:
Side of the closed cube (a) = 10 cm
Weight of the cube (W) = 200 gm
Density of water (ρ) = 1 gm/cm³

Formula Used:
Volume of a cuboid = Base Area × Height
Weight = Volume × Density
Law of Flotation: A floating body displaces its own weight of the fluid in which it floats.

Calculations:
⇒ Base area of the cube = Side × Side = 10 × 10 = 100 cm²
⇒ Let the height of the cube that sinks in water be h cm.
⇒ Volume of water displaced = Base area × Submerged height = 100 × h = 100h cm³
⇒ Weight of displaced water = Volume of displaced water × Density of water
⇒ Weight of displaced water = 100h × 1 = 100h gm

According to Archimedes' Principle:

⇒ Weight of the cube = Weight of the displaced water
⇒ 200 = 100h
⇒ h = 200 ÷ 100 = 2 cm
∴ The correct answer is 2 cm.

Additional Information
Archimedes' Principle

Any object wholly or partially immersed in a fluid experiences an upward buoyant force equal to the weight of the fluid displaced by the object.

Law of Flotation

An object will float if its average density is less than the density of the fluid. In equilibrium, the floating object displaces a weight of fluid strictly equal to its own weight.

Density and Volume Relation

Density (ρ) is defined as mass (or weight in a uniform gravitational field) per unit volume. Calculated as Weight = Volume × Density.

questions.question: In a ∆PQR, X, Y, Z are points on sides PQ, QR, PR such that PX ∶ XQ = 1 ∶ 1, PZ ∶ ZR = 1 ∶ 2, QY ∶ YR = 2 ∶ 3. What is the ratio of the area of quadrilateral XYRZ to that of ∆PXZ?
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Let the total area of ΔPQR be 30 units (using the LCM of denominator values 6 and 5).

Area of ΔPXZ = (1/2) × (1/3) × 30 = 5 units.
Area of ΔXQY = (1/2) × (2/5) × 30 = 6 units.
Area of quadrilateral XYRZ = Area of ΔPQR - (Area of ΔPXZ + Area of ΔXQY) = 30 - (5 + 6) = 19 units.
Required Ratio = Area of XYRZ ÷ Area of ΔPXZ = 19 / 5.
∴ The correct answer is 19/5.

Alternate Method
Given:
PX : XQ = 1 : 1 ⇒ PX / PQ = 1 / 2 and XQ / PQ = 1 / 2
PZ : ZR = 1 : 2 ⇒ PZ / PR = 1 / 3
QY : YR = 2 : 3 ⇒ QY / QR = 2 / 5

P / Q

R / X

Y / Z

1 / 1

1 / 2

2 / 3

5 units

6 units

19 units

Formula Used:
The ratio of the area of a smaller triangle sharing a vertex with a larger triangle is strictly equal to the product of the fractional length of the sides forming that included angle.

Calculations:
⇒ Let the total area of ΔPQR be A.
⇒ Area of ΔPXZ = (PX / PQ) × (PZ / PR) × A
⇒ Area of ΔPXZ = (1 / 2) × (1 / 3) × A = A / 6
⇒ Area of ΔXQY = (XQ / PQ) × (QY / QR) × A
⇒ Area of ΔXQY = (1 / 2) × (2 / 5) × A = A / 5
⇒ The quadrilateral XYRZ occupies the remaining area of ΔPQR.
⇒ Area of XYRZ = Area(ΔPQR) - [Area(ΔPXZ) + Area(ΔXQY)]
⇒ Area of XYRZ = A - (A / 6 + A / 5)
⇒ Area of XYRZ = A - (11A / 30) = 19A / 30
⇒ Required Ratio = Area(XYRZ) ÷ Area(ΔPXZ)
⇒ Ratio = (19A / 30) ÷ (A / 6)
⇒ Ratio = (19 / 30) × 6 = 19 / 5
∴ The correct answer is 19/5.

Additional Information
Area Proportion by Vertex

When two adjacent triangles share the same vertex and base line, their areas are directly proportional to the lengths of their respective bases since their vertical heights remain identically parallel.

Area Splitting Rule

Any segment intersecting two sides of a given triangle creates a smaller triangular region. Its relative area to the entire triangle is directly derived using: Area(ΔSmall) / Area(ΔLarge) = (Side1 Ratio) × (Side² Ratio).

Sine Function for Triangles

Area calculation involving side proportionality stems fundamentally from the theorem: Area = (1/2) × a × b × sin(θ). Thus, comparing the respective fractional sides perfectly substitutes finding angular heights.

questions.question: Suhas mistakenly took as dividend a number which was 10% less than the original dividend. He also mistakenly took as divisor a number which was 20% less than the original divisor. If the correct quotient of the original question of division was 24 and the remainder was 0, then what quotient did Suhas obtain, assuming there was no error in his calculations?
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
New Quotient = (New Dividend % ÷ New Divisor %) × Original Quotient
New Quotient = [(100% - 10%) ÷ (100% - 20%)] × 24
New Quotient = (90% ÷ 80%) × 24
New Quotient = (9 ÷ 8) × 24 = 27
∴ The correct answer is 27.

Alternate Method
Given:
Original Quotient = 24
Original Remainder = 0
New Dividend is 10% less than the Original Dividend.
New Divisor is 20% less than the Original Divisor.

Formula Used:
Dividend = (Divisor × Quotient) + Remainder

Calculations:
⇒ Let the Original Dividend be D and the Original Divisor be d.
⇒ D = (d × 24) + 0
⇒ D ÷ d = 24
⇒ New Dividend = D - (10% of D) = 0.9D
⇒ New Divisor = d - (20% of d) = 0.8d
⇒ New Quotient = New Dividend ÷ New Divisor
⇒ New Quotient = 0.9D ÷ 0.8d
⇒ New Quotient = (0.9 ÷ 0.8) × (D ÷ d)
⇒ Substitute D ÷ d = 24:
⇒ New Quotient = (9 ÷ 8) × 24
⇒ New Quotient = 9 × 3 = 27
∴ The correct answer is 27.

Additional Information
Division Algorithm

The foundational rule of division states that Dividend = (Divisor × Quotient) + Remainder. When the remainder is exactly zero, the dividend is a perfect multiple of the divisor.

Percentage Change in Fractions

If the numerator of a fraction changes by x% and the denominator changes by y%, the resulting fraction becomes [(100 ± x) ÷ (100 ± y)] × Original Fraction.

Base Change

When any given quantity is decreased by R%, the remaining quantity is computed directly as (100 - R)% of its original value. For example, a 10% decrease perfectly leaves 90% of the original value.

questions.question: A certain sum amounts to Rs. 4,900 in 3 years 4 months at the rate of 7.5% p.a. at simple interest. What will be the amount (in Rs.) of the same sum in 3 3/4 years at the rate of 8% p.a. simple interest?
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Effective interest in 1st case = 7.5% × (10/3) = 25% → Amount = 125% of Principal.
Effective interest in 2nd case = 8% × (15/4) = 30% → Amount = 130% of Principal.
Since 125% of Principal = ₹4900
130% of Principal = (4900 ÷ 125) × 130 = 39.2 × 130 = ₹5096.
∴ The correct answer is ₹5096.

Alternate Method
Given:
Amount in 1st case (A1) = ₹4900
Rate (R1) = 7.5% p.a., Time (T1) = 3 years 4 months = 3 + 1/3 = 10/3 years
Rate (R²) = 8% p.a., Time (T²) = 3 + 3/4 = 15/4 years

Formula Used:
Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

Calculations:
⇒ In the 1st case, SI1% = 7.5 × (10/3) = 25%
⇒ Amount (A1) = 100% + 25% = 125% of P
⇒ 125% of P = ₹4900
⇒ P = (4900 × 100) ÷ 125 = ₹3920
⇒ In the 2nd case, SI2% = 8 × (15/4) = 30%
⇒ Amount (A²) = 100% + 30% = 130% of P
⇒ A² = 130% of 3920 = (130 ÷ 100) × 3920
⇒ A² = 1.3 × 3920 = ₹5096
∴ The correct answer is ₹5096.

Additional Information
Effective Interest Rate in SI

In Simple Interest, the effective interest percentage for a given period is simply the product of the rate and time (R × T)%. This allows for direct calculation without finding the principal every time.

Amount Formula for Simple Interest

Amount (A) = P + SI = P(1 + RT/100). The principal remains constant throughout the entire period, unlike compound interest where interest is added to the principal.

Simple vs Compound Interest

For the first year, both simple and compound interests are identical (if compounded annually). From the second year onwards, CI will be greater than SI because interest is earned on accumulated interest.

Solution

Shortcut Trick
Triangles sharing the same vertex and having their bases on the same straight line have areas proportional to their base lengths.

Area of Δ SQR = (SR ÷ PR) × Area of Δ PQR

Concept Used: When two triangles share the same perpendicular height, the ratio of their areas is equal to the ratio of their respective bases.

Calculations:

Additional Information
Area of Triangles with Same Vertex

When two or more triangles share a common vertex and their bases lie on the same straight line, the ratio of their areas is exactly proportional to the ratio of their base lengths because their perpendicular height remains identical.

Similar Triangles Property

If two triangles are entirely similar, the ratio of their enclosed areas is equal to the square of the ratio of their corresponding sides: Area1 ÷ Area² = (Side1 ÷ Side²)2.

Median of a Triangle

A median divides a triangle into two smaller inner triangles of perfectly equal area because it naturally bisects the main base into a 1:1 ratio while sharing the exact same vertex height.

questions.question: A field roller, in the shape of a cylinder, has a diameter of 1 m and length of 11⁄4 m. if the speed at which the roller rolls is 14 revolutions per minute, then the maximum area (in m2) that roll in 1 hour
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Area rolled in 1 revolution = Curved Surface Area = πdh
Area per revolution = 22/7 × 1 × 5/4 = 55/14 m²
Total revolutions in 1 hour (60 min) = 14 × 60 = 840
Total area = Total revolutions × Area per revolution
Total area = 840 × (55/14) = 60 × 55 = 3300 m²
∴ The correct answer is 3300 m².

Alternate Method
Given:
Diameter of the roller (d) = 1 m
Length of the roller (h) = 11⁄4 m = 5/4 m
Speed = 14 revolutions per minute
Time = 1 hour = 60 minutes

Formula Used:
Curved Surface Area (CSA) of a cylinder = π × d × h
Total Area Rolled = Total Revolutions × CSA

Calculations:
⇒ Total revolutions in 1 hour = 14 revolutions/minute × 60 minutes = 840 revolutions
⇒ Area covered in 1 revolution (CSA) = (22/7) × 1 × (5/4)
⇒ Area covered in 1 revolution = 110/28 = 55/14 m²
⇒ Total area rolled in 1 hour = 840 × (55/14)
⇒ Total area = (840 ÷ 14) × 55
⇒ Total area = 60 × 55
⇒ Total area = 3300 m²
∴ The correct answer is 3300 m².

Additional Information
Cylinder Properties

Volume = πr2h | Total Surface Area = 2πr(r + h) | Curved Surface Area = 2πrh or πdh

Revolutions and Rolled Area

When a cylindrical roller rolls on the ground, the flat area covered in one full revolution is exactly equal to its Curved Surface Area (CSA).

Revolutions and Linear Distance

If a wheel or roller moves forward, the linear distance covered in one revolution is equal to the circumference of its circular base (2πr or πd).

questions.question: Three friends having a ball each stand at the three corners of a triangle. Each of them throws her ball independently at random to one of the others, once. The probability of no two friends throwing balls at each other is
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Each of the 3 friends has 2 choices of whom to throw the ball to, making the total possible outcomes = 23 = 8.

For no two friends to throw at each other, the throws must form a continuous complete cycle.

There are exactly 2 possible cycles: (A → B, B → C, C → A) and (A → C, C → B, B → A).
Required Probability = Favorable Outcomes ÷ Total Outcomes = 2 ÷ 8 = 1/4.
∴ The correct answer is 1/4.

Alternate Method
Given:
Three friends throw a ball to one of the other two independently.

Condition: No two friends throw balls at each other (no mutual throws).
Concept Used: Probability = (Number of Favorable Outcomes) ÷ (Total Number of Possible Outcomes)

Calculations:
⇒ Let the three friends be A, B, and C.
⇒ Choices for A = 2 (can throw to B or C)
⇒ Choices for B = 2 (can throw to A or C)
⇒ Choices for C = 2 (can throw to A or B)
⇒ Total possible outcomes = 2 × 2 × 2 = 8
⇒ To ensure no two friends throw at each other, there must be NO mutual exchange (like A throws to B and B throws to A).
⇒ Favorable Case 1: A throws to B, B throws to C, and C throws to A.
⇒ Favorable Case 2: A throws to C, C throws to B, and B throws to A.
⇒ These are the only 2 scenarios where no two persons throw at each other.
⇒ Favorable outcomes = 2
⇒ Required Probability = 2 ÷ 8
⇒ Required Probability = 1/4
∴ The correct answer is 1/4.

Additional Information
Derangements

A derangement is a permutation of elements where no element appears in its original position. For 3 elements, there are strictly 2 derangements, directly corresponding to the two valid cyclical throw sequences seen above.

Probability of Independent Events

When events are independent, the total number of combination outcomes is found by multiplying the choices for each separate event. Here, 2 options per person resulted in 2 × 2 × 2 = 8 total variations.

Cyclic Permutations

For n objects arranged sequentially in a circle, the number of distinct directional arrangements is (n - 1)!. For 3 objects, (3 - 1)! = 2! = 2 distinct complete cycles.

questions.question: Number "A" is increased by 20%, then decreased by 30%, and is finally increased by 50%. Now, the number "A" is decreased by 20%, then increased by 50%, and finally increased by 10%. Find the ratio of the second result to the first result for the number A.
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Let the initial number A be 100.
First result = 100 × 1.20 × 0.70 × 1.50 = 126
Second result = 100 × 0.80 × 1.50 × 1.10 = 132
Required ratio = Second result ÷ First result = 132 ÷ 126 = $\frac{22}{21}$
∴ The correct answer is $\frac{22}{21}$.

Alternate Method
Given:
Initial number = A
Process 1: Increased by 20%, decreased by 30%, increased by 50%
Process 2: Decreased by 20%, increased by 50%, increased by 10%

Calculations:
⇒ First Result = A × (1 + 20/100) × (1 - 30/100) × (1 + 50/100)
⇒ First Result = A × 1.20 × 0.70 × 1.50 = 1.26A
⇒ Second Result = A × (1 - 20/100) × (1 + 50/100) × (1 + 10/100)
⇒ Second Result = A × 0.80 × 1.50 × 1.10 = 1.32A
⇒ Required Ratio = Second Result ÷ First Result
⇒ Required Ratio = 1.32A ÷ 1.26A
⇒ Required Ratio = 132 ÷ 126 = $\frac{22}{21}$
∴ The correct answer is $\frac{22}{21}$.

Additional Information
Successive Percentage Change
When a value undergoes two successive percentage changes of x% and y%, the net equivalent percentage change is given by the formula: $(x + y + \frac{xy}{100})\%$.

Multiplying Factor Method
To calculate an increase of x%, multiply the base by $(1 + \frac{x}{100})$. For a decrease of y%, multiply by $(1 - \frac{y}{100})$. Successive changes can be efficiently calculated by continuously multiplying these factors together.

Base Value Update
In successive percentage problems, each percentage change is calculated on the most recently updated base value, not the initial starting value.

questions.question: What annual instalment will discharge a debt of Rs. 8,154 due in 3 years at 13.25% simple interest per annum? [Note: Instalments will be paid at the end of Year 1, Year 2 and Year 3.]
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Let the annual instalment be 100%.

Total amount paid to clear the debt includes the simple interest earned on each instalment up to the end of 3 years.

⇒ Total Debt = 100% + (100% + 13.25%) + (100% + 2 × 13.25%)
⇒ Total Debt = 100% + 113.25% + 126.5% = 339.75%
⇒ 339.75% = Rs. 8154 ⇒ 100% = (8154 ÷ 339.75) × 100 = Rs. 2400
∴ The correct answer is Rs. 2, 400.

Alternate Method
Given:
Debt (A) = Rs. 8, 154
Time (T) = 3 years
Rate (R) = 13.25% p.a.

Formula Used:
Annual Instalment = (100 × A) ÷ [100 × T + (R × T × (T - 1)) ÷ 2]

Calculations:
⇒ Annual Instalment = (100 × 8154) ÷ [100 × 3 + (13.25 × 3 × 2) ÷ 2]
⇒ Annual Instalment = 815400 ÷ [300 + 39.75]
⇒ Annual Instalment = 815400 ÷ 339.75
⇒ Annual Instalment = 2400
∴ The correct answer is Rs. 2, 400.

Additional Information
Simple Interest Instalment

Instalments paid earlier earn interest until the end of the term. For a debt due in n years, the first instalment earns interest for (n - 1) years, while the last instalment earns none.

Compound Interest Instalment

When clearing a loan with compound interest, the present value of all instalments equals the principal borrowed: P = x ÷ (1 + R ÷ 100) + x ÷ (1 + R ÷ 100)2 + ...

Present Worth and True Discount

Present Worth (PW) is the actual borrowed amount. The Debt (A) is the sum of Present Worth and True Discount (TD), where TD = (PW × R × T) ÷ 100.

questions.question: The simple interest on a certain sum for $4 \frac{1}{2}$ years at 10% p.a. is 60% of the compound interest on a sum of Rs. 12,000 for 1 year at 10% p.a, interest compounded half yearly. The sum on which the simple interest is calculated is:
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Effective rate for CI at 10% p.a. compounded half - yearly for 1 year = 5% + 5% + (5 × 5)/100 = 10.25%

Total Compound Interest = 10.25% of 12000 = Rs. 1230
Given Simple Interest = 60% of CI = 0.60 × 1230 = Rs. 738
Using SI = (P × R × T) / 100 ⇒ P × 10 × 4.5 / 100 = 738

P × 0.45 = 738 ⇒ P = 1640

∴ The correct answer is Rs. 1640.

Alternate Method
Given:
CI Principal = Rs. 12000
CI Rate = 10% p.a. (5% per half - year), Time = 1 year (2 half - years)
SI Rate = 10% p.a., Time = 4.5 years (9/2 years)

Compound Interest (Half - Yearly)

P = Rs. 12000 | R = 10% p.a. (5% per half - yr) | T = 1 yr
Effective Rate = 10.25% → CI = Rs. 1230

Simple Interest

P = ? | R = 10% p.a. | T = 4.5 yrs
SI = 60% of CI = Rs. 738

Formula Used:
CI = P × [(1 + R/100)T - 1]
SI = (P × R × T) / 100

Calculations:
⇒ Amount after 1 year (CI) = 12000 × (1 + 5/100)²
⇒ Amount = 12000 × (1.05)²
⇒ Amount = 12000 × 1.1025 = Rs. 13230
⇒ CI = 13230 - 12000 = Rs. 1230
⇒ Given that SI is 60% of CI:
⇒ SI = (60/100) × 1230 = Rs. 738
⇒ Now, substitute SI value in formula:
⇒ 738 = (Principal × 10 × 4.5) / 100
⇒ 738 = Principal × 45 / 100
⇒ 738 = Principal × 0.45
⇒ Principal = 738 / 0.45 = 1640
∴ The correct answer is Rs. 1640.

Additional Information
Half - Yearly Compound Interest

When interest is compounded half - yearly, the rate is halved (R/2) and the time periods are doubled (2T). Amount = P(1 + R/200)²T.

Effective Rate Formula

For two successive periods with the same rate R%, the effective rate can be found directly using: R + R + (R²/100)%.

Simple vs Compound Interest

Simple interest is calculated only on the principal amount uniformly across all years, while compound interest is calculated on both principal and the accumulated interest of previous periods.
