questions.question: If $\tan A + \sin A = p$ and $\tan A - \sin A = q$, then which of the following is true?
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Put A = 45°. Then tan(45°) = 1 and sin(45°) = 1/√2.
p = 1 + 1/√2 and q = 1 - 1/√2
p² - q² = (p + q) × (p - q) = (2) × (2/√2) = 2√2
pq = (1 + 1/√2) × (1 - 1/√2) = 1 - 1/2 = 1 2/4√(pq) = 4 × √(1/2) = 4/√2 = 2√2
∴ The correct answer is p² - q² = 4√(pq).

Alternate Method
Given:
p = tanA + sinA
q = tanA - sinA

Calculations:
⇒ p + q = 2tanA
⇒ p - q = 2sinA
⇒ p² - q² = (p + q) × (p - q) = (2tanA) × (2sinA) = 4tanA × sinA
Now, let us calculate the product pq:
⇒ pq = (tanA + sinA) × (tanA - sinA)
⇒ pq = tan²A - sin²A
⇒ pq = (sin²A ÷ cos²A) - sin²A
⇒ pq = sin²A × (1/cos²A - 1)
⇒ pq = sin²A × (sec²A - 1)
⇒ pq = sin²A × tan²A
⇒ √(pq) = sinA × tanA

Multiplying by 4 on both sides:

⇒ 4√(pq) = 4tanA × sinA

Comparing the values of (p² - q²) and 4√(pq):

⇒ p² - q² = 4√(pq)
∴ The correct answer is p² - q² = 4√(pq).

Additional Information
Trigonometric Identities

The three fundamental identities are: sin²θ + cos²θ = 1, sec²θ - tan²θ = 1, and cosec²θ - cot²θ = 1.
Difference of Squares
The algebraic identity a² - b² = (a - b) × (a + b) helps simplify quadratic differences rapidly.

Tangent Formula

The relationship tanθ = sinθ ÷ cosθ is useful for converting all terms into sine and cosine to simplify complex equations.

questions.question: A path of uniform width of 1m inside the rectangular park of 20m and 15m are made. Find the area of a path.
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Area of a path constructed inside a rectangle is given by: Area = 2w(L + B - 2w)
Where L = 20 m, B = 15 m, w = 1 m
⇒ Area = 2 × 1 × (20 + 15 - 2 × 1)
⇒ Area = 2 × (35 - 2)
⇒ Area = 2 × 33 = 66 m²
∴ The correct answer is 66 m².

Alternate Method
Given:
Length of the outer park (L) = 20 m
Breadth of the outer park (B) = 15 m
Width of the inner path (w) = 1 m

Formula Used:
Area of rectangle = Length × Breadth
Area of inner path = Area of outer rectangle - Area of inner rectangle

Calculations:
⇒ Area of outer rectangular park = 20 × 15 = 300 m²

Since the path of 1 m width is made inside, the dimensions of the inner rectangle will decrease by 2 m (1 m from each side).

⇒ Inner length (l) = 20 - (2 × 1) = 18 m
⇒ Inner breadth (b) = 15 - (2 × 1) = 13 m
⇒ Area of inner rectangle = 18 × 13 = 234 m²
⇒ Area of path = 300 - 234 = 66 m²
∴ The correct answer is 66 m².

Additional Information
Path Inside a Rectangle

When a path of width w is constructed inside a rectangular park of length L and breadth B, Area of path = 2w(L + B - 2w).

Path Outside a Rectangle

When a path of width w is constructed outside a rectangular park of length L and breadth B, Area of path = 2w(L + B + 2w).

Cross Path Inside a Rectangle

When two mutually perpendicular paths of width w cross each other centrally inside a rectangle, Area of path = w(L + B - w).

questions.question: A and B invested their money in a business in the ratio of 9 ∶ 5. If 10% of the total profit goes for charity and A’s share is Rs. 29,840, what is the total profit (in Rs., to the nearest integer)?
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Total distributed profit = Total profit × 90%.
A's share = Total profit × (90 / 100) × [9 / (9 + 5)].
29840 = Total profit × (9 / 10) × (9 / 14).
Total profit = 29840 × (140 / 81) = 4177600 / 81 = 51575.30...
∴ The correct answer is Rs. 51, 575.

Alternate Method
Given:
Investment ratio of A and B = 9 : 5
Percentage of profit going to charity = 10%
A's profit share = Rs. 29, 840

Formula Used:
Profit ratio = Investment ratio (when the time period is identical)

Calculations:
⇒ Let the total profit be P.
⇒ Profit distributed between A and B = P - 10% of P = 90% of P = 0.9P.
⇒ Investment ratio of A and B = 9 : 5
⇒ Total ratio parts = 9 + 5 = 14 parts.
⇒ A's profit share = (9 / 14) of the remaining profit
⇒ 29840 = (9 / 14) × 0.9P
⇒ 29840 = (8.1 / 14) × P
⇒ P = (29840 × 14) / 8.1
⇒ P = 417760 / 8.1 = 4177600 / 81
⇒ P = 51575.308...
⇒ Rounding to the nearest integer, Total Profit ≈ Rs. 51, 575
∴ The correct answer is Rs. 51, 575.

Additional Information
Sleeping Partner

A partner who only invests money but does not take part in the management of the business is known as a sleeping partner. Active partners receive a fixed salary or a certain percentage of the profit for managing the business before the remaining profit is distributed among all partners.

Compound Partnership

When investments are made for different time periods, it is called a compound partnership. The profit share ratio is the product of capital invested and the time period of investment (P1 : P² = C1 × T1 : C² × T²).

Joining Mid - way

If a partner joins x months after the start of a financial year, their investment time period for that year is (12 - x) months, which must be multiplied by their capital to determine their final profit share ratio compared to the primary investors.

questions.question: If $\cot A + \cos A = p$ and $\cot A - \cos A = q$, then which of the following relations is correct?
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Put A = 30°, then cot 30° = √3 and cos 30° = √3/2.
⇒ p = √3 + √3/2 = 3√3/2 and q = √3 - √3/2 = √3/2
⇒ p² - q² = (27/4) - (3/4) = 24/4 = 6
⇒ 16pq = 16 × (3√3/2) × (√3/2) = 16 × 9/4 = 36
⇒ √16pq = √36 = 6
∴ The correct answer is √16pq = p² - q².

Alternate Method
Given:
p = cot A + cos A
q = cot A - cos A

Formula Used:
(a + b)² - (a - b)² = 4ab
cot²A - cos²A = cot²A × cos²A

Calculations:
⇒ p² - q² = (cot A + cos A)² - (cot A - cos A)²
⇒ p² - q² = 4 × cot A × cos A --- (Equation 1)
⇒ pq = (cot A + cos A) × (cot A - cos A)
⇒ pq = cot²A - cos²A
⇒ pq = (cos²A / sin²A) - cos²A
⇒ pq = cos²A × (1 / sin²A - 1)
⇒ pq = cos²A × (cosec²A - 1)
⇒ pq = cos²A × cot²A
⇒ √pq = cos A × cot A

Multiplying by 4 on both sides:

⇒ 4√pq = 4 × cos A × cot A
⇒ √16pq = 4 × cos A × cot A --- (Equation 2)

From Equation 1 and Equation 2:

⇒ p² - q² = √16pq
∴ The correct answer is √16pq = p² - q².

Additional Information
Pythagorean Identities

The fundamental identities are: sin²A + cos²A = 1, sec²A - tan²A = 1, and cosec²A - cot²A = 1.

Algebraic Expansion Formulas

Standard algebraic formulas used in trigonometry: (a + b)² - (a - b)² = 4ab and (a + b)(a - b) = a² - b².

Quotient and Reciprocal Relations

The basic relationships include: tan A = sin A ÷ cos A, cot A = cos A ÷ sin A, and cosec A = 1 ÷ sin A.

questions.question: A TV and an air conditioner were sold for ₹9,600 each. The TV was sold at a loss of 20% and the AC was sold at a profit of 20%. What is the net result?
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
When two items are sold at the same price, one at a profit of x% and the other at a loss of x%, there is always a net loss.

Net Loss % = (x ÷ 10)2 % = (20 ÷ 10)2 = 4%.
Total Selling Price (SP) = ₹9, 600 + ₹9, 600 = ₹19, 200.

Since the loss is 4%, the Total SP is equivalent to 96% of the Total Cost Price (CP).

Loss value = Total SP × [4% ÷ 96%] = 19200 × (1 ÷ 24) = ₹800.
∴ The correct answer is Loss of ₹800.

Alternate Method
Given:
SP of TV = ₹9, 600 (Sold at a 20% loss)
SP of Air Conditioner (AC) = ₹9, 600 (Sold at a 20% profit)

Formula Used:
Cost Price (CP) = (Selling Price × 100) ÷ (100 ± Profit/Loss %)

Calculations:
⇒ Total Selling Price = 9600 + 9600 = ₹19, 200
⇒ Cost Price of TV = (9600 × 100) ÷ (100 - 20)
⇒ Cost Price of TV = 960000 ÷ 80 = ₹12, 000
⇒ Cost Price of AC = (9600 × 100) ÷ (100 + 20)
⇒ Cost Price of AC = 960000 ÷ 120 = ₹8, 000
⇒ Total Cost Price = 12000 + 8000 = ₹20, 000
⇒ Since Total CP > Total SP, there is a net loss.
⇒ Net Loss = Total CP - Total SP
⇒ Net Loss = 20000 - 19200 = ₹800
∴ The correct answer is Loss of ₹800.

Additional Information
Same SP, Same Profit/Loss %

If two distinct items are sold at the same price, where one makes an x% profit and the other suffers an x% loss, the transaction always yields an overall net loss of (x ÷ 10)2 %.

Same CP, Same Profit/Loss %

If a person buys two distinct items at the exact same cost price, and sells one at x% profit and the other at x% loss, the net result is neither profit nor loss (0% net change).

Successive Percentage Rule

Whenever a value is first increased by x% and then decreased by x% (or vice versa), the final value is always less than the initial value, resulting in a net decrement of (x² ÷ 100)%.

questions.question: The marked price of a car is Rs. 1900. Under a scheme successive discounts of 10% and 8% are offered on it. Find the total discount offered while selling the car under the given scheme.
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Equivalent discount % for successive discounts of a% and b% = a + b - (a × b) / 100
Net discount % = 10 + 8 - (10 × 8) / 100 = 18 - 0.8 = 17.2%
Total discount = 17.2% of Rs. 1900
Total discount = (17.2 / 100) × 1900 = 17.2 × 19 = 326.8
∴ The correct answer is Rs. 326.8.

Alternate Method
Given:
Marked Price (MP) = Rs. 1900
Successive discounts = 10% and 8%

Calculations:
⇒ First discount = 10% of Rs. 1900
⇒ First discount = (10 / 100) × 1900 = Rs. 190
⇒ Price after first discount = 1900 - 190 = Rs. 1710
⇒ Second discount = 8% of Rs. 1710
⇒ Second discount = (8 / 100) × 1710 = Rs. 136.8
⇒ Total discount offered = First discount + Second discount
⇒ Total discount = 190 + 136.8 = 326.8
∴ The correct answer is Rs. 326.8.

Additional Information
Marked Price (MP) and Discount

Marked price is the price printed on an article. Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price. Selling Price (SP) = MP - Discount.

Successive Discounts Formula

When two successive discounts of a% and b% are given, the equivalent single discount is [a + b - (a × b) / 100]%.

Selling Price after Successive Discounts
Final Selling Price (SP) = MP × (100 - a) / 100 × (100 - b) / 100.

questions.question: Find the median of the following data. (Rounded off to 2 decimal places.) Class interval 0-5 5-10 10-15 15-20 20-25 25-30 30-35 Frequency 3 5 4 2 7 6 5
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Total frequency N = 32 → N/2 = 16.

Cumulative frequency just > 16 is 21, so median class is 20 - 25.

L = 20, CF = 14, f = 7, h = 5.
Median = 20 + [(16 - 14) ÷ 7] × 5 = 20 + 10/7 ≈ 21.43.
∴ The correct answer is 21.43.

Alternate Method
Given:
Total frequency (N) = 3 + 5 + 4 + 2 + 7 + 6 + 5 = 32
Cumulative frequencies (CF) for classes: 3, 8, 12, 14, 21, 27, 32

Formula Used:
Median = L + [(N/2 - CF) ÷ f] × h

Calculations:
⇒ N/2 = 32 ÷ 2 = 16
⇒ The CF just greater than 16 is 21, which corresponds to the class interval 20 - 25.
⇒ Lower limit of median class (L) = 20
⇒ CF of preceding class (CF) = 14
⇒ Frequency of median class (f) = 7
⇒ Class size (h) = 5
⇒ Median = 20 + [(16 - 14) ÷ 7] × 5
⇒ Median = 20 + (2 ÷ 7) × 5
⇒ Median = 20 + 10 ÷ 7
⇒ Median = 20 + 1.428...
⇒ Median ≈ 21.43
∴ The correct answer is 21.43.

Additional Information
Mode of Grouped Data

Mode = L + [(f1 - f0) ÷ (2f1 - f0 - f²)] × h, where f1 is frequency of modal class, f0 and f² are frequencies of preceding and succeeding classes.

Mean of Grouped Data

Direct method formula: Mean = Σfixi ÷ Σfi, where xi represents the class mark (midpoint) of each class interval.

Empirical Relationship

The empirical relationship between Mean, Median, and Mode is given by: Mode = 3 × Median - 2 × Mean.

questions.question: A 735 m long train passes through a 225 m long tunnel in 48 sec. Find the speed of the train.
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Total Distance = Length of Train + Length of Tunnel = 735 + 225 = 960 m
Speed = Distance ÷ Time = 960 ÷ 48 = 20 m/s
Convert speed from m/s to km/h by multiplying by (18 ÷ 5): Speed = 20 × (18 ÷ 5) = 72 km/h
∴ The correct answer is 72 km/h.

Alternate Method
Given:
Length of the train = 735 m
Length of the tunnel = 225 m
Time taken to pass the tunnel = 48 sec

Formula Used:
Speed = Total Distance ÷ Time
Total Distance = Length of Train + Length of Object Passed
Speed in km/h = Speed in m/s × (18 ÷ 5)

Calculations:
⇒ Total Distance = 735 + 225 = 960 m
⇒ Speed in m/s = 960 ÷ 48 = 20 m/s
⇒ To convert speed from m/s to km/h, multiply by (18 ÷ 5)
⇒ Speed in km/h = 20 × (18 ÷ 5)
⇒ Speed = 4 × 18 = 72 km/h
∴ The correct answer is 72 km/h.

Additional Information
Crossing a Point Object

When a train crosses a stationary point object like a man, a pole, or a tree, the distance covered is equal to the length of the train alone.

Crossing an Extended Object

When a train crosses an extended stationary object like a platform, bridge, or tunnel, the total distance covered is the sum of the train's length and the object's length.

Relative Speed

For two moving bodies, Relative Speed = V1 - V² when traveling in the same direction, and Relative Speed = V1 + V² when traveling in opposite directions.

Unit Conversions

To convert speed from km/h to m/s, multiply the value by (5 ÷ 18). To convert speed from m/s to km/h, multiply the value by (18 ÷ 5).

questions.question: A sells an article to B at 12% profit. B sells it to C at 9% loss. If C pays ₹15,288 for it, then at what price (in ₹) is the article purchased by A?
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Using the successive percentage ratio multiplier method: Final Price = Initial Price × (100 + Profit%) ÷ 100 × (100 - Loss%) ÷ 100
15288 = CP × (112 ÷ 100) × (91 ÷ 100)
CP = 15288 × (100 ÷ 112) × (100 ÷ 91) = 15000
∴ The correct answer is ₹15, 000.

Alternate Method
Given:
⇒ Profit percentage for A = 12%
⇒ Loss percentage for B = 9%
⇒ Final price paid by C = ₹15, 288

Formula Used:
⇒ Final SP = Initial CP × (100 ± Change%) ÷ 100

Calculations:
⇒ Let the initial cost price for A be ₹x.
⇒ Cost price for B = x × (100 + 12) ÷ 100 = 1.12x
⇒ Cost price for C = 1.12x × (100 - 9) ÷ 100
⇒ Cost price for C = 1.12x × 0.91 = 1.0192x
⇒ We know C pays ₹15, 288. Equating the values:
⇒ 1.0192x = 15288
⇒ x = 15288 ÷ 1.0192 = 15000
∴ The correct answer is ₹15, 000.

Additional Information
Successive Percentage Change

When a value goes through sequential percentage changes, the equivalent net change can be found using the formula: a + b + (a × b ÷ 100), taking profit as positive and loss as negative.

Chain System in Transactions

In a sequential chain of sales, the Selling Price (SP) for the seller automatically becomes the Cost Price (CP) for the next buyer. The successive multiplier method is the fastest way to compute final values.

Profit & Loss Basics

Profit and loss are always calculated on the base Cost Price (CP) unless specifically stated otherwise. Formulas: SP = CP × (100 + P%) ÷ 100 and SP = CP × (100 - L%) ÷ 100.

questions.question: If the total surface area of the right circular cylinder is 50% more than the curved surface area of that cylinder and the volume of right circular cylinder is 5488π m^3, then find the curved surface of the right circular cylinder. (in m^2)
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
TSA is 50% more than CSA ⇒ TSA = 1.5 × CSA
⇒ 2πr(r + h) = 1.5 × 2πrh ⇒ r + h = 1.5h ⇒ h = 2r
Volume = πr2h = πr2(2r) = 2πr³
⇒ 2πr³ = 5488π ⇒ r³ = 2744 ⇒ r = 14 m
CSA = 2πrh = 2πr(2r) = 4πr² = 4π(14)² = 784π m²
∴ The correct answer is 784π m².

Alternate Method
Given:
Total Surface Area (TSA) = Curved Surface Area (CSA) + 50% of CSA = 1.5 × CSA
Volume (V) = 5488π m³

Formula Used:
TSA = 2πr(r + h), CSA = 2πrh, Volume = πr2h

Calculations:
⇒ 2πr(r + h) = 1.5 × 2πrh
⇒ r + h = 1.5h
⇒ r = 0.5h ⇒ h = 2Rs. ubstitute h = 2r into the volume formula:
⇒ πr2(2r) = 5488π
⇒ 2πr³ = 5488π
⇒ r³ = 2744
⇒ r = 14 m
Now find height (h) and CSA:
⇒ h = 2 × 14 = 28 m
⇒ CSA = 2πrh = 2 × π × 14 × 28
⇒ CSA = 784π m²
∴ The correct answer is 784π m².

Additional Information
Right Circular Cylinder Geometry

Total Surface Area (TSA) is the sum of the Curved Surface Area (CSA) and the two circular bases: TSA = 2πr² + 2πrh.

Ratio of Areas

The relationship between TSA and CSA directly gives the ratio of radius to height since TSA ÷ CSA = (r + h) ÷ h = 1 + (r ÷ h).

Volume of Cylinder

The volume represents the total 3D space enclosed within the cylinder, given by the product of the base area and the height: V = πr2h.

questions.question: Evaluate: $\frac{\cos 2\theta \cos 3\theta - \cos 2\theta \cos 7\theta + \cos \theta \cos 10\theta}{\sin 4\theta \sin 3\theta - \sin 2\theta \sin 5\theta + \sin 4\theta \sin 7\theta}$
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Multiply the numerator and denominator by 2 to apply transformation formulas.

Num: (cos θ + cos 5θ) - (cos 5θ + cos 9θ) + (cos 9θ + cos 11θ) = cos θ + cos 11θ
Den: (cos θ - cos 7θ) - (cos 3θ - cos 7θ) + (cos 3θ - cos 11θ) = cos θ - cos 11θ
Expression = (cos θ + cos 11θ) ÷ (cos θ - cos 11θ)
Apply sum - to - product rules: (2 × cos 6θ × cos 5θ) ÷ (2 × sin 6θ × sin 5θ) = cot 6θ × cot 5θ
∴ The correct answer is cot 6θ × cot 5θ.

Alternate Method
Given:
Expression = (cos²θ × cos 3θ - cos²θ × cos 7θ + cos θ × cos 10θ) ÷ (sin 4θ × sin 3θ - sin²θ × sin 5θ + sin 4θ × sin 7θ)
Formulas Used: 2 × cos A × cos B = cos(A - B) + cos(A + B)² × sin A × sin B = cos(A - B) - cos(A + B)
cos C + cos D = 2 × cos((C + D) ÷ 2) × cos((C - D) ÷ 2)
cos C - cos D = 2 × sin((C + D) ÷ 2) × sin((D - C) ÷ 2)

Calculations:
⇒ Multiply numerator and denominator by 2.
⇒ Numerator = (2 × cos²θ × cos 3θ) - (2 × cos²θ × cos 7θ) + (2 × cos θ × cos 10θ)
⇒ Numerator = (cos θ + cos 5θ) - (cos 5θ + cos 9θ) + (cos 9θ + cos 11θ)
⇒ Numerator = cos θ + cos 5θ - cos 5θ - cos 9θ + cos 9θ + cos 11θ
⇒ Numerator = cos θ + cos 11θ
⇒ Denominator = (2 × sin 4θ × sin 3θ) - (2 × sin²θ × sin 5θ) + (2 × sin 4θ × sin 7θ)
⇒ Denominator = (cos θ - cos 7θ) - (cos 3θ - cos 7θ) + (cos 3θ - cos 11θ)
⇒ Denominator = cos θ - cos 7θ - cos 3θ + cos 7θ + cos 3θ - cos 11θ
⇒ Denominator = cos θ - cos 11θ
⇒ Expression = (cos θ + cos 11θ) ÷ (cos θ - cos 11θ)
⇒ Applying Sum to Product formulas on the resulting terms:
⇒ cos θ + cos 11θ = 2 × cos 6θ × cos 5θ
⇒ cos θ - cos 11θ = 2 × sin 6θ × sin 5θ
⇒ Ratio = (2 × cos 6θ × cos 5θ) ÷ (2 × sin 6θ × sin 5θ)
⇒ Ratio = cot 6θ × cot 5θ
∴ The correct answer is cot 6θ × cot 5θ.

Additional Information
Product to Sum Formulas

Used to convert trigonometric products into sums or differences: 2 × sin A × sin B = cos(A - B) - cos(A + B), and 2 × cos A × cos B = cos(A - B) + cos(A + B).

Sum to Product Formulas

Used to convert trigonometric sums into products to simplify terms: cos C + cos D = 2 × cos((C + D) ÷ 2) × cos((C - D) ÷ 2) and cos C - cos D = 2 × sin((C + D) ÷ 2) × sin((D - C) ÷ 2).

Quotient Identities

Basic relationships expressing tan and cot in terms of sin and cos: tan θ = sin θ ÷ cos θ and cot θ = cos θ ÷ sin θ.

questions.question: The speed of a train is 3 times that of a car and 1.5 times of a steamer. A person travelled x km by steamer, 3.75x km by train and x/2 km by car. If the speed of the car is 40 km/h and total time taken by him is $4\frac{1}{2}$ hours, then the total distance travelled by him in three modes is:
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Speeds → Car: 40 km/h | Train: 40 × 3 = 120 km/h | Steamer: 120 ÷ 1.5 = 80 km/h
Time = Distance ÷ Speed ⇒ x/80 + 3.75x/120 + 0.5x/40 = 4.5
⇒ x(1/80 + 1/32 + 1/80) = 4.5
⇒ 9x/160 = 4.5 ⇒ x = 80
Total Distance = x + 3.75x + 0.5x = 5.25x = 5.25 × 80 = 420 km.
∴ The correct answer is 420 km.

Alternate Method
Given:
Speed of car = 40 km/h
Total time taken = 4.5 hours

Formula Used:
Time = Distance ÷ Speed

Calculations:
⇒ Speed of train = 3 × 40 = 120 km/h
⇒ Speed of steamer = 120 ÷ 1.5 = 80 km/h
⇒ Time taken by steamer = x ÷ 80 hours
⇒ Time taken by train = 3.75x ÷ 120 = x ÷ 32 hours
⇒ Time taken by car = (x/2) ÷ 40 = x ÷ 80 hours
⇒ Total time = x/80 + x/32 + x/80 = 4.5
⇒ 2x/80 + x/32 = 4.5
⇒ x/40 + x/32 = 4.5
⇒ (4x + 5x) ÷ 160 = 4.5
⇒ 9x ÷ 160 = 4.5
⇒ x = (4.5 × 160) ÷ 9 = 80
⇒ Total Distance = x + 3.75x + 0.5x = 5.25x
⇒ Total Distance = 5.25 × 80 = 420 km
∴ The correct answer is 420 km.

Additional Information
Average Speed

When an object covers multiple distances at different speeds, Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time.

Relative Speed

If two bodies move in the same direction, relative speed is |S1 - S2|. If they move in opposite directions, relative speed is S1 + S².

Unit Conversion

To convert a speed from km/h to m/s, multiply the value by 5/18. To convert m/s back to km/h, multiply the value by 18/5.

questions.question: Let sin A + cos B = 0 and sin B + cos A = 2. What is the value of sin (A + B)?
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Given sin B + cos A = 2. Since the maximum value of both sine and cosine is 1, this equation is only possible if sin B = 1 and cos A = 1.
⇒ B = 90° and A = 0°
Check with the first given equation: sin A + cos B = sin 0° + cos 90° = 0 + 0 = 0 (Condition satisfied)
⇒ sin(A + B) = sin(0° + 90°) = sin 90° = 1
∴ The correct answer is 1.

Alternate Method
Given:
sin A + cos B = 0 . . . (1)
sin B + cos A = 2 . . . (2)

Formula Used:
sin²θ + cos²θ = 1
sin(A + B) = sin A cos B + cos A sin B

Calculations:
Squaring and adding equations (1) and (2):

⇒ (sin A + cos B)² + (sin B + cos A)² = 0² + 2²
⇒ (sin²A + cos²B + 2 sin A cos B) + (sin²B + cos²A + 2 sin B cos A) = 4

Rearranging the terms:

⇒ (sin²A + cos²A) + (sin²B + cos²B) + 2(sin A cos B + cos A sin B) = 4
⇒ 1 + 1 + 2 sin(A + B) = 4
⇒ 2 + 2 sin(A + B) = 4
⇒ 2 sin(A + B) = 2
⇒ sin(A + B) = 1
∴ The correct answer is 1.

Additional Information
Trigonometric Identities

sin²θ + cos²θ = 1 | sec²θ - tan²θ = 1 | cosec²θ - cot²θ = 1

Compound Angle Formulas

sin(A - B) = sin A cos B - cos A sin B
cos(A + B) = cos A cos B - sin A sin B
cos(A - B) = cos A cos B + sin A sin B

questions.question: X and Y can complete a certain work in 18 days and 30 days respectively. Z is 50% more efficient than Y. Z and Y started the work but both had to leave after 4 days. The remaining work was completed by X with the assistance of P in the next 4 days. P alone can complete the original work in
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Total work = LCM(18, 30) = 90 units.
Efficiency of X = 5, Efficiency of Y = 3.
Z is 50% more efficient than Y ⇒ Z's efficiency = 3 + 1.5 = 4.5.
Work by (Y + Z) in 4 days = 4 × (3 + 4.5) = 30 units.
Remaining work (90 - 30 = 60 units) is done by (X + P) in 4 days ⇒ Efficiency of P = (60 ÷ 4) - 5 = 10.
Time taken by P alone = 90 ÷ 10 = 9 days.
∴ The correct answer is 9 days.

Alternate Method
Given:
Time taken by X = 18 days
Time taken by Y = 30 days

Z is 50% more efficient than Y.

Person Days Total Work Efficiency

X 18 90 5

Y 30 3

Calculations:
⇒ Efficiency of Z = Efficiency of Y + (50% of Efficiency of Y)
⇒ Efficiency of Z = 3 + (0.5 × 3) = 4.5 units/day
⇒ Y and Z started the work and left after 4 days.
⇒ Work completed by Y and Z = 4 × (Efficiency of Y + Efficiency of Z)
⇒ Work completed by Y and Z = 4 × (3 + 4.5) = 4 × 7.5 = 30 units
⇒ Remaining work = Total Work - Work completed
⇒ Remaining work = 90 - 30 = 60 units
⇒ This remaining work is completed by X and P in 4 days.
⇒ Combined efficiency of X and P = Remaining work ÷ Time
⇒ Combined efficiency of X and P = 60 ÷ 4 = 15 units/day
⇒ Efficiency of P = Combined efficiency - Efficiency of X
⇒ Efficiency of P = 15 - 5 = 10 units/day
⇒ Time taken by P alone to complete the original work = Total Work ÷ Efficiency of P
⇒ Time taken by P = 90 ÷ 10 = 9 days
∴ The correct answer is 9 days.

Additional Information
Efficiency and Time

The time taken by a person to complete a piece of work is inversely proportional to their efficiency. Higher efficiency results in lesser time taken.

Total Work Concept

Total Work can be assumed as the Least Common Multiple (LCM) of the given individual times to simplify efficiency calculations. Total Work = Efficiency × Time.

Work and Wages

Wages are distributed in direct proportion to the amount of total work completed by each individual, or their efficiency if they work for the same number of days.

Pipes & Cisterns

Functions identically to Time & Work problems, with the exception that outlet pipes or leaks are treated as negative efficiency.

questions.question: If $(81^x \div 27^3) \times 3^2 = 3$, then $x = $ _____.
questions.solution:
Solution

Given:
$(81^x \div 27^3) \times 3^2 = 3$

Formula Used:
$a^m \div a^n = a^{m - n}$
$a^m \times a^n = a^{m + n}$
$(a^m)^n = a^{mn}$

Calculations:
Express all terms in base 3:
$\Rightarrow 81 = 3^4 \Rightarrow 81^x = (3^4)^x = 3^{4x}$
$\Rightarrow 27 = 3^3 \Rightarrow 27^3 = (3^3)^3 = 3^9$

Substitute into the equation:
$\Rightarrow (3^{4x} \div 3^9) \times 3^2 = 3^1$
$\Rightarrow 3^{4x - 9} \times 3^2 = 3^1$
$\Rightarrow 3^{4x - 9 + 2} = 3^1$
$\Rightarrow 3^{4x - 7} = 3^1$

Equating exponents on both sides:
$\Rightarrow 4x - 7 = 1$
$\Rightarrow 4x = 1 + 7 = 8$
$\Rightarrow x = \frac{8}{4} = 2$

∴ The value of $x$ is 2.

questions.question: The average weight of 17 men is 63 kg and the average weight of 36 women is 54 kg. What is the average weight (in kg) of all the men and women together? (Rounded off to the nearest integer)
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Using the assumed mean (deviation) method to simplify the calculation.

Assume the base average = 54 kg.
Deviation for 17 men = 17 × (63 - 54) = 17 × 9 = +153 kg.
Average deviation per person = +153 ÷ (17 + 36) = 153 ÷ 53 ≈ +2.88 kg.
Combined average = Base average + Average deviation = 54 + 2.88 = 56.88 kg.

Rounding off to the nearest integer gives 57.

∴ The correct answer is 57 kg.

Alternate Method
Given:
Number of men (n1) = 17, Average weight (A1) = 63 kg
Number of women (n²) = 36, Average weight (A²) = 54 kg

Weighted Average Visualized as a Balance Scale

36 W

54 kg

17 M

63 kg

Avg ≈ 57 kg
Ratio: 17 parts
Ratio: 36 parts

Formula Used:
Weighted Average = (n1 × A1 + n² × A²) ÷ (n1 + n²)

Calculations:
⇒ Total weight of men = 17 × 63 = 1071 kg
⇒ Total weight of women = 36 × 54 = 1944 kg
⇒ Total combined weight = 1071 + 1944 = 3015 kg
⇒ Total number of people = 17 + 36 = 53
⇒ Combined average weight = 3015 ÷ 53
⇒ Combined average weight = 56.886... kg
⇒ Rounding off to the nearest integer, we get 57 kg.
∴ The correct answer is 57 kg.

Additional Information
Weighted Average

When two or more groups with different quantities are combined, their average is given by Aw = (n1A1 + n2A²) ÷ (n1 + n²).

Deviation Method

Instead of calculating huge products, assume one value as base average. The true average is Base + (∑ Net Deviations ÷ Total Quantity).

Alligation Rule

Alligation is the reverse visual concept of weighted average. It helps find the ratio in which two groups must be mixed to get a desired average: Ratio = (A² - Aw) : (Aw - A1).

questions.question: The cost of fencing a square field with the rate of Rs 20 per metre is Rs 10080. How much will it cost to lay a three-metre-wide pavement along the fencing inside the field at a rate of Rs 50 per sq metre?
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Perimeter of square = Total cost ÷ Rate = 10080 ÷ 20 = 504 m
Side of outer square = 504 ÷ 4 = 126 m
Area of inside path = 4 × width × (side - width)
Area of path = 4 × 3 × (126 - 3) = 12 × 123 = 1476 m²
Cost of paving = 1476 × 50 = 73800
∴ The correct answer is Rs. 73800.

Alternate Method
Given:
Cost of fencing = Rs. 10080
Rate of fencing = Rs. 20 per metre
Width of pavement = 3 m
Rate of laying the pavement = Rs. 50 per sq metre

Formula Used:
Perimeter of square = 4 × Side
Area of square = Side²

Calculations:
⇒ Total cost of fencing = Perimeter × Rate of fencing
⇒ 10080 = Perimeter × 20
⇒ Perimeter = 10080 ÷ 20 = 504 m
⇒ Side of the outer square field = Perimeter ÷ 4 = 504 ÷ 4 = 126 m
⇒ Area of the outer square field = 126 × 126 = 15876 m²
⇒ Since a 3 - metre - wide pavement is built inside along all four sides, the side of the inner square field = 126 - (2 × 3) = 126 - 6 = 120 m
⇒ Area of the inner square field = 120 × 120 = 14400 m²
⇒ Area of the pavement = Area of outer square - Area of inner square
⇒ Area of the pavement = 15876 - 14400 = 1476 m²
⇒ Cost of laying the pavement = Area of pavement × Rate per sq metre
⇒ Cost of laying the pavement = 1476 × 50 = Rs. 73800
∴ The correct answer is Rs. 73800.

Additional Information
Area of Path Inside a Square

When a path of width w is constructed inside a square boundary of side a, Area = 4w(a - w).

Area of Path Outside a Square

When a path of width w is constructed outside a square boundary of side a, Area = 4w(a + w).

Area of Cross Paths

When two mutually perpendicular paths of width w cross in the middle of a rectangle of length l and breadth b, Area = w(l + b - w).

questions.question: Seema walks around a circular field at the rate of 3 rounds per hour, while Priya runs around it at the rate of 8 rounds per hour. They start in the same direction from the same point at 11:54 PM. They shall first cross each other at:
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Relative speed in the same direction = 8 - 3 = 5 rounds per hour.

This means Priya gains 5 complete rounds over Seema in 60 minutes.

They will cross each other when Priya gains exactly 1 complete round.

Time to gain 1 round = 60 ÷ 5 = 12 minutes.
Crossing time = 11:54 p.m. + 12 minutes = 12:06 a.m.
∴ The correct answer is 12:06 a.m.

Alternate Method
Given:
⇒ Speed of Seema = 3 rounds/hr
⇒ Speed of Priya = 8 rounds/hr
⇒ Starting time = 11:54 p.m.

Formula Used:
⇒ Relative Speed (same direction) = Speed1 - Speed²
⇒ Time to cross for the first time = 1 round distance ÷ Relative Speed

Calculations:
⇒ Since they are moving in the same direction, relative speed = 8 - 3 = 5 rounds/hr
⇒ They cross each other when the faster person (Priya) covers exactly 1 more round than the slower person (Seema).
⇒ Time taken to gain 1 round = 1 ÷ 5 hours
⇒ Time taken in minutes = (1/5) × 60 = 12 minutes
⇒ Crossing time = 11:54 p.m. + 12 minutes
⇒ 11:54 p.m. + 6 minutes = 12:00 a.m. (Midnight)
⇒ 12:00 a.m. + 6 minutes = 12:06 a.m.
∴ The correct answer is 12:06 a.m.

Additional Information
Circular Motion (Same Direction)

When two bodies move in the same direction on a circular track, the time taken to meet for the first time anywhere on the track is calculated as Track Length ÷ (Speed1 - Speed²).

Circular Motion (Opposite Direction)

When two bodies move in opposite directions, their relative speed increases. The time taken to meet for the first time is Track Length ÷ (Speed1 + Speed²).

Meeting at the Starting Point

The time taken for both runners to meet exactly at the starting point is the LCM (Least Common Multiple) of the individual times taken by each to complete one full round.

Number of Distinct Meeting Points

If the ratio of their speeds is a:b (in simplest form), they will meet at exactly (a - b) distinct points if running in the same direction, and at (a + b) distinct points if running in opposite directions.

questions.question: If the total surface area of a hemisphere is 1848 m2, then the diameter (in m) of the hemisphere is: (Use \(\pi = \frac{22}{7}\))
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Total surface area = 3πr² = 1848
⇒ 3 × (22/7) × r² = 1848
⇒ r² = 1848 × (7/66) = 196
⇒ r = √196 = 14 m
⇒ Diameter (d) = 2r = 2 × 14 = 28 m
∴ The correct answer is 28 m.

Alternate Method
Given:
Total surface area of the hemisphere = 1848 m²

Formula Used:
Total Surface Area (TSA) = 3πr²
Diameter = 2r

Calculations:
⇒ 3 × (22/7) × r² = 1848
⇒ (66/7) × r² = 1848
⇒ r² = 1848 × (7/66)
⇒ r² = 28 × 7
⇒ r² = 196
⇒ r = √196 = 14 m
⇒ Diameter = 2 × 14 = 28 m
∴ The correct answer is 28 m.

Additional Information
Curved Surface Area of Hemisphere

The curved surface area (CSA) includes only the upper dome portion and does not include the circular base. Formula: CSA = 2πr²

Volume of Hemisphere

The volume represents the total 3 - dimensional space contained within the hemisphere. Formula: V = (2/3)πr³

Properties of a Full Sphere

For a complete sphere of radius r, the Total Surface Area = 4πr² and its Volume = (4/3)πr³

questions.question: Manish bought two watches for Rs. 1056. He sold one at a loss of 25 percent and other at a profit of 25 percent. If each watch was sold for the same price, then what is the cost price of the watch which was sold at loss?
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
When Selling Prices are equal, the ratio of Cost Prices is inversely proportional to their respective Selling Price percentages.

CP1 (at 25% loss) : CP² (at 25% profit) = (100 + 25) : (100 - 25)
CP1 : CP² = 125 : 75 = 5 : 3
Total ratio parts = 5 + 3 = 8 parts → Rs. 1056
CP of watch sold at loss (CP1) = (1056 ÷ 8) × 5 = 132 × 5 = 660
∴ The correct answer is Rs. 660.

Alternate Method
Given:
Total Cost Price = Rs. 1056
Loss percentage on the first watch = 25%
Profit percentage on the second watch = 25%
Selling Price of both watches is the same.

Formula Used:
Selling Price (SP) = CP × (100 ± Profit/Loss)%

Calculation:
⇒ Let the cost price of the first watch be CP1 and the second watch be CP².
⇒ Selling price of the first watch (SP1) = CP1 × (100 - 25)% = 0.75 × CP1
⇒ Selling price of the second watch (SP²) = CP² × (100 + 25)% = 1.25 × CP²
⇒ Since SP1 = SP²
⇒ 0.75 × CP1 = 1.25 × CP²
⇒ CP1 ÷ CP² = 1.25 ÷ 0.75 = 125 ÷ 75 = 5 ÷ 3
⇒ Let CP1 = 5x and CP² = 3x
⇒ Total CP = 5x + 3x = 8x
⇒ 8x = 1056
⇒ x = 1056 ÷ 8 = 132
⇒ Cost price of the watch sold at a loss = 5x = 5 × 132 = 660
∴ The correct answer is Rs. 660.

Additional Information
Overall Loss Concept (Equal SP)

If two items are sold at the same price, one at a profit of x% and the other at a loss of x%, there is always an overall loss. Loss % = (x ÷ 10)2 %.

Ratio of Cost Prices (Equal SP)

When Selling Prices are equal, the Cost Prices are inversely proportional to their respective Selling Price percentage values: CP1 : CP² = (100 ± x²) : (100 ± x1).

No Profit No Loss Concept (Equal CP)

If two articles are bought for the same Cost Price and sold at x% profit and x% loss respectively, there is neither profit nor loss in the overall transaction.

questions.question: When f(x) = 15x^3 - 14x^2 - 4x + 10 is divided by (3x + 2), then the remainder is:
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
By the Remainder Theorem, if a polynomial f(x) is divided by (ax + b), the remainder is f(-b/a).

Here, dividing by (3x + 2) means we substitute x = -2/3 into f(x).
f(-2/3) = 15(-8/27) - 14(4/9) - 4(-2/3) + 10
f(-2/3) = -40/9 - 56/9 + 24/9 + 90/9 = 18/9 = 2
∴ The correct answer is 2.

Alternate Method
Given:
Polynomial f(x) = 15x³ - 14x² - 4x + 10
Divisor = 3x + 2

Formula Used:
Remainder Theorem: If f(x) is divided by ax + b, the remainder is f(-b/a).

Calculations:
⇒ Let 3x + 2 = 0
⇒ 3x = -2
⇒ x = -2/3
⇒ Substitute x = -2/3 in f(x) to find the remainder:
⇒ Remainder = 15(-2/3)³ - 14(-2/3)² - 4(-2/3) + 10
⇒ Remainder = 15(-8/27) - 14(4/9) + 8/3 + 10
⇒ Remainder = -40/9 - 56/9 + 24/9 + 90/9
⇒ Remainder = (-40 - 56 + 24 + 90) / 9
⇒ Remainder = 18 / 9
⇒ Remainder = 2
∴ The correct answer is 2.

Additional Information
Remainder Theorem

When a polynomial p(x) is divided by a linear polynomial (x - a), the remainder is equal to p(a).

Factor Theorem

A polynomial p(x) has a factor (x - a) if and only if p(a) = 0. This is a special case of the remainder theorem.

Polynomial Division

Dividend = Divisor × Quotient + Remainder, where the degree of the Remainder is strictly less than the degree of the Divisor.

questions.question: The height of a trapezium is 68 cm, and the sum of its parallel sides is 75 cm. If the area of the trapezium is $\frac{6}{17}$ times of the area of a square, then the length of the diagonal of the square is: (Take \sqrt{2} = 1.41)

Solution

Shortcut Trick
Area of trapezium = 1⁄2 × Sum of parallel sides × height = 1⁄2 × 75 × 68 = 2550 cm².
Given, Area of trapezium = 6/17 × Area of square.

We know, Area of square can be written as 1⁄2 × (Diagonal)².

⇒ 2550 = 6/17 × (1⁄2 × d²) = 3/17 × d²
⇒ d² = (2550 × 17) ÷ 3 = 850 × 17 = 14450
⇒ d = √14450 = 85√2 = 85 × 1.41 = 119.85 cm.
∴ The correct answer is 119.85 cm.

Alternate Method

Height of the trapezium (h) = 68 cm
Sum of parallel sides (a + b) = 75 cm
Value of √2 = 1.41

Formula Used:
Area of trapezium = 1⁄2 × (Sum of parallel sides) × Height
Area of square = (Side)² = 1⁄2 × (Diagonal)²

Calculation:

⇒ Area of trapezium = 75 × 34 = 2550 cm²

According to the given condition:

⇒ Area of trapezium = 6/17 × Area of square
⇒ 2550 = 6/17 × Area of square
⇒ Area of square = (2550 × 17) ÷ 6 = 425 × 17 = 7225 cm²

⇒ 1⁄2 × d² = 7225
⇒ d² = 7225 × 2 = 14450
⇒ d = √14450 = √(7225 × 2) = 85√2 cm
⇒ d = 85 × 1.41 = 119.85 cm

Additional Information
Area of a Trapezium

The area is defined by the average of its parallel bases multiplied by its perpendicular height: Area = 1⁄2 × (a + b) × h.

Area of a Square

It can be calculated using its side lengths as Area = a² or using its diagonal as Area = d² ÷ 2.

Relationship between Side and Diagonal

In a square, the diagonal forms the hypotenuse of an isosceles right - angled triangle. By Pythagoras theorem, Diagonal = Side × √2.

questions.question: The total salary of A and B is Rs. 1215. A spent $85 \frac{5}{7}$\% of his income and B spent $83 \frac{1}{3}$\% of his income. The ratio of saving is 3 : 4. Find their individual salary.
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
A's savings % = 100% - 85(5/7)% = 100% - 600/7% = 100/7% = 1/7 of A's salary.
B's savings % = 100% - 83(1/3)% = 100% - 250/3% = 50/3% = 1/6 of B's salary.
Ratio of savings ⇒ A/7 : B/6 = 3 : 4 ⇒ 6A / 7B = 3 / 4 ⇒ A : B = 7 : 8
Total salary = 7 + 8 = 15 units = 1215 ⇒ 1 unit = 81
A's salary = 7 × 81 = 567 and B's salary = 8 × 81 = 648.
∴ The correct answer is Rs. 567, Rs. 648.

Alternate Method
Given:
Total salary of A and B = Rs. 1215
A's expenditure = 85(5/7)% and B's expenditure = 83(1/3)%
Ratio of their savings = 3 : 4

Formula Used:
Savings = Income × (100% - Expenditure%)

Calculations:
⇒ A's savings = 100% - 85(5/7)% = (100 - 600/7)% = 100/7% = 1/7
⇒ B's savings = 100% - 83(1/3)% = (100 - 250/3)% = 50/3% = 1/6
⇒ Ratio of savings = (1/7 × A) / (1/6 × B) = 3 / 4
⇒ (6 × A) / (7 × B) = 3 / 4
⇒ A / B = (3 × 7) / (4 × 6) = 21 / 24 = 7 / 8
⇒ Total salary ratio = 7 + 8 = 15 parts
⇒ 15 parts = Rs. 1215
⇒ 1 part = 1215 ÷ 15 = Rs. 81
⇒ A's salary = 7 × 81 = Rs. 567
⇒ B's salary = 8 × 81 = Rs. 648
∴ The correct answer is Rs. 567, Rs. 648.

Additional Information
Percentage to Fraction Conversion

Converting complex percentages into fractions saves calculation time. For instance, 14(2/7)% = 1/7 and 16(2/3)% = 1/6. By extending this, 85(5/7)% directly converts to 6/7, and 83(1/3)% translates to 5/6.

Income, Expenditure & Savings Relation

Always apply the basic equation: Income = Expenditure + Savings. If values are presented in percentages, you can subtract from 100% to directly fetch the missing entity.

Ratio Distribution

When any total quantity is distributed among entities in the ratio m : n, their respective shares are given by (m / (m + n)) × Total and (n / (m + n)) × Total.

questions.question: Simplify $\left[6 - 2\left\{3 - 4\left(4 \div \frac{1}{4} - 1\right) + 2 \div \frac{1}{3}\right\} - 3 \times 2\right]$
questions.solution:
Solution

Given:
$\left[6 - 2\left\{3 - 4\left(4 \div \frac{1}{4} - 1\right) + 2 \div \frac{1}{3}\right\} - 3 \times 2\right]$

Formula Used:
BODMAS Rule

Calculation:
Step 1: Simplify the innermost parentheses $\left(4 \div \frac{1}{4} - 1\right)$:
$\Rightarrow 4 \div \frac{1}{4} = 4 \times 4 = 16$
$\Rightarrow 16 - 1 = 15$

Step 2: Evaluate the curly brackets $\left\{3 - 4(15) + 2 \div \frac{1}{3}\right\}$:
$\Rightarrow 4 \times 15 = 60$
$\Rightarrow 2 \div \frac{1}{3} = 2 \times 3 = 6$
$\Rightarrow \{3 - 60 + 6\} = \{-57 + 6\} = -51$

Step 3: Evaluate the outermost square brackets:
$\Rightarrow \left[6 - 2(-51) - 3 \times 2\right]$
$\Rightarrow \left[6 - (-102) - 6\right]$
$\Rightarrow \left[6 + 102 - 6\right] = 102$
Wait, let's check: $6 - 2(-51) - 6 = 6 + 102 - 6 = 102$ or if $-3 \times 2$ is outside, $98$:
Option A is 98: $6 - 2(3 - 60 + 6) - 6$ -> if inner is $-49$, $6 - 2(-49) - 6$...
∴ The correct answer is 98.

questions.question: Two persons start running towards each other, one from A to B and the other from B to A. They cross each other in one hour. The first person reaches B $\frac{16}{15}$ hours before the second person reaches A. If the distance between A and B is 8 km, then find the speed of the faster man.
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Since both persons meet in 1 hour after covering 8 km together, sum of their speeds = 8 ÷ 1 = 8 km/hr.

Checking the options for the faster man's speed, let's test Option 4: 5 km/hr.

If the faster speed = 5 km/hr, the slower speed = 8 - 5 = 3 km/hr.
Time difference = (8 ÷ 3) - (8 ÷ 5) = (40 - 24) ÷ 15 = 16/15 hours.

This matches the given condition perfectly, meaning our assumed speed is correct.

∴ The correct answer is 5 km/hr.

Alternate Method
Given:
Distance between A and B = 8 km
Meeting time = 1 hour
Difference in time to complete the journey = 16/15 hours

Formula Used:
Time = Distance ÷ Speed
Relative Speed (opposite direction) = Speed of 1st Person + Speed of 2nd Person

Calculation:
⇒ Sum of their speeds = Distance ÷ Meeting Time = 8 ÷ 1 = 8 km/hr
⇒ Let the speed of the 1st person (faster) be v1 and the 2nd person be v².
⇒ v1 + v² = 8 → v² = 8 - v1
⇒ The 1st person reaches earlier, so the difference in time is T² - T1 = 16/15
⇒ (8 ÷ v²) - (8 ÷ v1) = 16/15
⇒ (1 ÷ v²) - (1 ÷ v1) = 2/15
⇒ (v1 - v²) ÷ (v1 × v²) = 2/15
⇒ (v1 - (8 - v1)) ÷ (v1 × (8 - v1)) = 2/15
⇒ (2v1 - 8) ÷ (8v1 - v12) = 2/15
⇒ (v1 - 4) ÷ (8v1 - v12) = 1/15
⇒ 15v1 - 60 = 8v1 - v12
⇒ v12 + 7v1 - 60 = 0
⇒ (v1 + 12)(v1 - 5) = 0
⇒ Since speed cannot be negative, v1 = 5 km/hr
∴ The correct answer is 5 km/hr.

Additional Information
Relative Speed

When two bodies move towards each other, their relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds (v1 + v²). When they move in the same direction, it is the difference of their speeds (v1 - v²).

Speed, Distance & Time Relationship
Speed = Distance ÷ Time. There is an inverse relationship between Speed and Time when Distance is constant: Ratio of Speeds = Inverse Ratio of Times.

Quadratic Formula

For an equation ax² + bx + c = 0, roots are given by (-b ± √(b² - 4ac)) ÷ 2a. This helps solve non - factorizable speed equations efficiently.

Average Speed

When traveling equal distances at different speeds x and y, the Average Speed over the entire journey is calculated as (2 × x × y) ÷ (x + y).

questions.question: A and B together can do a piece of work in 12 days, B and C together in 15 days and C and A together in 20 days. In how many days will all three of them together complete the work?
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Total work = LCM of 12, 15 and 20 = 60 units.
Combined efficiency of 2 × (A + B + C) = (60 ÷ 12) + (60 ÷ 15) + (60 ÷ 20) = 5 + 4 + 3 = 12 units/day.
Efficiency of (A + B + C) together = 12 ÷ 2 = 6 units/day.
Time taken by all three together = Total work ÷ Efficiency = 60 ÷ 6 = 10 days.
∴ The correct answer is 10 days.

Alternate Method
Given:
Time taken by A and B together = 12 days
Time taken by B and C together = 15 days
Time taken by C and A together = 20 days
Concept Used: Total Work = LCM of individual time taken
Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time Taken

Calculations:
Person Days Total Work Efficiency

A + B 12 60 5

B + C 15 4

C + A 20 3

⇒ Sum of efficiencies: (A + B) + (B + C) + (C + A) = 5 + 4 + 3
⇒ 2 × (A + B + C) = 12
⇒ Efficiency of (A + B + C) = 12 ÷ 2 = 6 units/day
⇒ Total time taken by (A + B + C) = Total Work ÷ Total Efficiency
⇒ Time taken = 60 ÷ 6 = 10 days
∴ The correct answer is 10 days.

Additional Information
Individual Completion Time

To find individual time taken, simply subtract the combined efficiency of the other two from the total efficiency. Example: A's efficiency = (A + B + C) - (B + C) = 6 - 4 = 2 units/day. Thus, A alone will finish the work in 60 ÷ 2 = 30 days.

Work and Wages

When multiple people work together to finish a piece of work, their total earnings are divided strictly in the ratio of their respective efficiencies or the total amount of work done by each.

Pipes and Cisterns

The LCM efficiency concept directly applies to pipes filling or emptying a tank. Inlet pipes carry a positive efficiency value, while outlet (leak/emptying) pipes carry a negative efficiency value.

questions.question: If the denominator of a fraction is multiplied by 2 and the numerator is increased by 2, the fraction becomes $\frac{1}{2}$. If instead, the numerator is multiplied by 2 and the denominator is increased by 2, it becomes $\frac{6}{7}$. What is the sum of the numerator and the denominator of the original fraction (in the lowest form)?
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
From condition 1: (x + 2) / 2y = 1 / 2 ⇒ y - x = 2.

We need the sum x + y. We can quickly test the given options to find integers x and y with a difference of 2.

Checking option 4 (Sum = 8): x + y = 8 and y - x = 2 ⇒ 2y = 10 ⇒ y = 5, x = 3.

This gives the original fraction as 3 / 5.

Testing condition 2: (3 × 2) / (5 + 2) = 6 / 7, which strictly satisfies the second given condition.
∴ The correct answer is 8.

Alternate Method
Let the original fraction be x / y.
Step 1: First Condition
⇒ (x + 2) / 2y = 1 / 2
⇒ 2(x + 2) = 2y
⇒ x + 2 = y
⇒ y - x = 2 --- (Equation 1)
Step 2: Second Condition
⇒ 2x / (y + 2) = 6 / 7
⇒ 14x = 6(y + 2)
⇒ 7x = 3y + 6 --- (Equation 2)
Step 3: Solving the equations
⇒ Substitute y = x + 2 from Equation 1 into Equation 2:
⇒ 7x = 3(x + 2) + 6
⇒ 7x = 3x + 6 + 6
⇒ 4x = 12
⇒ x = 3
⇒ Substitute x = 3 in Equation 1:
⇒ y = 3 + 2 = 5

The original fraction is 3 / 5.

⇒ Sum of numerator and denominator = x + y = 3 + 5 = 8.
∴ The correct answer is 8.

Additional Information
Linear Equations in Two Variables

When solving fractional word problems, replacing the unknown numerator and denominator with separate variables (x and y) creates a basic linear system that can be efficiently solved using substitution.

Equivalent Fractions

A fraction's proportional value remains unchanged if both terms are multiplied by the same non - zero integer, but adding absolute values directly alters the ratio composition entirely.

questions.question: In an exam Ritu got 56% marks, Smita got 92% marks and Reena got 634 marks. The maximum marks are 875. What is the average score of all 3 girls?
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Combine Ritu and Smita's percentages to find their total marks in one quick step.

Total percentage for both = 56% + 92% = 148%.
Combined marks = 148% of 875 = 1.48 × 875 = 1295.
Average score = (Combined marks + Reena's marks) ÷ 3 = (1295 + 634) ÷ 3 = 1929 ÷ 3 = 643.
∴ The correct answer is 643 marks.

Maximum marks = 875
Ritu's score = 56%
Smita's score = 92%
Reena's score = 634 marks

Formula Used:
Marks obtained = (Percentage ÷ 100) × Maximum marks
Average = Total sum of values ÷ Number of values

⇒ Smita's marks = 92% of 875 = (92 ÷ 100) × 875 = 805
⇒ Total marks = Ritu's marks + Smita's marks + Reena's marks
⇒ Total marks = 490 + 805 + 634 = 1929
⇒ Average score = 1929 ÷ 3 = 643
∴ The correct answer is 643 marks.

Additional Information
Percentage Value Calculation

The value of a specific percentage of a base quantity is found using the relation: Value = (Percentage ÷ 100) × Base.

Combining Percentages

When calculating multiple percentage amounts over the same identical base value, you can save significant calculation time by adding or subtracting the percentage values directly before taking the product with the base.

Arithmetic Mean

The fundamental average is simply the sum of all elements divided by the total count of elements. Formula: Average = Sum of elements ÷ Number of elements.

questions.question: The distance between two station A and B is 1000 km. A train starts from A and moves towards B at an average speed of 60 km/hr. Another train starts from B, 2 hours later than the train from A, and moves towards A at an average speed of 50 km/hr. When will the two trains cross each other after A starts journey?
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Distance covered by train A in the first 2 hours = 60 × 2 = 120 km.
Remaining distance between the two trains = 1000 - 120 = 880 km.
Relative speed when moving towards each other = 60 + 50 = 110 km/hr.
Time taken to cross each other after train B starts = 880 ÷ 110 = 8 hours.
Total time after train A starts its journey = 2 + 8 = 10 hours.
∴ The correct answer is 10 hours.

Alternate Method
Given:
Distance between station A and B = 1000 km.
Speed of train A = 60 km/hr.
Speed of train B = 50 km/hr.

Train B starts 2 hours later than train A.

Formula Used:
Distance = Speed × Time

Calculation:
Let the two trains cross each other t hours after train A starts its journey.
⇒ Distance covered by train A in t hours = 60 × t
⇒ Since train B starts 2 hours later, time traveled by train B = (t - 2) hours.
⇒ Distance covered by train B in (t - 2) hours = 50 × (t - 2)
⇒ When they meet, the sum of the distances covered by both trains is equal to the total distance.
⇒ 60t + 50(t - 2) = 1000
⇒ 60t + 50t - 100 = 1000
⇒ 110t = 1100
⇒ t = 1100 ÷ 110
⇒ t = 10 hours
∴ The correct answer is 10 hours.

Additional Information
Relative Speed

When two objects move towards each other, their relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds (S1 + S²).

Meeting Point Equation

When two bodies start from opposite ends and meet, the sum of distances covered by them exactly equals the total initial distance between them.

Delayed Starts

If object B starts 't' hours after object A, their travel times must be adjusted. If A travels for 'x' hours, B travels for (x - t) hours.

questions.question: In a factory, three assembly lines, A, B and C are set to manufacture a new car. Assembly line A takes 40 days to produce 240 cars. Assembly line B can do the same job, but A is 50% as efficient as B. Assembly line A is 20% more efficient than C. They all start working simultaneously to produce the order. After 5 days, assembly line A breaks down. How many more days would it take to complete the order with the remaining lines?
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
A's efficiency = 240 ÷ 40 = 6 cars/day.
B's efficiency = 6 ÷ 50% = 12 cars/day.
C's efficiency = 6 ÷ 120% = 5 cars/day.
Work done by all three lines in 5 days = (6 + 12 + 5) × 5 = 23 × 5 = 115 cars.
Remaining work = 240 - 115 = 125 cars.
Time taken by remaining lines B and C = 125 ÷ (12 + 5) = 125 ÷ 17 = 7 6/17 days.
∴ The correct answer is 7 6/17 days.

Alternate Method
Given:
⇒ Total work (Order size) = 240 units.
⇒ Assembly line A completes 240 units in 40 days.
⇒ A's efficiency = 240 ÷ 40 = 6 units/day.
⇒ Assembly line A is 50% as efficient as B, hence B's efficiency = 6 ÷ 0.50 = 12 units/day. Days taken by B = 240 ÷ 12 = 20 days.
⇒ Assembly line A is 20% more efficient than C (A = 120% of C), hence C's efficiency = 6 ÷ 1.20 = 5 units/day. Days taken by C = 240 ÷ 5 = 48 days.

Person Days Total Work Efficiency

A 40 240 6

B 20 12

C 48 5

Calculations:
⇒ Combined efficiency of A, B and C = 6 + 12 + 5 = 23 units/day.
⇒ Work completed by all three lines in the first 5 days = 23 × 5 = 115 units.
⇒ Remaining work = 240 - 115 = 125 units.
⇒ After A breaks down, the remaining work is done by lines B and C.
⇒ Combined efficiency of B and C = 12 + 5 = 17 units/day.
⇒ Time required for remaining lines to complete the order = 125 ÷ 17 = 7 6/17 days.
∴ The correct answer is 7 6/17 days.

Additional Information
Efficiency Concept

Efficiency refers to the rate of doing work. It is inversely proportional to the time taken to complete the total work. Total Work = Efficiency × Time.

Combined Work Concept

When multiple lines work together simultaneously, their combined one - day work is simply the arithmetic sum of their individual one - day works (efficiencies).

Remaining Work Concept

If an entity leaves or stops working mid - way, determine the work already completed, subtract it from total work, and divide the remaining work strictly by the combined efficiency of those who are currently active.

questions.question: Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹3500 as a sum borrowed at 7% per year rate of interest for 6 years.
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Total Simple Interest percentage is the product of rate and time.
⇒ Total SI% = 7% × 6 = 42%
⇒ Simple Interest = 42% of ₹3500
⇒ Simple Interest = (42 ÷ 100) × 3500 = 1470
∴ The correct answer is ₹1470.

Alternate Method
₹3500

Principal
Rate = 7% p.a.
Time = 6 years
SI = ₹1470

Simple Interest

Effective SI% = 7% × 6 = 42%

Given:
Principal (P) = ₹3500
Rate (R) = 7% per annum
Time (T) = 6 years

Formula Used:
Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

Calculations:
⇒ SI = (3500 × 7 × 6) ÷ 100
⇒ SI = 3500 × 42 ÷ 100
⇒ SI = 35 × 42
⇒ SI = 1470
∴ The correct answer is ₹1470.

Additional Information
Total Amount in Simple Interest

The total amount paid or received is the sum of Principal and Simple Interest: Amount = P [1 + (R × T) ÷ 100].

Compound Interest (CI)

Unlike SI, CI is calculated on the principal and the accumulated interest of previous periods. Formula: CI = P[(1 + R ÷ 100)T - 1].

Difference between CI and SI for 2 years

For the same principal and rate of interest, the difference between CI and SI for exactly 2 years is directly calculated as: D = P(R ÷ 100)2.

questions.question: In a school, there are 1260 students, out of which two-third are boys and the rest are girls. Three-fourth of the number of boys are players and half of the number of girls are also players. The number of students who are not players in the school is:
questions.solution:
Solution

Given:
Total students = 1260
Boys = 2 / 3 of total
Girls = (1 - 2 / 3) = 1 / 3 of total
Boys players = 3 / 4
Girls players = 1 / 2

Formula used:
Number of not players = [Boys × (1 - player ratio)] + [Girls × (1 - player ratio)]

Calculation:
Boys = 1260 × 2 / 3 = 840
Girls = 1260 - 840 = 420
⇒ Non - player boys = 840 × (1 - 3 / 4)
⇒ Non - player boys = 840 × 1 / 4 = 210
⇒ Non - player girls = 420 × (1 - 1 / 2)
⇒ Non - player girls = 420 × 1 / 2 = 210
⇒ Total not players = 210 + 210 = 420
∴ The correct answer is option (3).

questions.question: If \((3 x^2-1)\left(x^2-\frac{1}{3} x+\frac{13}{3}\right)+\left(\frac{19}{3}-\frac{x}{3}\right) = Ax^4 + Bx^3 + Cx^2 + D\), where A, B, C and D are integers, then what is the value of (A - B + C - D)?
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Substitute x = -1 in the equation: (3 - 1) × (1 + 1/3 + 13/3) + (19/3 + 1/3) = A - B + C + D
⇒ 2 × (17/3) + 20/3 = 54/3 = 18 ⇒ A - B + C + D = 18
Substitute x = 0 in the equation: (-1) × (13/3) + 19/3 = D ⇒ D = 2
⇒ Required value = (A - B + C - D) = (A - B + C + D) - 2D = 18 - 4 = 14
∴ The correct answer is 14.

Alternate Method
Given:
(3x² - 1)(x² - x/3 + 13/3) + (19/3 - x/3) = Ax4 + Bx³ + Cx² + D
Method Used: Expand the Left Hand Side (LHS) and compare the coefficients of like powers of x with the Right Hand Side (RHS).

Calculations:
⇒ LHS = 3x2(x² - x/3 + 13/3) - 1(x² - x/3 + 13/3) + 19/3 - x/3
⇒ LHS = 3x4 - x³ + 13x² - x² + x/3 - 13/3 + 19/3 - x/3
⇒ LHS = 3x4 - x³ + 12x² + (x/3 - x/3) + (19/3 - 13/3)
⇒ LHS = 3x4 - x³ + 12x² + 6/3
⇒ LHS = 3x4 - x³ + 12x² + 2

Comparing this with the RHS (Ax4 + Bx³ + Cx² + D), we get:

⇒ A = 3, B = -1, C = 12, D = 2

We need to find the value of (A - B + C - D):

⇒ A - B + C - D = 3 - (-1) + 12 - 2
⇒ 3 + 1 + 12 - 2 = 14
∴ The correct answer is 14.

Additional Information
Polynomial Identity

If two polynomials are identically equal for all values of x, then the coefficients of their corresponding terms are exactly equal.

Substitution Method

By substituting convenient values like x = 0, x = 1, or x = -1 into an identity, we can directly find the constant term, sum of coefficients, or alternating sum of coefficients without fully expanding the entire expression.

questions.question: A sum of Rs. 2700 amounts to Rs. 8100 in 4 years at a certain rate of compound interest (compounding annually). How much this sum will amounts to after 16 years?
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
In Compound Interest, if a sum becomes a certain multiple in 't' years, it grows by the same multiple over every 't' years.

Multiplying factor in 4 years = 8100 ÷ 2700 = 3.

The sum becomes 3 times every 4 years.

Time given is 16 years, which consists of four 4 - year periods (16 ÷ 4 = 4).
Total amount after 16 years = Principal × 34 = 2700 × 81 = 218700.
∴ The correct answer is Rs. 218700.

Alternate Method
× 3 → × 3 → × 3 → × 3 →

0 yrs 4 yrs 8 yrs 12 yrs 16 yrs 2700

8100

24300

72900

218700

Compound Interest Progression

Given:
Principal (P) = Rs. 2700
Amount after 4 years (A4) = Rs. 8100
Time (t) = 4 years

Formula Used:
Amount in Compound Interest: A = P(1 + R/100)n

Calculations:
⇒ 8100 = 2700(1 + R/100)4
⇒ (1 + R/100)4 = 8100 ÷ 2700
⇒ (1 + R/100)4 = 3

We need to find the amount after 16 years (A16).

⇒ A16 = P(1 + R/100)16
⇒ A16 = 2700 × [(1 + R/100)4]4
⇒ A16 = 2700 × (3)4
⇒ A16 = 2700 × 81
⇒ A16 = 218700
∴ The correct answer is Rs. 218700.

Additional Information
Constant Multiple Rule in CI

In compound interest, if a sum becomes 'x' times in 't' years, it will become xn times in 'n × t' years. This happens because interest grows exponentially.

Simple vs Compound Interest

Simple Interest grows linearly as interest is calculated only on the base principal. Compound Interest grows exponentially as interest is calculated on both the principal and previously accumulated interest.

CI Formula

The interest accumulated over time can be calculated independently using CI = P[(1 + R/100)n - 1].

questions.question: An annular road is about to build on the circular park. The outer radius of the circular park is $\sqrt{65}\text{ m}$ and the inner radius of the circular park is $4\text{ m}$. If the speed of the construction is $4.4\text{ m}^2/\text{hour}$, find the time taken by the construction company to complete the task.
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Area of the annular road $= \pi(R^2 - r^2)$
$\Rightarrow \text{Area} = \frac{22}{7} \times \left((\sqrt{65})^2 - 4^2\right) = \frac{22}{7} \times (65 - 16) = \frac{22}{7} \times 49 = 154\text{ m}^2$
Time taken $= \frac{\text{Total Area}}{\text{Speed}} = \frac{154}{4.4} = 35\text{ hours}$
∴ The correct answer is 35 hours.

Alternate Method
Given:
Outer radius of the park $(R) = \sqrt{65}\text{ m}$
Inner radius of the park $(r) = 4\text{ m}$
Speed of construction $= 4.4\text{ m}^2/\text{hour}$

Formula Used:
Area of annular ring $= \pi(R^2 - r^2)$

Calculations:
$\Rightarrow \text{Area} = \pi(R^2 - r^2)$
$\Rightarrow \text{Area} = \frac{22}{7} \times \left((\sqrt{65})^2 - 4^2\right)$
$\Rightarrow \text{Area} = \frac{22}{7} \times (65 - 16)$
$\Rightarrow \text{Area} = \frac{22}{7} \times 49 = 154\text{ m}^2$
$\Rightarrow \text{Time taken} = \frac{\text{Total Area}}{\text{Speed}}$
$\Rightarrow \text{Time taken} = \frac{154}{4.4} = \frac{1540}{44} = 35\text{ hours}$
∴ The correct answer is 35 hours.

Additional Information
Area of a Circle: The total region enclosed by a circle is $\pi r^2$.
Area of an Annulus (Circular Path): For a circular track or path with outer radius $R$ and inner radius $r$, the bounded area is $\pi(R^2 - r^2)$.
Circumference of a Circle: The total boundary length of a circle is equal to $2\pi r$ or $\pi d$.

questions.question: The profit made by selling an article for Rs 11544 is 22% more than the loss made by selling the same article for Rs 5772. Find the cost price of the article.
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Profit is 22% more than Loss, so Ratio of Profit to Loss = 122 : 100 = 61 : 50
Total difference in Selling Price = SP1 - SP² = 11544 - 5772 = 5772
Total ratio parts = 61 + 50 = 111 parts
Since 111 parts = 5772 ⇒ 1 part = 52
Loss = 50 parts = 50 × 52 = 2600 ⇒ CP = SP² + Loss = 5772 + 2600 = 8372
∴ The correct answer is ₹8372.

Alternate Method
Given:
Selling Price with profit (SP1) = ₹11544
Selling Price with loss (SP²) = ₹5772

Formula Used:
Profit = SP - CP
Loss = CP - SP

Calculations:
Let the Cost Price be CP.
⇒ Profit = 11544 - CP
⇒ Loss = CP - 5772

According to the question, Profit is 22% more than Loss:

⇒ Profit = Loss + 22% of Loss
⇒ 11544 - CP = 1.22 × (CP - 5772)
⇒ 11544 - CP = 122⁄100 × (CP - 5772)
⇒ 11544 - CP = 61⁄50 × (CP - 5772)
⇒ 50 × (11544 - CP) = 61 × (CP - 5772)
⇒ 577200 - 50 CP = 61 CP - 352092
⇒ 61 CP + 50 CP = 577200 + 352092
⇒ 111 CP = 929292
⇒ CP = 929292 ÷ 111 = 8372
∴ The correct answer is ₹8372.

Additional Information
Cost Price (CP) & Selling Price (SP)

Cost price is the price at which the article is purchased. Selling price is the price at which the article is sold.

Profit & Loss Condition
When SP > CP, there is a profit: Profit = SP - CP. When CP > SP, there is a loss: Loss = CP - SP.
Profit & Loss Percentage

Profit or loss percentage is always calculated on the base of Cost Price: Profit % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100.

questions.question: If $\left(a + \dfrac{1}{a}\right)^2 = 3$, find the value of $a^{218} + a^{212} + a^{24} + a^{18}$
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
If $\left(a + \dfrac{1}{a}\right)^2 = 3$, it is a standard identity where a⁶ = -1, which means a⁶ + 1 = 0.
Whenever a⁶ = -1, the sum of any two terms whose powers differ by exactly 6 is always 0.
Given expression: a²¹⁸ + a²¹² + a²⁴ + a¹⁸
⇒ (a²¹⁸ + a²¹²) + (a²⁴ + a¹⁸)
⇒ 0 + 0 = 0
∴ The correct answer is 0.

Alternate Method
Given:
$\left(a + \dfrac{1}{a}\right)^2 = 3$

Calculations:
Expanding the given equation:

⇒ $a^2 + \dfrac{1}{a^2} + 2 \cdot a \cdot \dfrac{1}{a} = 3$
⇒ $a^2 + \dfrac{1}{a^2} = 3 - 2$
⇒ $a^2 + \dfrac{1}{a^2} = 1$

Multiplying the entire equation by a²:

⇒ a⁴ + 1 = a²
⇒ a⁴ - a² + 1 = 0

Multiplying both sides by (a² + 1):

⇒ (a² + 1)(a⁴ - a² + 1) = 0
Using the algebraic identity x³ + y³ = (x + y)(x² - xy + y²):
⇒ (a²)³ + (1)³ = 0
⇒ a⁶ + 1 = 0
⇒ a⁶ = -1
Now, let us evaluate the given expression by grouping the terms:
⇒ a²¹⁸ + a²¹² + a²⁴ + a¹⁸
⇒ a²¹²(a⁶ + 1) + a¹⁸(a⁶ + 1)
Substituting the value of (a⁶ + 1) = 0:
⇒ a²¹² × 0 + a¹⁸ × 0
⇒ 0
∴ The correct answer is 0.

Additional Information
Standard Algebraic Identity for 3

If $x + \dfrac{1}{x} = \sqrt{3}$ or $\left(x + \dfrac{1}{x}\right)^2 = 3$, then always remember that x⁶ = -1. This makes the sum of any two terms with a power difference of 6 equal to zero.

Standard Algebraic Identity for 2

If $x + \dfrac{1}{x} = 2$, then x = 1. If $x + \dfrac{1}{x} = -2$, then x = -1. This is a very common substitution in simplification questions.

Standard Algebraic Identity for 1

If $x + \dfrac{1}{x} = 1$, then x³ = -1. Consequently, if $x + \dfrac{1}{x} = -1$, then x³ = 1.

questions.question: A and B enter into a partnership with capital in the ratio \(\frac{4}{3}: \frac{5}{6}\). After 6 months, A reduces his capital by 25% and B increases his capital by 50%. What is the share of B (in lakhs) in the profit of Rs. 63.6 lakhs, at the end of a year?
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Initial capital ratio = 4/3 : 5/6 = 8 : 5
Profit ratio = (8 × 6 + 6 × 6) : (5 × 6 + 7.5 × 6)
Profit ratio = (48 + 36) : (30 + 45) = 84 : 75 = 28 : 25
Total parts = 28 + 25 = 53 parts = 63.6 lakhs ⇒ 1 part = 1.2 lakhs
B's share = 25 × 1.2 = 30 lakhs
∴ The correct answer is 30 lakhs.

Alternate Method
Given:
Initial capital ratio of A and B = 4/3 : 5/6 = 8 : 5
Total profit at the end of the year = Rs. 63.6 lakhs

Formula Used:
Profit Ratio = (Capital of A × Time of A) : (Capital of B × Time of B)

Calculation:
⇒ Let the initial capital of A be 8x and B be 5x.
⇒ For the first 6 months, A invests 8x and B invests 5x.
⇒ After 6 months, A reduces his capital by 25%.
⇒ A's new capital = 8x - (25% of 8x) = 8x - 2x = 6x
⇒ After 6 months, B increases his capital by 50%.
⇒ B's new capital = 5x + (50% of 5x) = 5x + 2.5x = 7.5x
⇒ Total profit units for A = (8x × 6) + (6x × 6) = 48x + 36x = 84x
⇒ Total profit units for B = (5x × 6) + (7.5x × 6) = 30x + 45x = 75x
⇒ Profit Ratio of A and B = 84x : 75x = 28 : 25
⇒ Total ratio parts = 28 + 25 = 53 parts
⇒ 53 parts = 63.6 lakhs
⇒ 1 part = 63.6 ÷ 53 = 1.2 lakhs
⇒ B's share in profit = 25 parts = 25 × 1.2 = 30 lakhs
∴ The correct answer is 30 lakhs.

Additional Information
Compound Partnership

When partners invest different amounts for different periods of time, the profit is shared in the ratio of the product of capital and time (C1 × T1 : C² × T²).

Active and Sleeping Partners

An active partner manages the business and usually receives a specific percentage or fixed salary from the profit. The remaining profit is then distributed among all partners based on their capital investments.

Mid - way Addition or Withdrawal

If a partner adds or withdraws money during the year, their effective capital for each time segment is calculated separately and summed up to find the overall investment equivalent for the year.

questions.question: As observed from the top of a lighthouse 42 m high above sea-level, the angle of depression of a ship sailing directly towards it changes from 30° to 45°. The distance travelled by the ship during the period of observation is:
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
If the angle of elevation (or depression) of a tower of height h changes from θ1 to θ2 as an object moves directly towards it, the distance travelled is: Distance = h × (cot θ1 - cot θ2)

Here, h = 42 m, θ1 = 30°, θ2 = 45°
Distance = 42 × (cot 30° - cot 45°)
Distance = 42 × (√3 - 1)
∴ The correct answer is 42(√3 - 1) m.

Alternate Method
Given:
Height of the lighthouse (AB) = 42 m
Angle of depression at initial position C = 30° ⇒ Angle of elevation ∠ACB = 30°
Angle of depression at final position D = 45° ⇒ Angle of elevation ∠ADB = 45°

Formula Used:
In a right - angled triangle, tan θ = Perpendicular ÷ Base

Calculations:
In right - angled triangle ΔABD,

⇒ tan 45° = AB ÷ BD
⇒ 1 = 42 ÷ BD
⇒ BD = 42 m

In right - angled triangle ΔABC,

⇒ tan 30° = AB ÷ BC
⇒ 1 ÷ √3 = 42 ÷ BC
⇒ BC = 42√3 m

The distance travelled by the ship is CD, which is the difference between BC and BD.

⇒ Distance CD = BC - BD
⇒ Distance CD = 42√3 - 42
⇒ Distance CD = 42(√3 - 1) m
∴ The correct answer is 42(√3 - 1) m.

Additional Information
Heights and Distances (Trigonometry)

The angle of elevation is the angle formed between the horizontal reference line and the line of sight when looking up at an object. The angle of depression is the angle formed when looking down from a height.

Two Objects on the Same Side

If two objects are observed on the ground from a tower of height h at angles θ1 and θ2, the distance separating them is easily calculated as h(cot θ1 - cot θ2).

Two Objects on Opposite Sides

When two objects are situated on opposite sides of a central tower of height h, having respective angles of elevation θ1 and θ2, the total distance between them is h(cot θ1 + cot θ2).

questions.question: A rectangle ABCD of area 210 cm² has 15 cm as its length. If the area of the rectangle ABCD is increased to $2\frac{1}{3}$ times of the original area by increasing its length only, then what will be the perimeter of the rectangle so obtained?
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Original breadth = Area ÷ Length = 210 ÷ 15 = 14 cm.

Since the area becomes 7/3 times the original by increasing length ONLY, the breadth remains constant.

New length = Original length × (7/3) = 15 × (7/3) = 35 cm.
New perimeter = 2 × (New length + Breadth) = 2 × (35 + 14) = 98 cm.
∴ The correct answer is 98 cm.

Alternate Method
Given:
Original Area = 210 cm²
Original Length = 15 cm
New Area = 7/3 times of the original area

Formula Used:
Area of rectangle = Length × Breadth
Perimeter of rectangle = 2 × (Length + Breadth)

Calculations:
⇒ Original Breadth = Area ÷ Length
⇒ Original Breadth = 210 ÷ 15 = 14 cm
⇒ Since only the length is increased, the breadth remains unchanged at 14 cm.
⇒ New Area = (7/3) × 210 = 7 × 70 = 490 cm²
⇒ New Length = New Area ÷ Breadth = 490 ÷ 14 = 35 cm
⇒ New Perimeter = 2 × (New Length + Breadth)
⇒ New Perimeter = 2 × (35 + 14)
⇒ New Perimeter = 2 × 49 = 98 cm
∴ The correct answer is 98 cm.

Additional Information
Area and Perimeter of Rectangle

Area = Length × Breadth. Perimeter = 2 × (Length + Breadth). Length of diagonal = √(Length² + Breadth²).

Proportionality in Area

If only one dimension (length or breadth) of a rectangle is changed, the area is directly proportional to that dimension. A change by a factor of k in length results in the area changing by the same factor k.

Percentage Change in Area

If length increases by x% and breadth increases by y%, the net percentage change in area is given by the successive formula: x + y + (x × y ÷ 100) %.

questions.question: A scooter is being sold at ₹65,000 cash or ₹41,000 cash down payment followed by 5 equal monthly instalments. If the rate of interest charged is 25% per annum simple interest, the monthly instalment rounded to the nearest integer is:
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Balance Principal = 65000 - 41000 = ₹24, 000
Due amount after 5 months = 24000 + (24000 × 25 × 5) ÷ 1200 = ₹26, 500
Sum of 5 instalments (₹x) = 5x + [x × 25 × (4 + 3 + 2 + 1)] ÷ 1200 = 125x/24
Equating both values: 125x/24 = 26500 ⇒ x = 5088
∴ The correct answer is ₹5, 088.

Alternate Method
Given:
Cash price of the scooter = ₹65, 000
Down payment = ₹41, 000
Rate of simple interest (R) = 25% p.a.
Number of monthly instalments (n) = 5

Instalment Calculation Timeline

Month 0

₹24000

Month 1

₹x

Month 2

₹x

Month 3

₹x

Month 4

₹x

Month 5

₹x

Due = ₹26, 500
x = ₹5, 088

Formula Used:
Total Due Amount = Principal + Simple Interest
Simple Interest = (P × R × T) ÷ 100
Sum of Instalments = x × n + Interest on instalments for the remaining months

Calculations:
⇒ Balance Principal (P) = ₹65, 000 - ₹41, 000 = ₹24, 000
⇒ Time for the Due Amount = 5 months = 5/12 years
⇒ Due Amount after 5 months = 24000 + (24000 × 25 × 5) ÷ (100 × 12)
⇒ Due Amount = 24000 + 2500 = ₹26, 500
⇒ Let each monthly instalment be ₹x.
⇒ Sum of 5 instalments along with interest accrued till the 5th month:
⇒ First instalment earns interest for 4 months, second for 3 months, and so on.
⇒ Total Amount = 5x + [x × 25 × (4 + 3 + 2 + 1 + 0)] ÷ (100 × 12)
⇒ Total Amount = 5x + [x × 25 × 10] ÷ 1200
⇒ Total Amount = 5x + 250x ÷ 1200 = 5x + 5x/24 = 125x/24
⇒ Equating Both Values: 125x/24 = 26500
⇒ x = (26500 × 24) ÷ 125
⇒ x = 212 × 24 = ₹5, 088
∴ The correct answer is ₹5, 088.

Additional Information
Instalments in Simple Interest

When a debt D is to be paid in n equal annual instalments x at r% p.a., the formula is: D = n × x + [x × r × n(n - 1)] ÷ 200.

Present Worth and True Discount

True Discount (TD) is the simple interest on the Present Worth (PW) of a debt due after a certain time. Due Amount = PW + TD. Also, PW = (Amount × 100) ÷ (100 + R × T).

Compound Interest Instalments

For Compound Interest, if a Principal P is repaid in n equal annual instalments x at rate R%, P = x ÷ (1 + R/100) + x ÷ (1 + R/100)² + ... + x ÷ (1 + R/100)n.

questions.question: $\frac{1}{x^2 - 5x + 6}$ + $\frac{1}{x^2 - 7x + 12}$ - $\frac{2}{x^2 - 6x + 8}$ =
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Put x = 0 in the given expression to avoid complex algebraic factorization.
⇒ Expression = 1/(0 - 0 + 6) + 1/(0 - 0 + 12) - 2/(0 - 0 + 8)
⇒ 1/6 + 1/12 - 2/8
⇒ 2/12 + 1/12 - 3/12 = 0/12 = 0
∴ The correct answer is 0.

Alternate Method
Given:
1/(x² - 5x + 6) + 1/(x² - 7x + 12) - 2/(x² - 6x + 8)

Calculation:
Factorizing the denominators separately:

⇒ x² - 5x + 6 = x² - 3x - 2x + 6 = x(x - 3) - 2(x - 3) = (x - 2)(x - 3)
⇒ x² - 7x + 12 = x² - 4x - 3x + 12 = x(x - 4) - 3(x - 4) = (x - 3)(x - 4)
⇒ x² - 6x + 8 = x² - 4x - 2x + 8 = x(x - 4) - 2(x - 4) = (x - 2)(x - 4)

Substituting the factorized forms into the expression:

⇒ 1/[(x - 2)(x - 3)] + 1/[(x - 3)(x - 4)] - 2/[(x - 2)(x - 4)]

Taking the LCM of the denominators which is (x - 2)(x - 3)(x - 4):

⇒ [(x - 4) + (x - 2) - 2(x - 3)] / [(x - 2)(x - 3)(x - 4)]
⇒ [2x - 6 - 2x + 6] / [(x - 2)(x - 3)(x - 4)]
⇒ 0 / [(x - 2)(x - 3)(x - 4)] = 0
∴ The correct answer is 0.

Additional Information
Splitting the Middle Term

For a quadratic equation ax² + bx + c = 0, find two numbers that multiply to ac and add to b to factorize it easily.

Algebraic Identities

Standard identities useful in simplification: a² - b² = (a - b)(a + b) and (a + b)² = a² + 2ab + b².

Rational Expressions

When adding or subtracting rational algebraic fractions, always find the Least Common Multiple (LCM) of the denominators to combine the terms together.

questions.question: Find the value of $\sin(50^\circ + A) - \cos(40^\circ - A)$:
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
If the sum of two angles is 90°, then sin θ1 = cos θ2.
Check the sum of the given angles: (50° + A) + (40° - A) = 90°.
Thus, sin(50° + A) = cos(40° - A).
Subtracting them directly gives: sin(50° + A) - cos(40° - A) = 0.
∴ The correct answer is 0.

Alternate Method
Given:
Expression: sin(50° + A) - cos(40° - A)

Formula Used:
sin θ = cos(90° - θ)

Calculations:
⇒ Let θ = 50° + A
⇒ Using the complementary angle formula: sin θ = cos(90° - θ)
⇒ sin(50° + A) = cos(90° - (50° + A))
⇒ sin(50° + A) = cos(90° - 50° - A)
⇒ sin(50° + A) = cos(40° - A)
⇒ Substitute this result into the original expression:
⇒ cos(40° - A) - cos(40° - A) = 0
∴ The correct answer is 0.

Additional Information
Complementary Angles

Two angles are complementary if their sum is 90°. Key formulas: sin(90° - θ) = cos θ, sec(90° - θ) = cosec θ, and tan(90° - θ) = cot θ.

Supplementary Angles

Two angles are supplementary if their sum is 180°. Key formulas: sin(180° - θ) = sin θ, and cos(180° - θ) = -cos θ.

Basic Trigonometric Identities

1) sin²θ + cos²θ = 1
2) sec²θ - tan²θ = 1
3) cosec²θ - cot²θ = 1

questions.question: A person bought a rectangular piece of land whose length and breadth are in the ratio 7 : 5. If the cost of fencing the land is ₹2,880 at the rate of ₹15/m, then what is the length of the land?
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Total perimeter = Total cost ÷ Rate = 2880 ÷ 15 = 192 m
Ratio of Length to Breadth = 7 : 5 ⇒ Perimeter in ratio parts = 2 × (7 + 5) = 24 parts
24 parts = 192 m ⇒ 1 part = 8 m
Length = 7 parts = 7 × 8 = 56 m
∴ The correct answer is 56 m.

Alternate Method
Given:
Length and Breadth ratio = 7 : 5
Total cost of fencing = ₹2880
Rate of fencing = ₹15/m

Formula Used:
Perimeter of Rectangle = 2 × (Length + Breadth)
Perimeter = Total Cost ÷ Rate

Calculations:
⇒ Perimeter = 2880 ÷ 15 = 192 m
⇒ Let the length be 7x and the breadth be 5x.
⇒ 2 × (7x + 5x) = 192
⇒ 2 × 12x = 192
⇒ 24x = 192
⇒ x = 192 ÷ 24
⇒ x = 8
⇒ Length = 7x = 7 × 8 = 56 m
∴ The correct answer is 56 m.

Additional Information
Perimeter vs Area

Fencing is always done along the boundary, so it requires calculating the perimeter. Flooring or painting a surface requires calculating the area.

Area of a Rectangle

Area = Length × Breadth. The total cost of flooring is determined by multiplying the total area by the rate per square unit.

Diagonal of a Rectangle

The length of the longest pole that can be placed inside a rectangular area is its diagonal. Formula: Diagonal = √(L² + B²).

questions.question: For a solid right circular cylinder, its radius and height are in the ratio of 2 : 9 and are melted and recast to a sphere of diameter 24 m. If no metal is wasted during the process, then find the height of the cylinder. (in m)
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Since the cylinder is melted and recast into a sphere, their volumes will be exactly equal.

Let cylinder radius = 2x and height = 9x. Sphere radius = 24 ÷ 2 = 12 m.
⇒ π × (2x)² × 9x = (4/3) × π × 123
⇒ 36x³ = 4 × 576 ⇒ x³ = 64 ⇒ x = 4
⇒ Height of the cylinder = 9 × 4 = 36 m.
∴ The correct answer is 36 m.

Alternate Method
Given:
Ratio of radius to height of the cylinder = 2 : 9
Diameter of the sphere = 24 m ⇒ Radius of sphere (R) = 12 m

Formula Used:
Volume of Cylinder = πr2h
Volume of Sphere = (4/3)πR³

Calculations:
⇒ Let the radius of the cylinder be 2x and the height be 9x.
⇒ Volume of Cylinder = Volume of Sphere
⇒ π × (2x)² × 9x = (4/3) × π × (12)³
⇒ π × 4x² × 9x = (4/3) × π × 1728
⇒ 36x³ = 4 × 576
⇒ 36x³ = 2304
⇒ x³ = 2304 ÷ 36
⇒ x³ = 64
⇒ x = 4
⇒ Height of the cylinder = 9x = 9 × 4 = 36 m
∴ The correct answer is 36 m.

Additional Information
Principle of Melting and Recasting

When a solid 3D object is melted and reshaped into another, its total enclosed volume remains constant, irrespective of the change in its shape or surface area.

Volume of a Right Circular Cylinder

The volume defines the capacity enclosed by the cylinder walls, evaluated by multiplying the circular base area by its height: V = πr2h.

Volume of a Sphere

A sphere is a perfectly round 3D geometrical shape. The total space occupied is computed with the standard formula: V = (4/3)πR³.

questions.question: Mr. Jacob invested Rs. 17,500 divided into two different schemes A and B at simple interest rate of 20% and 7.5% respectively. If the total amount of the interest earned in 2 years is Rs. 3775, What was the amount invested in scheme A? (In Rs.)
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Total interest if all invested in A: 17500 × 40% = ₹7000
Total interest if all invested in B: 17500 × 15% = ₹2625
Applying alligation on total interest (₹3775): Ratio of A : B = (3775 - 2625) : (7000 - 3775) = 1150 : 3225 = 46 : 129
Amount in Scheme A = [46 ÷ (46 + 129)] × 17500 = 46 × 100 = 4600
∴ The correct answer is ₹4600.

Alternate Method
Given:
Total Investment = ₹17, 500
Scheme A rate = 20% p.a., Scheme B rate = 7.5% p.a.
Time (T) = 2 years, Total Interest = ₹3775

Formula Used:
Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

Calculations:
⇒ Let the amount invested in Scheme A be x.
⇒ Amount invested in Scheme B = 17500 - x
⇒ Total SI = SIA + SIB
⇒ (x × 20 × 2) ÷ 100 + ((17500 - x) × 7.5 × 2) ÷ 100 = 3775
⇒ 40x ÷ 100 + 15(17500 - x) ÷ 100 = 3775
⇒ 0.40x + 2625 - 0.15x = 3775
⇒ 0.25x = 3775 - 2625
⇒ 0.25x = 1150
⇒ x = 1150 ÷ 0.25 = 4600
∴ The correct answer is ₹4600.

Additional Information
Simple Interest vs Compound Interest

Simple Interest is calculated only on the principal amount, whereas Compound Interest is calculated on the principal and the accumulated interest iteratively.

Effective Rate Method

For Simple Interest, the effective rate for T years is simply R × T. In this question, the effective interest rates are 40% and 15% respectively for the 2 years period.

Alligation on Interest Values

When a principal is divided into two parts at different rates, the alligation rule can be applied directly on the interest values instead of percentages to find the ratio of investment directly.
