questions.question: The ratio of the number of boys and girls in a hostel is 5 : 7. If 40% of boys and 50% of girls are getting scholarships for their studies, what is the percentage of hostel students who are not getting any scholarships?
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Let the number of boys be 50 and girls be 70, making the total number of students 120.

Boys without scholarships = 60% of 50 = 30.
Girls without scholarships = 50% of 70 = 35.
Total students without scholarships = 30 + 35 = 65.
Required percentage = (65 ÷ 120) × 100 = 325 ÷ 6 = 54 1/6%.
∴ The correct answer is 54 1/6%.

Alternate Method
Given:
Ratio of Boys to Girls = 5 : 7
Boys getting scholarships = 40%
Girls getting scholarships = 50%

Formula Used:
Percentage = (Favorable Value ÷ Total Value) × 100

Calculations:
Let the number of boys be 5x and the number of girls be 7x.
⇒ Total students = 5x + 7x = 12x

Since 40% of boys get scholarships, those who do not get scholarships = (100 - 40)% = 60%

⇒ Number of boys without scholarships = 60% of 5x = (60 ÷ 100) × 5x = 3x

Since 50% of girls get scholarships, those who do not get scholarships = (100 - 50)% = 50%

⇒ Number of girls without scholarships = 50% of 7x = (50 ÷ 100) × 7x = 3.5x
⇒ Total students without scholarships = 3x + 3.5x = 6.5x
⇒ Required percentage = (6.5x ÷ 12x) × 100
⇒ (65 ÷ 120) × 100 = 1300 ÷ 24 = 325 ÷ 6 = 54 1/6%
∴ The correct answer is 54 1/6%.

Additional Information
Percentage Base Assumption

When working with ratios and percentages, assuming bases as multiples of 10 or 100 eliminates decimals and speeds up calculations significantly.

Complementary Percentage

If a certain percentage (P%) satisfies a condition, the remaining (100 - P)% does not. Directly calculating the required part saves an extra subtraction step.

Weighted Average

The combined percentage of multiple groups is essentially their weighted average: Combined % = (n1p1 + n2p²) ÷ (n1 + n²).

questions.question: A thief is spotted by a policeman from a distance of 249 m. When the policeman starts the chase, the thief also starts running. Assuming the speed of the thief is 4 m/s and that of the policeman is 7 m/s, how far the thief would have run before he is overtaken by the policeman?
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Since the time taken by both to reach the catch point is the same, distance is directly proportional to their speed.

Ratio of distances = Ratio of speeds = Policeman : Thief = 7 : 4
Difference in distance ratio = 7 - 4 = 3 parts
Here, 3 parts = 249 m ⇒ 1 part = 83 m
Distance run by the thief = 4 parts = 4 × 83 = 332 m
∴ The correct answer is 332 m.

Alternate Method
Given:
Initial distance between policeman and thief = 249 m
Speed of policeman = 7 m/s
Speed of thief = 4 m/s

Formula Used:
Distance = Speed × Time
Relative Speed (same direction) = S1 - S²

Calculations:
⇒ Relative speed = 7 - 4 = 3 m/s
⇒ Time taken to catch the thief = Distance ÷ Relative speed
⇒ Time = 249 ÷ 3 = 83 seconds
⇒ Distance run by the thief (d) = Speed of thief × Time
⇒ Distance = 4 × 83 = 332 m
∴ The correct answer is 332 m.

Additional Information
Relative Speed (Same Direction)

When two bodies move in the same direction, their relative speed is the difference of their individual speeds: Srel = S1 - S².

Relative Speed (Opposite Direction)

When two bodies move towards each other, their relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds: Srel = S1 + S².

Time to Catch/Meet

The time taken for a faster object to catch a slower one is calculated by dividing their initial distance gap by their relative speed.

questions.question: The amount payable on maturity of a certain sum which is invested for 5 years at a certain rate per cent p. a. is Rs. 9,800 and the amount payable on the same sum invested for 10 years at the same rate is Rs. 12,600. If simple interest is offered in both cases, the rate of interest p. a. is:
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Simple interest remains constant for every year.

SI for 5 years = A10 - A5 = 12600 - 9800 = ₹2800
Principal (P) = A5 - SI for 5 years = 9800 - 2800 = ₹7000
SI for 1 year = 2800 ÷ 5 = ₹560
Rate % = (SI for 1 year ÷ P) × 100 = (560 ÷ 7000) × 100 = 8%
∴ The correct answer is 8%.

Alternate Method
Given:
Amount after 5 years (A5) = ₹9800
Amount after 10 years (A10) = ₹12600

Formula Used:
Amount = Principal + Simple Interest
Simple Interest (I) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

0 Years 5 Years 10 Years

P

₹9800

₹12600 + ₹2800 (SI for 5 yrs) + ₹2800 (SI for 5 yrs)

P = ₹9800 - ₹2800 = ₹7000

Calculations:
⇒ Simple Interest for 5 years = Amount after 10 years - Amount after 5 years
⇒ SI for 5 years = 12600 - 9800 = ₹2800
⇒ Simple Interest for 1 year = 2800 ÷ 5 = ₹560
⇒ Principal (P) = Amount after 5 years - SI for 5 years
⇒ P = 9800 - 2800 = ₹7000
Now, substitute the values in the SI formula for 1 year:
⇒ 560 = (7000 × R × 1) ÷ 100
⇒ 560 = 70 × R
⇒ R = 560 ÷ 70 = 8
∴ The correct answer is 8%.

Additional Information
Simple Interest vs Compound Interest

Simple Interest is calculated only on the principal amount, hence it remains constant every year. Compound Interest is calculated on the principal plus the accumulated interest of previous periods.

Difference Between CI and SI for 2 Years

The difference between compound interest and simple interest for exactly 2 years at rate R% is given by the formula: D = P × (R ÷ 100)2.

Amount Formula for SI

The total amount A accumulated after time T at rate R is calculated directly as: A = P(1 + (R × T) ÷ 100).

questions.question: A dealer allows 36% discount on the marked price of an article and still gains 25%. If the cost price of the article is reduced by 20%, then how much percentage discount should she give now on the same marked price to earn the same profit percentage as before?
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Let Marked Price (MP) = 100 units.
Initial SP = 100 - 36% = 64 units.
Initial CP = 64 ÷ 1.25 = 51.2 units.
New SP = (0.8 × Initial CP) × 1.25 = Initial CP = 51.2 units.
New Discount % = 100 - 51.2 = 48.8%.
∴ The correct answer is 48.8%.

Alternate Method
Given:
Initial Discount = 36%
Initial Profit = 25%
New Cost Price = Reduced by 20%
New Profit = 25% (same as before)

Formula Used:
Selling Price (SP) = Marked Price (MP) × (100 - Discount%) ÷ 100
Cost Price (CP) = SP × 100 ÷ (100 + Profit%)

Calculations:
⇒ Let the Marked Price (MP) be 100 units.
⇒ Initial Selling Price (SP) = 100 × (100 - 36) ÷ 100 = 64 units.
⇒ Initial Cost Price (CP) = 64 × 100 ÷ 125 = 51.2 units.
⇒ The new Cost Price is reduced by 20%, so New CP = 51.2 × 0.8 = 40.96 units.
⇒ The dealer earns the same profit of 25%, so New SP = 40.96 × 1.25 = 51.2 units.
⇒ (Notice that New SP = Initial CP, because reducing by 20% and increasing by 25% cancel out exactly: 0.8 × 1.25 = 1).
⇒ New Discount = Marked Price - New Selling Price = 100 - 51.2 = 48.8 units.
⇒ Required Discount Percentage = (48.8 ÷ 100) × 100 = 48.8%.
∴ The correct answer is 48.8%.

Additional Information
Relation between CP and MP

A direct relationship formula connects Cost Price and Marked Price: MP ÷ CP = (100 + Profit%) ÷ (100 - Discount%).

Successive Discounts

When two consecutive discounts of a% and b% are offered, the effective single discount is calculated as (a + b - a × b ÷ 100)%. It always results in a lower effective discount than their straightforward arithmetic sum.

Mark Up Percentage

Mark up percentage is the percentage by which the Marked Price is set above the Cost Price. Mark Up % = (MP - CP) ÷ CP × 100.

questions.question: The compound interest on a sum of money for 3rd year & 4th year are 1206 and 1809 respectively. Find the 5 years S.I on the same sum.
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Ratio of consecutive years' CI gives the multiplier: 1809 ÷ 1206 = 3/2 ⇒ Rate = 50% (or 1/2).
CI for 3rd year = P × (3/2)² × (1/2) = 1206
⇒ P × 9/8 = 1206 ⇒ P = 1072
5 years SI = P × Rate × 5 = 1072 × 1/2 × 5 = 2680.
∴ The correct answer is Rs.2680.

Alternate Method
Given:
Compound Interest for 3rd year = Rs.1206
Compound Interest for 4th year = Rs.1809

Formula Used:
CI for (n + 1)th year = CI for nth year × (1 + R/100)
Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

Start (P)

1st yr

2nd yr

3rd yr

4th yRs. um

CI 1

CI 2

1206 / 1809 × (1 + R/100)

Calculations:
⇒ Multiplier = CI4 ÷ CI³ = 1809 ÷ 1206 = 3/2
⇒ (1 + R/100) = 3/2
⇒ R/100 = 1/2 ⇒ R = 50%
⇒ Amount at end of 2nd year (A²) = P × (1 + R/100)² = P × (3/2)² = 9P/4
⇒ CI for 3rd year = A² × (R/100)
⇒ 1206 = (9P/4) × (1/2)
⇒ 1206 = 9P/8
⇒ P = (1206 × 8) ÷ 9 = 134 × 8 = 1072
⇒ 5 years SI = P × R × T ÷ 100
⇒ SI = 1072 × 50 × 5 ÷ 100 = 1072 × 2.5 = 2680
∴ The correct answer is Rs.2680.

Additional Information
Successive Compound Interest

The difference between the compound interest of two successive years is effectively the simple interest calculated on the previous year's compound interest amount.

Compound Interest vs Simple Interest

SI remains constant for each year if the principal and rate are the same, whereas CI increases each year because interest is earned on accumulated interest.

Compound Interest Formula

Total Amount A = P(1 + R/100)n. Total CI = A - P. The specific CI for the nth year can be calculated as An - 1 × (R/100).

questions.question: In the given figure AOB is a quadrant of a circle where PT = 96 cm, PB = 36 cm, OT = r. Find radius of the circle.
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Using the Tangent - Secant Theorem: PT² = PB × PC, where PC is the total secant length.
The secant passing through the center forms total length PC = PB + 2r.
962 = 36 × PC ⇒ PC = 9216 ÷ 36 = 256 cm.
Since PC = PB + diameter ⇒ 256 = 36 + 2r
2r = 220 cm ⇒ radius r = 110 cm.
∴ The correct answer is 110 cm.

Alternate Method
Given:
Tangent PT = 96 cm, External segment PB = 36 cm.
Radius OT = OB = r.
Distance from center to P is OP = OB + PB = r + 36.

O / A

B / P

T / r

r

36 cm

96 cm

OP = r + 36

Formula Used:
Pythagoras Theorem: Hypotenuse² = Base² + Perpendicular²

Calculations:
⇒ The tangent PT is perpendicular to radius OT, making ∠OTP = 90°.
⇒ In right - angled ΔOTP:
⇒ OP² = OT² + PT²
⇒ (r + 36)² = r² + 962
⇒ r² + 72r + 1296 = r² + 9216
⇒ 72r = 9216 - 1296
⇒ 72r = 7920
⇒ r = 110
∴ The correct answer is 110 cm.

Additional Information
Tangent - Secant Theorem

If a tangent and a secant line intersect outside a circle, the square of the tangent is equal to the product of the external secant part and the total secant length.

Tangent to a Circle

A line tangent to a circle forms exactly a 90° angle with the circle's radius at the exact point of contact.

questions.question: The average marks of the students of a class in a particular exam is 80. If 5 students whose average marks in that exam is 40 are excluded, the average marks of the remaining students will be 90. Find the number of students who wrote the exam.
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Using the zero net deviation method around the overall average of 80: Total deviation of 5 excluded students = 5 × (40 - 80) = -200.

Number of remaining students = Total required deviation ÷ Surplus per student = +200 ÷ (90 - 80) = 20.
Total number of students = 20 (remaining) + 5 (excluded) = 25.
∴ The correct answer is 25 students.

Alternate Method
Given:
Overall average marks of the class = 80
Average marks of 5 excluded students = 40
Average marks of the remaining students = 90
Method Used: We can solve this efficiently using the Rule of Alligation to find the ratio of the number of remaining students to the excluded students.
Remaining

Excluded

90 / 40

80 / 40

10

Ratio → 40 : 10 = 4 : 1

Calculations:
⇒ From the Alligation cross diagram, Ratio of (Remaining students) to (Excluded students) = (80 - 40) : (90 - 80)
⇒ Ratio = 40 : 10 = 4 : 1
⇒ Let the number of remaining students be 4x and the excluded students be 1x
⇒ We are given that the number of excluded students is 5, so 1x = 5
⇒ Total ratio parts for all students = 4x + 1x = 5x
⇒ Total number of students = 5 × 5 = 25
∴ The correct answer is 25 students.

Additional Information
Combined Average Formula

If two groups have sizes n1 and n² with averages A1 and A², the combined average is given by: A = (n1A1 + n2A²) ÷ (n1 + n²).

Rule of Alligation

It is a quick method used to find the exact ratio in which two components or groups are mixed. The ratio is always taken as cross differences: (Higher Average - Combined Average) : (Combined Average - Lower Average).

Zero Net Deviation Rule

The sum of algebraic deviations of all items in a group from their arithmetic mean is exactly zero. Any missing quantity or number of observations can be found by balancing the negative and positive deviations.

questions.question: When the price of sugar gets raised by 30%, a person increases his expenditure on sugar only by 12%. By what percentage (correct up to two decimal places) should he reduce his consumption of sugar so as to be able to maintain the same level of expenditure?
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Let both the initial price and expenditure be 100.
New Price = 100 + 30 = 130
New Expenditure = 100 + 12 = 112
Required reduction on the new price = 130 - 112 = 18
% Reduction in consumption = (18 ÷ 130) × 100 = 13.846% ≈ 13.85%
∴ The correct answer is 13.85%.

Alternate Method
Given:
Percentage increase in price of sugar = 30%
Percentage increase in expenditure = 12%

Formula Used:
Expenditure = Price × Consumption

Calculation:
Let the initial price be 100 and initial expenditure be 100.
⇒ Initial Consumption = 100 ÷ 100 = 1 unit
⇒ New Price = 100 + 30 = 130
⇒ New Expenditure = 100 + 12 = 112
⇒ New Consumption = 112 ÷ 130 = 56/65 units
⇒ Reduction in consumption = 1 - (56/65) = 9/65 units
⇒ Percentage reduction = [(9/65) ÷ 1] × 100
⇒ Percentage reduction = 900 ÷ 65 = 180/13 = 13.846%
⇒ Rounding to two decimal places, it becomes 13.85%.
∴ The correct answer is 13.85%.

Additional Information
Percentage Change

The percentage change is calculated as the ratio of the difference between the final and initial values to the initial value, multiplied by 100. Formula: % Change = [(New Value - Initial Value) ÷ Initial Value] × 100.

Successive Percentage Change

If a quantity undergoes two consecutive percentage changes of a% and b%, the effective percentage change is calculated using the formula: Net % Change = a + b + (a × b) ÷ 100.

Base Change Concept

If the price of a commodity increases by R%, the reduction in consumption required to keep the expenditure exactly the same is given by: Reduction % = [R ÷ (100 + R)] × 100.

questions.question: An ice-cream cone with a lid has a total surface area equal to the area of another circle of certain radius. If the radius of the circle is equal to average of the slant height and the radius of the cone, then the ratio of the slant height of the cone to the radius of the circle is:
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Total surface area of cone = Area of circle ⇒ πr(l + r) = πR² ⇒ R² = r(l + r)
Given R = (l + r) ÷ 2 ⇒ l + r = 2Rs. ubstitute (l + r) in first equation: R² = r(2R) ⇒ R = 2r
Now, l + r = 2R = 2(2r) = 4r ⇒ l = 3r
Ratio of slant height to circle radius = l : R = 3r : 2r = 3 : 2
∴ The correct answer is 3 : 2.

Alternate Method
Given:
Total Surface Area of an ice - cream cone with a lid = Area of a circle with radius R.
Radius of the circle (R) = Average of the slant height (l) and radius (r) of the cone.
Formulas Used: Total Surface Area of a Cone = πrl + πr² = πr(l + r)
Area of a Circle = πR²

Calculations:
⇒ According to the given condition, Area of Circle = Total Surface Area of Cone
⇒ πR² = πr(l + r)
⇒ R² = r(l + r) ............. (Equation 1)
⇒ It is also given that R is the average of l and r:
⇒ R = (l + r) ÷ 2
⇒ Squaring both sides, R² = (l + r)² ÷ 4 ............. (Equation 2)
⇒ Equating Equation 1 and Equation 2:
⇒ (l + r)² ÷ 4 = r(l + r)
⇒ Since l + r is a strictly positive length, dividing both sides by (l + r):
⇒ (l + r) ÷ 4 = r
⇒ l + r = 4r
⇒ l = 3r
⇒ Substituting l = 3r back into the formula for R:
⇒ R = (3r + r) ÷ 2 = 4r ÷ 2 = 2r
⇒ The required ratio of the slant height of the cone (l) to the radius of the circle (R) is:
⇒ l : R = 3r : 2r = 3 : 2
∴ The correct answer is 3 : 2.

Additional Information
Total Surface Area of a Cone

It comprises the curved surface area (πrl) and the flat base area (πr²). Therefore, Total Surface Area = πr(l + r).

Volume of a Cone

The volume represents the total internal capacity of the cone. Formula: Volume = (1 ÷ 3)πr2h, where h is the perpendicular height.

Slant Height Relationship

The slant height (l), base radius (r), and perpendicular height (h) form a right - angled triangle. By Pythagoras theorem, l = √(r² + h²).

Area of a Circle

The two - dimensional space enclosed by the boundary of a circle is its area, represented by the formula Area = πR².

questions.question: If A and B are digits and A3 + 8B = 150, then the value of A - B is
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Look at the units column: 3 + B must give a sum ending in 0.
Since B is a single digit, 3 + B = 10 ⇒ B = 7.

This generates a carry of 1 to the tens column.

Look at the tens column: A + 8 + 1 (carry) = 15 ⇒ A = 6.
Therefore, A - B = 6 - 7 = -1.
∴ The correct answer is - 1.

Alternate Method
Given:
A³ + 8B = 150, where A and B are single digits.

Formula Used:
A two - digit number XY can be written as 10X + Y.

Calculations:
⇒ Expand the numbers A³ and 8B using their place values.
⇒ (10 × A + 3) + (10 × 8 + B) = 150
⇒ 10A + 3 + 80 + B = 150
⇒ 10A + B + 83 = 150
⇒ 10A + B = 150 - 83
⇒ 10A + B = 67
Since A and B are single digits, 10A + B represents the two - digit number AB.
⇒ This implies the two - digit number AB is 67.
⇒ By comparing the digits, A = 6 and B = 7.
⇒ We need to find the value of A - B.
⇒ A - B = 6 - 7 = -1.
∴ The correct answer is - 1.

Additional Information
Place Value Expansion

A general two - digit number XY is mathematically represented as 10X + Y, where X is the tens digit and Y is the units digit. For a three - digit number XYZ, the expansion is 100X + 10Y + Z.

Cryptarithm Puzzles

These are mathematical puzzles where digits are replaced by letters. The key is to analyze the units column first and account for carries to the next higher place value.

Digit Reversal Rule

When the digits of a two - digit number XY are reversed to form YX, the difference between the two numbers is always a multiple of 9: (10X + Y) - (10Y + X) = 9(X - Y).

questions.question: A cylinder of height 28 cm and radius 10 cm is melted and formed into 4 square base pyramids each has the same height H and the base length of each pyramid is equal. Find the height of the pyramid, if the length of its base is 20 cm.
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Volume of Cylinder = 4 × Volume of Square Pyramid
⇒ πr2h = 4 × (1/3 × a² × H)
⇒ 22/7 × 100 × 28 = 4 × 1/3 × 400 × H
⇒ 8800 = (1600/3) × H ⇒ H = (8800 × 3) ÷ 1600 = 16.5 cm
∴ The correct answer is 16.5 cm.

Alternate Method
Given:
Radius of cylinder (r) = 10 cm, Height of cylinder (h) = 28 cm
Base side of square pyramid (a) = 20 cm, Number of pyramids = 4
Let the height of each pyramid be H.

Formula Used:
Volume of Cylinder = πr2h
Volume of a Pyramid = 1/3 × Base Area × Height

Calculations:
When a solid is melted and recast to form new objects, the total volume remains constant.

⇒ Volume of Cylinder = 4 × Volume of Square Pyramid
⇒ πr2h = 4 × (1/3 × a² × H)
⇒ (22/7) × 102 × 28 = 4 × (1/3 × 202 × H)
⇒ (22/7) × 100 × 28 = 4/3 × 400 × H
⇒ 22 × 100 × 4 = (1600/3) × H
⇒ 8800 = (1600/3) × H
⇒ H = (8800 × 3) ÷ 1600
⇒ H = (88 × 3) ÷ 16
⇒ H = (11 × 3) ÷ 2
⇒ H = 33 ÷ 2 = 16.5 cm
∴ The correct answer is 16.5 cm.

Additional Information
Melting and Recasting

When a 3D object is melted and recast into another shape, the total volume always remains constant regardless of the change in dimensions.

Volume of a Cone

V = 1/3 × πr2h, where r is the base radius and h is the vertical height. A cone is essentially a circular base pyramid.

Volume of a Prism

V = Base Area × Height. The volume formula of a cylinder is a special case of a prism with a circular base.

questions.question: Pipes A and B can fill a tank in 4 hours and 6 hours 40 minutes, respectively; whereas a third pipe C can empty the full tank in 1 hour 40 minutes. A and B are opened at 2:00 p.m. and 3:00 p.m., respectively and C is opened at 4:00 p.m. The tank will be completely empty at:
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Total Work = LCM of (4, 20/3, 5/3) = 20 units.
Efficiencies: A = +5, B = +3, C = -12 units/hr.
Work done till 4:00 p.m. = (5 × 2) + (3 × 1) = 13 units.
Net efficiency after 4:00 p.m. = 5 + 3 - 12 = -4 units/hr.
Time to empty 13 units = 13 ÷ 4 = 3 hours 15 mins → 4:00 p.m. + 3 hrs 15 mins = 7:15 p.m.
∴ The correct answer is 7:15 p. m.

Alternate Method
Given:
Time taken by pipe A = 4 hours
Time taken by pipe B = 6 hours 40 minutes = 20/3 hours
Time taken by pipe C (to empty) = 1 hour 40 minutes = 5/3 hours

Pipe Time (Hours) Total Work Efficiency

A 4 20 + 5

B 20/3 + 3

C 5/3 - 12

Calculations:
⇒ Between 2:00 p.m. and 4:00 p.m. (2 hours), pipe A operates.
⇒ Volume filled by A = 5 × 2 = 10 units
⇒ Between 3:00 p.m. and 4:00 p.m. (1 hour), pipe B operates.
⇒ Volume filled by B = 3 × 1 = 3 units
⇒ Total volume filled by 4:00 p.m. = 10 + 3 = 13 units
⇒ At 4:00 p.m., pipe C is opened.
⇒ Combined efficiency of A, B, and C = 5 + 3 - 12 = -4 units/hour
⇒ The negative sign implies the tank starts emptying.
⇒ Time required to empty 13 units = 13 ÷ 4 = 3 hours 15 minutes
⇒ Tank completely empties at = 4:00 p.m. + 3 hours 15 minutes = 7:15 p.m.
∴ The correct answer is 7:15 p. m.

Additional Information
Pipes & Cisterns Rules

If a pipe can fill a tank in x hours, its filling rate is + 1/x per hour. If a pipe can empty it in y hours, its emptying rate is - 1/y per hour.

LCM Method for Total Capacity

For mixed fractions, the LCM of the numerators represents the Total Capacity. Efficiency = Total Capacity ÷ Time taken.

Net Filling / Emptying Rate

If net efficiency is positive, the tank is filling up. If net efficiency is negative, the tank is emptying. The time to empty is calculated only on the volume already filled in the tank.

questions.question: What is the value of \(\dfrac{3}{5} \times \left[ {\left( {\overline {\dfrac{9}{14} + \dfrac{3}{7}} \times \dfrac{7}{15}} \right) - \dfrac{3}{5}} \right]\)?
questions.solution:
Solution

Given:
\(\dfrac{3}{5} \times \left[ {\left( {\dfrac{9}{{14}} + \dfrac{3}{7}} \right) \times \dfrac{7}{{15}}} \right] - \dfrac{3}{5}\)

Formula used:
BODMAS Rule

Calculation:
\(\dfrac{3}{5} \times \left[ {\left( {\dfrac{9}{{14}} + \dfrac{3}{7}} \right) \times \dfrac{7}{{15}}} \right] - \dfrac{3}{5}\)

⇒ \(\dfrac{3}{5} \times \left[ {\left( {\dfrac{9 + 6}{14}} \right) \times \dfrac{7}{{15}}} \right] - \dfrac{3}{5}\)
⇒ \(\dfrac{3}{5} \times \left[ {\dfrac{15}{14} \times \dfrac{7}{15}} \right] - \dfrac{3}{5}\)
⇒ \(\dfrac{3}{5} \times \left[ \dfrac{1}{2} - \dfrac{3}{5} \right]\)
⇒ \(\dfrac{3}{5} \times \left[ \dfrac{5 - 6}{10} \right]\)
⇒ \(\dfrac{3}{5} \times \dfrac{-1}{10}\)
⇒ \(\dfrac{-3}{50}\)
∴ The correct answer is option (2).

questions.question: A hundred rupee note measures 15 cm × 8 cm and a bundle of 125 such notes is 2 cm thick. Find the value of the hundred-rupee notes that can be contained in a box of size 48 cm × 36 cm × 30 cm, if the bundles are tightly packed in it without any empty space.
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Volume of the box = 48 × 36 × 30 = 51840 cm³
Volume of 1 bundle = 15 × 8 × 2 = 240 cm³
Number of bundles = 51840 ÷ 240 = 216
Value per bundle = 125 × 100 = ₹12500
Total Value = 216 × 12500 = ₹27, 00, 000 = ₹27 Lakhs
∴ The correct answer is ₹27 Lakhs.

Alternate Method
Given:
Dimensions of a 100 - rupee note = 15 cm × 8 cm
Thickness of a bundle of 125 notes = 2 cm
Dimensions of the box = 48 cm × 36 cm × 30 cm

Formula Used:
Volume of a cuboid = Length × Breadth × Height
Number of items = Total Container Volume ÷ Volume of 1 item

Calculations:
⇒ Volume of the box = 48 × 36 × 30 = 51840 cm³
⇒ Volume of 1 bundle = 15 × 8 × 2 = 240 cm³
⇒ Number of bundles = 51840 ÷ 240 = 216
⇒ Total notes in the box = 216 × 125 = 27000 notes
⇒ Total value of the notes = 27000 × ₹100 = ₹27, 00, 000
⇒ Total value in Lakhs = ₹27 Lakhs
∴ The correct answer is ₹27 Lakhs.

Additional Information
Cuboid Volume

The space occupied by a 3 - dimensional solid with rectangular faces is its volume, calculated strictly as Length × Breadth × Height.

Packaging Optimization

When checking how many small items perfectly fit into a larger container without any gaps, divide the total volume of the container by the volume of a single small unit.

Number System Units

In the Indian numbering system, 1 Lakh equals 1, 00, 000 (one hundred thousand). This conversion simplifies managing large monetary values in competitive exams.

questions.question: The mean expenditure of 35 persons reduced by ₹1 when 7 new persons join the group and the total expenditure is increased by ₹42 find the new expenditure.
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Total change in expenditure = (New persons × New average) + (Old persons × Change in average)
⇒ 42 = 7 × New Average + 35 × (-1)
⇒ 42 + 35 = 7 × New Average ⇒ 77 = 7 × New Average
⇒ New Average = 11
⇒ New Total Expenditure = Total persons × New Average = 42 × 11 = 462
∴ The correct answer is ₹462.

Alternate Method
Given:
Initial number of persons = 35
Number of new persons joined = 7
Total number of persons = 35 + 7 = 42
Reduction in mean expenditure = ₹1
Increase in total expenditure = ₹42
Old Total = 35 × x
New Total = 42 × (x - 1)
Increase = 42
42(x - 1) - 35x = 42

Calculations:
Let the initial mean expenditure be x.
⇒ Initial total expenditure = 35 × x = 35x
New mean expenditure = (x - 1)
⇒ New total expenditure = 42 × (x - 1)
Since the total expenditure is increased by ₹42:
⇒ 42(x - 1) - 35x = 42
⇒ 42x - 42 - 35x = 42
⇒ 7x - 42 = 42
⇒ 7x = 84
⇒ x = 12
Therefore, initial mean expenditure = ₹12
⇒ New total expenditure = 42 × (12 - 1)
⇒ New total expenditure = 42 × 11 = 462
∴ The correct answer is ₹462.

Additional Information
Average Formula

Average = Sum of all observations ÷ Total number of observations.

Combined Average

When two groups of sizes n1 and n² have averages A1 and A² respectively, their Combined Average = (n1A1 + n2A²) ÷ (n1 + n²).

Effect of Change on Average

If every observation in a dataset is increased or decreased by a constant value 'k', the new average will also increase or decrease by the same value 'k'.

questions.question: The cost price of an article 'A' is 42.85% of the marked price of the article 'A'. If the article is sold at the discount of ₹100, then the profit percentage earned on the article 'A' is 50%. If the selling price of the article is ₹5.625x, then find the value of x^(3/5).
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Fractional value of 42.85% is 3/7. Let MP = 7 units, then CP = 3 units.

Profit = 50% ⇒ SP = 3 × 1.5 = 4.5 units.
Discount = MP - SP = 7 - 4.5 = 2.5 units.
2.5 units = ₹100 ⇒ 1 unit = ₹40 ⇒ SP = 4.5 × 40 = ₹180.
Now, 5.625x = 180 ⇒ (45/8)x = 180 ⇒ x = 32.
Value of x³/5 = (32)³/5 = (25)³/5 = 23 = 8.
∴ The correct answer is 8.

Alternate Method
Given:
Cost Price (CP) is 42.85% of Marked Price (MP).
Discount = ₹100
Profit percentage = 50%
Selling Price (SP) = 5.625x

Formula Used:
SP = CP + Profit
SP = MP - Discount

Calculations:
⇒ Fraction equivalent of 42.85% = 3/7
⇒ Let CP = 3a and MP = 7a
⇒ Profit = 50% of CP = 50/100 × 3a = 1.5a
⇒ SP = CP + Profit = 3a + 1.5a = 4.5a
⇒ Discount = MP - SP = 7a - 4.5a = 2.5a
⇒ 2.5a = 100
⇒ a = 100 ÷ 2.5 = 40
⇒ SP = 4.5 × 40 = ₹180
Given SP = 5.625x, so equating both values:
⇒ 5.625 × x = 180
⇒ (45/8) × x = 180
⇒ x = (180 × 8) ÷ 45 = 32

Finding the value of x³/5:

⇒ (32)³/5 = (25)³/5 = 23 = 8
∴ The correct answer is 8.

Additional Information
Marked Price and Discount

Discount is always computed on the Marked Price (MP). It denotes the reduction offered on the labeled price. Formula: SP = MP × (100 - Discount%) ÷ 100.

Profit and Loss Percentage

Profit or Loss is always evaluated on the Cost Price (CP) unless explicitly stated otherwise. Formula: SP = CP × (100 + Profit%) ÷ 100.

Crucial Percentage to Fraction Conversions

14.28% = 1/7 | 28.56% = 2/7 | 42.85% = 3/7 | 57.14% = 4/7 | 71.42% = 5/7 | 85.71% = 6/7.

questions.question: If $3 \tan \theta = 2\sqrt{3} \sin \theta$, where $0^\circ < \theta < 90^\circ$, then find the value of $\frac{3}{4}\left(\frac{\operatorname{cosec}^2 2\theta + \cot^2 2\theta}{\sin^2 \theta + \tan^2 2\theta}\right)$:
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Given: 3 tan θ = 2√3 sin θ
⇒ 3 × (sin θ / cos θ) = 2√3 sin θ ⇒ cos θ = 3 / 2√3 = √3 / 2 ⇒ θ = 30°
Substitute θ = 30° in the expression: (3/4) × [ (cosec² 60° + cot² 60°) ÷ (sin² 30° + tan² 60°) ]
⇒ (3/4) × [ (4/3 + 1/3) ÷ (1/4 + 3) ]
⇒ (3/4) × [ (5/3) ÷ (13/4) ] = (3/4) × (5/3) × (4/13) = 5/13
∴ The correct answer is 5/13.

Alternate Method
Given:
3 tan θ = 2√3 sin θ

Formula Used:
tan θ = sin θ / cos θ
cosec θ = 1 / sin θ , cot θ = cos θ / sin θ

Calculations:
⇒ 3 × (sin θ / cos θ) = 2√3 sin θ
Since 0° < θ < 90°, sin θ = ̸ 0. Dividing both sides by sin θ:
⇒ 3 / cos θ = 2√3
⇒ cos θ = 3 / (2√3)
⇒ cos θ = √3 / 2
⇒ θ = 30°

We need to find the value of:

⇒ (3 / 4) × [ (cosec² 2θ + cot² 2θ) / (sin²θ + tan² 2θ) ]
Substituting θ = 30° into the expression:
⇒ (3 / 4) × [ (cosec² 60° + cot² 60°) / (sin² 30° + tan² 60°) ]

Using standard trigonometric values:

⇒ cosec 60° = 2 / √3 ⇒ cosec² 60° = 4 / 3
⇒ cot 60° = 1 / √3 ⇒ cot² 60° = 1 / 3
⇒ sin 30° = 1 / 2 ⇒ sin² 30° = 1 / 4
⇒ tan 60° = √3 ⇒ tan² 60° = 3

Putting these values in the expression:

⇒ (3 / 4) × [ (4/3 + 1/3) / (1/4 + 3) ]
⇒ (3 / 4) × [ (5/3) / (13/4) ]
⇒ (3 / 4) × (5 / 3) × (4 / 13)
⇒ 60 / 156
⇒ 5 / 13
∴ The correct answer is 5/13.

Additional Information
Trigonometric Identities

The three primary Pythagorean identities are: sin²θ + cos²θ = 1, 1 + tan²θ = sec²θ, and 1 + cot²θ = cosec²θ.

Values of Trigonometric Ratios

Key values to remember for 30° and 60° angles: sin 30° = cos 60° = 1/2, sin 60° = cos 30° = √3/2, and tan 60° = √3.

Signs of Trigonometric Functions

In the first quadrant (0° to 90°), all six basic trigonometric functions (sin, cos, tan, cosec, sec, cot) yield positive values.

questions.question: The tops of two buildings, 90 m and 55 m high, are connected by a metal wire. If the metal wire makes an angle $\theta$ with the horizontal and $\tan \theta = \frac{3}{7}$, what is the distance (in metres) between the two buildings?
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Difference in heights of the buildings = 90 - 55 = 35 m.
From the right - angled triangle formed, tan θ = Height Difference ÷ Distance.
⇒ Distance = Height Difference ÷ tan θ
⇒ Distance = 35 ÷ (3/7) = (35 × 7) ÷ 3 = 245 ÷ 3
⇒ Distance ≈ 81.66 m, which is estimated to 82 meter.
∴ The correct answer is 82 meter.

Alternate Method
Given:
Height of taller building = 90 m
Height of shorter building = 55 m
Angle of the metal wire with the horizontal = θ
tan θ = 3/7

Formula Used:
In a right - angled triangle, tan θ = Perpendicular ÷ Base

Calculation:
⇒ Difference in height (Perpendicular) = 90 - 55 = 35 m
⇒ Let the horizontal distance between the buildings be 'd'.
⇒ In the right - angled triangle formed, tan θ = 35 ÷ d
⇒ 3/7 = 35 ÷ d
⇒ 3 × d = 35 × 7
⇒ 3d = 245
⇒ d = 245 ÷ 3
⇒ d ≈ 81.66 m
⇒ The estimated distance is 82 meter.
∴ The correct answer is 82 meter.

Additional Information
Angle of Elevation

The angle formed by the line of sight with the horizontal when viewing an object located above the horizontal level.

Trigonometric Ratios

For any right - angled triangle, tan θ = Perpendicular ÷ Base, sin θ = Perpendicular ÷ Hypotenuse, and cos θ = Base ÷ Hypotenuse.

Pythagoras Theorem

In a right - angled triangle, the square of the hypotenuse is equal to the sum of the squares of the other two sides: Hypotenuse² = Perpendicular² + Base².

questions.question: Avinash's age is 5 times his son Aravind's age. Four years hence, the age of Avinash will be four times Aravind's age. Find the average of their present ages.
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Present age ratio = 5 : 1 (Difference = 4)
Ratio after 4 years = 4 : 1 (Difference = 3)
Equating age difference: Multiply present by 3 → 15 : 3, future by 4 → 16 : 4

1 ratio part increase (16 - 15) corresponds to 4 years.

Total present age parts = 15 + 3 = 18 parts → Total age = 18 × 4 = 72 years.
Average of present ages = 72 ÷ 2 = 36 years.
∴ The correct answer is 36 years.

Alternate Method
Given:
Avinash's present age is 5 times Aravind's age.

Four years hence, Avinash's age will be 4 times Aravind's age.

Calculations:
Let Aravind's present age be x years.
⇒ Avinash's present age = 5x years

After 4 years:

⇒ Aravind's age = (x + 4) years
⇒ Avinash's age = (5x + 4) years

According to the given condition:

⇒ 5x + 4 = 4 × (x + 4)
⇒ 5x + 4 = 4x + 16
⇒ 5x - 4x = 16 - 4
⇒ x = 12

Finding their present ages:

⇒ Aravind's age = 12 years
⇒ Avinash's age = 5 × 12 = 60 years
Average of their present ages = (Aravind's age + Avinash's age) ÷ 2
⇒ Average = (12 + 60) ÷ 2
⇒ Average = 72 ÷ 2 = 36 years
∴ The correct answer is 36 years.

Additional Information
Ratio Difference Method for Ages

Since the age difference between two individuals remains constant throughout their lifetime, equating the difference in their ratio parts helps find the equivalent age directly without variables.

Cross - Multiplication Trick

For an initial ratio a:b, if an equal quantity x is added to both to form a new ratio c:d, then 1 ratio part = x(c - d) ÷ (ad - bc).

Concept of Average Ages

The average age of n persons is the sum of their ages divided by n. If every person's age increases by x years, the new average naturally becomes (Old Average + x).

questions.question: A man’s basic pay for a 40 hours’ week is Rs. 200. Overtimes is paid at 25% above the basic rate. In a certain week, he worked overtime and his total was Rs. 300. He therefore, worked for a total of (in hours):
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Basic rate = 200 ÷ 40 = Rs. 5/hr.
Overtime rate = 5 × 1.25 = Rs. 6.25/hr.
Overtime amount = 300 - 200 = Rs. 100.
Overtime hours = 100 ÷ 6.25 = 16 hours.
Total hours worked = 40 + 16 = 56 hours.
∴ The correct answer is 56 hours.

Alternate Method
Given:
Basic pay for 40 hours = Rs. 200
Total pay earned in a certain week = Rs. 300

Overtime rate is 25% above the basic rate.

Calculations:
⇒ Basic rate per hour = 200 ÷ 40 = Rs. 5
⇒ Overtime rate per hour = 5 + (25% of 5) = 5 + 1.25 = Rs. 6.25
⇒ Amount earned through overtime = Total pay - Basic pay = 300 - 200 = Rs. 100
⇒ Overtime hours = Overtime pay ÷ Overtime rate per hour = 100 ÷ 6.25 = 16 hours
⇒ Total hours worked = Basic hours + Overtime hours = 40 + 16 = 56 hours
∴ The correct answer is 56 hours.

Additional Information
Time and Wages

Wages are directly proportional to the time spent working if the rate is uniform. Formula: Total Wages = Rate per hour × Total hours worked.

Percentage Increase

When a value is increased by R%, the new value is Base × (1 + R/100). Here, the overtime rate is 1.25 times the basic rate.

Work and Efficiency

In cases of varied efficiency or piece - rate work, wages are divided in the ratio of the efficiency or the part of total work completed by each individual.

questions.question: If $3 \tan \theta = 2\sqrt{3} \sin \theta$, where $0^\circ < \theta < 90^\circ$, then find the value of $\frac{3}{4}\left(\frac{\operatorname{cosec}^2 2\theta + \cot^2 2\theta}{\sin^2 \theta + \tan^2 2\theta}\right)$:
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Given: 3 tan θ = 2√3 sin θ
⇒ 3 × (sin θ / cos θ) = 2√3 sin θ ⇒ cos θ = 3 / 2√3 = √3 / 2 ⇒ θ = 30°
Substitute θ = 30° in the expression: (3/4) × [ (cosec² 60° + cot² 60°) ÷ (sin² 30° + tan² 60°) ]
⇒ (3/4) × [ (4/3 + 1/3) ÷ (1/4 + 3) ]
⇒ (3/4) × [ (5/3) ÷ (13/4) ] = (3/4) × (5/3) × (4/13) = 5/13
∴ The correct answer is 5/13.

Alternate Method
Given:
3 tan θ = 2√3 sin θ

Formula Used:
tan θ = sin θ / cos θ
cosec θ = 1 / sin θ , cot θ = cos θ / sin θ

Calculations:
⇒ 3 × (sin θ / cos θ) = 2√3 sin θ
Since 0° < θ < 90°, sin θ = ̸ 0. Dividing both sides by sin θ:
⇒ 3 / cos θ = 2√3
⇒ cos θ = 3 / (2√3)
⇒ cos θ = √3 / 2
⇒ θ = 30°

We need to find the value of:

⇒ (3 / 4) × [ (cosec² 2θ + cot² 2θ) / (sin²θ + tan² 2θ) ]
Substituting θ = 30° into the expression:
⇒ (3 / 4) × [ (cosec² 60° + cot² 60°) / (sin² 30° + tan² 60°) ]

Using standard trigonometric values:

⇒ cosec 60° = 2 / √3 ⇒ cosec² 60° = 4 / 3
⇒ cot 60° = 1 / √3 ⇒ cot² 60° = 1 / 3
⇒ sin 30° = 1 / 2 ⇒ sin² 30° = 1 / 4
⇒ tan 60° = √3 ⇒ tan² 60° = 3

Putting these values in the expression:

⇒ (3 / 4) × [ (4/3 + 1/3) / (1/4 + 3) ]
⇒ (3 / 4) × [ (5/3) / (13/4) ]
⇒ (3 / 4) × (5 / 3) × (4 / 13)
⇒ 60 / 156
⇒ 5 / 13
∴ The correct answer is 5/13.

Additional Information
Trigonometric Identities

The three primary Pythagorean identities are: sin²θ + cos²θ = 1, 1 + tan²θ = sec²θ, and 1 + cot²θ = cosec²θ.

Values of Trigonometric Ratios

Key values to remember for 30° and 60° angles: sin 30° = cos 60° = 1/2, sin 60° = cos 30° = √3/2, and tan 60° = √3.

Signs of Trigonometric Functions

In the first quadrant (0° to 90°), all six basic trigonometric functions (sin, cos, tan, cosec, sec, cot) yield positive values.

questions.question: The tops of two buildings, 90 m and 55 m high, are connected by a metal wire. If the metal wire makes an angle $\theta$ with the horizontal and $\tan \theta = \frac{3}{7}$, what is the distance (in metres) between the two buildings?
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Difference in heights of the buildings = 90 - 55 = 35 m.
From the right - angled triangle formed, tan θ = Height Difference ÷ Distance.
⇒ Distance = Height Difference ÷ tan θ
⇒ Distance = 35 ÷ (3/7) = (35 × 7) ÷ 3 = 245 ÷ 3
⇒ Distance ≈ 81.66 m, which is estimated to 82 meter.
∴ The correct answer is 82 meter.

Alternate Method
Given:
Height of taller building = 90 m
Height of shorter building = 55 m
Angle of the metal wire with the horizontal = θ
tan θ = 3/7

Formula Used:
In a right - angled triangle, tan θ = Perpendicular ÷ Base

Calculation:
⇒ Difference in height (Perpendicular) = 90 - 55 = 35 m
⇒ Let the horizontal distance between the buildings be 'd'.
⇒ In the right - angled triangle formed, tan θ = 35 ÷ d
⇒ 3/7 = 35 ÷ d
⇒ 3 × d = 35 × 7
⇒ 3d = 245
⇒ d = 245 ÷ 3
⇒ d ≈ 81.66 m
⇒ The estimated distance is 82 meter.
∴ The correct answer is 82 meter.

Additional Information
Angle of Elevation

The angle formed by the line of sight with the horizontal when viewing an object located above the horizontal level.

Trigonometric Ratios

For any right - angled triangle, tan θ = Perpendicular ÷ Base, sin θ = Perpendicular ÷ Hypotenuse, and cos θ = Base ÷ Hypotenuse.

Pythagoras Theorem

In a right - angled triangle, the square of the hypotenuse is equal to the sum of the squares of the other two sides: Hypotenuse² = Perpendicular² + Base².

questions.question: x is the smallest number of 5-digits which when divided by 10, 15, 24, 35 and 42, leaves a remainder 7 in each case. The sum of the digits of x is:
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
LCM of the divisors (10, 15, 24, 35, 42) = 840.

The smallest 5 - digit number is 10000.

Smallest 5 - digit multiple of 840 = 10000 + (840 - 760) = 10080.
Since the remainder is 7 in each case, the required number x = 10080 + 7 = 10087.
Sum of the digits = 1 + 0 + 0 + 8 + 7 = 16.
∴ The correct answer is 16.

Alternate Method
Given:
The divisors are 10, 15, 24, 35, and 42.

The remainder in each case is 7.

The number x is the smallest 5 - digit number satisfying this condition.

Formula Used:
Required Number = (Multiple of LCM of given divisors) + Remainder

Calculation:
⇒ First, find the prime factorization of each divisor:
⇒ 10 = 2 × 5
⇒ 15 = 3 × 5
⇒ 24 = 23 × 3
⇒ 35 = 5 × 7
⇒ 42 = 2 × 3 × 7
⇒ LCM(10, 15, 24, 35, 42) = 23 × 3 × 5 × 7 = 840
⇒ The smallest 5 - digit number is 10000.
⇒ Now, divide 10000 by 840 to find the nearest multiple:
⇒ 10000 ÷ 840 gives a quotient of 11 and a remainder of 760.
⇒ The smallest 5 - digit multiple of 840 = 10000 + (840 - 760) = 10080.
⇒ To get a remainder of 7 when divided by the given numbers, add 7 to this multiple.
⇒ x = 10080 + 7 = 10087
⇒ Sum of the digits of x = 1 + 0 + 0 + 8 + 7 = 16
∴ The correct answer is 16.

Additional Information
LCM and Remainder Concept (Same Remainder)

When a number is divided by a, b, and c leaving the same remainder r in each case, the required number is of the general form: k × LCM(a, b, c) + r (where k is a positive integer).

LCM and Remainder Concept (Different Remainders)

When a number divided by a, b, and c leaves remainders p, q, and s respectively, such that the difference between the divisor and remainder is constant i.e., (a - p) = (b - q) = (c - s) = d, the required number is of the form: k × LCM(a, b, c) - d.

Highest Common Factor (HCF) Rules

To find the greatest number that will divide x, y, and z leaving remainders a, b, and c respectively, find the HCF of (x - a), (y - b), and (z - c).

questions.question: A and B together can complete a work in 8 days while B and C together can complete it in 12 days. A worked for 4 days, B worked for 6 days and then C finishes the remaining work in 11 days. In what time C alone can complete the work?
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Total work = LCM(8, 12) = 24 units.
Efficiency of (A + B) = 3 units/day, and (B + C) = 2 units/day.
Total work done: 4A + 6B + 11C = 4(A + B) + 2(B + C) + 9C = 24
⇒ 4(3) + 2(2) + 9C = 24 ⇒ 16 + 9C = 24 ⇒ C = 8/9 units/day.
Time for C alone = 24 ÷ (8/9) = 27 days.
∴ The correct answer is 27 days.

Alternate Method
Given:
Time taken by (A + B) together = 8 days
Time taken by (B + C) together = 12 days

A worked for 4 days, B worked for 6 days, and C finishes the remaining work in 11 days.

Formula Used:
Total Work = LCM of given days

Calculations:
Let the daily efficiency of A, B, and C be A, B, and C units respectively.
⇒ Total work done = 4A + 6B + 11C = 24

We can rewrite the equation by splitting the terms to match the known combined efficiencies:

⇒ 4A + 4B + 2B + 2C + 9C = 24
⇒ 4(A + B) + 2(B + C) + 9C = 24

Substitute the efficiencies of (A + B) and (B + C) from the table:

⇒ 4 × 3 + 2 × 2 + 9C = 24
⇒ 12 + 4 + 9C = 24
⇒ 16 + 9C = 24
⇒ 9C = 24 - 16
⇒ 9C = 8
⇒ C = 8/9 units/day
Now, calculate the total time C alone will take to complete the total work:
⇒ Time taken by C = Total Work ÷ Efficiency of C
⇒ Time taken by C = 24 ÷ (8/9)
⇒ Time taken by C = (24 × 9) ÷ 8
⇒ Time taken by C = 3 × 9 = 27 days
∴ The correct answer is 27 days.

Additional Information
Pipes & Cisterns

Conceptually identical to Time & Work. Inlet pipes have positive efficiency (filling work) while outlet pipes have negative efficiency (emptying work).

Work & Wages

Wages are strictly distributed in the ratio of the actual total work done by each individual, not merely based on their time spent or efficiency alone.

Alternate Days Work

Calculate the combined work done in one complete rotation cycle (e.g., 2 days for 2 people) and multiply by an integer to reach closest to the total work.

questions.question: A train X takes 2 hours less than a train Y to cover a distance of 192 km between two cities. Their average speeds differ by 16 km/hr. How long does the faster train take to cover the journey?
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
For such questions, the fastest method is checking the options to satisfy the given condition.

Let T be the time taken by the faster train, so the slower train takes (T + 2) hours.

Difference in speeds = 192/T - 192/(T + 2) = 16.
Check T = 4 hours from Option 2: Speeds are 192/4 = 48 km/hr and 192/6 = 32 km/hr.
Difference = 48 - 32 = 16 km/hr, which perfectly satisfies the condition.
∴ The correct answer is 4 hours.

Alternate Method
Given:
Distance between the two cities = 192 km
Time difference between trains X and Y = 2 hours
Speed difference between trains X and Y = 16 km/hr

Formula Used:
Speed = Distance ÷ Time

Calculations:
Let the time taken by the faster train (Train X) be T hours.
Then, the time taken by the slower train (Train Y) = (T + 2) hours.
⇒ Speed of the faster train = 192 / T km/hr
⇒ Speed of the slower train = 192 / (T + 2) km/hr

According to the given condition, the difference in speeds is 16 km/hr:

⇒ 192/T - 192/(T + 2) = 16

Dividing the entire equation by 16:

⇒ 12/T - 12/(T + 2) = 1
⇒ [12(T + 2) - 12T] ÷ [T(T + 2)] = 1
⇒ 24 ÷ (T² + 2T) = 1
⇒ T² + 2T = 24
⇒ T² + 2T - 24 = 0
⇒ T² + 6T - 4T - 24 = 0
⇒ T(T + 6) - 4(T + 6) = 0
⇒ (T - 4)(T + 6) = 0
Since time cannot be negative, T = 4 hours.
∴ The correct answer is 4 hours.

Additional Information
Relative Speed

When two bodies are moving in the same direction, Relative Speed = |S1 - S2|. When moving in opposite directions, Relative Speed = S1 + S².

Average Speed

Average Speed is the total distance traveled divided by the total time taken. For two equal distances covered at speeds S1 and S², Average Speed = (2 × S1 × S²) ÷ (S1 + S²).

Unit Conversion

To convert km/hr to m/s, multiply the speed by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/hr, multiply by 18/5.

questions.question: When the article sold at the rate of Rs.3753 earned a profit of 11% more than that of the loss incurred when the same article sold at the rate of Rs.1432. Find the Cost price of the article.
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Ratio of Loss to Profit = 100 : 111
Total difference in SP = 3753 - 1432 = 2321
Sum of ratio parts = 100 + 111 = 211 units
Value of 1 unit = 2321 ÷ 211 = 11
Loss = 100 units × 11 = ₹1100
Cost Price = Lower SP + Loss = 1432 + 1100 = ₹2532
∴ The correct answer is ₹2532.

Alternate Method
Given:
Selling Price 1 (SP1) = ₹3753 (Profit is earned)
Selling Price 2 (SP²) = ₹1432 (Loss is incurred)
Profit at SP1 is 11% more than the loss at SP².

Calculations:
⇒ Let the Loss incurred at SP² be 100x.
⇒ Profit = 100x + 11% of 100x = 111x
⇒ Difference in Selling Prices = SP1 - SP²
⇒ Difference = 3753 - 1432 = 2321
⇒ Also, Difference in Selling Prices = Profit + Loss
⇒ 111x + 100x = 2321
⇒ 211x = 2321
⇒ x = 2321 ÷ 211 = 11
⇒ Loss = 100x = 100 × 11 = ₹1100
⇒ Cost Price (CP) = SP² + Loss
⇒ CP = 1432 + 1100 = ₹2532
∴ The correct answer is ₹2532.

Additional Information
Basic Profit and Loss Structure

Profit occurs when SP > CP (Profit = SP - CP) and Loss occurs when CP > SP (Loss = CP - SP).

Gap/Difference Method

Whenever an article is sold twice producing a profit in one case and a loss in another, the numerical difference between the two selling prices always equals the sum of the profit and the loss amounts.

Equal Profit and Loss Case

If the profit amount earned is exactly equal to the loss amount incurred across two different selling prices, the Cost Price is exactly the average of the two Selling Prices: CP = (SP1 + SP²) ÷ 2.

questions.question: The average weight of all the students of a class is 43 kg. Four more students whose weights are 43 kg, 36.5 kg, 39.5 kg and 42 kg join the class. Now their average weight becomes 500 grams less than before. Initially the number of students is:
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Using Net Deviation: sum of deviations of new students from the initial 43 kg average is: (43 - 43) + (36.5 - 43) + (39.5 - 43) + (42 - 43) = 0 - 6.5 - 3.5 - 1 = -11 kg.

This total deviation of - 11 kg reduces the overall class average by 0.5 kg per student.

Total number of students = Absolute Total Deviation ÷ Decrease in Average = 11 ÷ 0.5 = 22.
Initial number of students = 22 (total) - 4 (new) = 18.
∴ The correct answer is 18 students.

Alternate Method
Given:
⇒ Initial average weight = 43 kg
⇒ Total weight of 4 new students = 43 + 36.5 + 39.5 + 42 = 161 kg
⇒ Decrease in average = 500 g = 0.5 kg

Formula Used:
Quantity Ratio = (Combined Avg - Avg 2) : (Avg 1 - Combined Avg)

Calculations:
⇒ Average weight of 4 new students = 161 ÷ 4 = 40.25 kg
⇒ Combined average of the class = 43 - 0.5 = 42.5 kg
⇒ Applying Alligation (as shown in the diagram):
⇒ Ratio of Initial Students to New Students = (42.5 - 40.25) : (43 - 42.5)
⇒ Ratio = 2.25 : 0.5 = 22.5 : 5 = 9 : 2
⇒ We know the new group has 4 students.
⇒ 2 units = 4 students ⇒ 1 unit = 2 students
⇒ Initial number of students = 9 units = 9 × 2 = 18
∴ The correct answer is 18 students.

Additional Information
Net Deviation Method

If new items join a group, the change in the average is equal to the sum of deviations of the new items from the old average, divided by the total number of items in the final combined group.

Alligation Rule

When two groups with averages A1 and A² are mixed to form a combined average Aw, the ratio of their quantities is n1 : n² = (A² - Aw) : (Aw - A1).

Weighted Average Formula

The overall average of multiple groups can also be verified using the standard formula Aw = (n1A1 + n2A²) ÷ (n1 + n²).

questions.question: A student walks from his house at 5 km/hr and reaches his school 10 minute late. If his speed had been 6 km/hr he would have reached 15 minutes early. Then what is the distance of his school from his house?
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
If distance is constant, Distance = (S1 × S²) ÷ (S² - S1) × Δt
Time difference Δt = 10 min late + 15 min early = 25 min = 25 ÷ 60 hours
Distance = (5 × 6) ÷ (6 - 5) × (25 ÷ 60)
Distance = 30 × (5 ÷ 12) = 12.5 km
∴ The correct answer is 12.5 km.

Alternate Method
Distance from Home to School

Home

School

Distance = D km
Speed: 5 km/hr | Time: Late by 10 min
Speed: 6 km/hr | Time: Early by 15 min

Given:
Speed 1 (S1) = 5 km/hRs. peed 2 (S²) = 6 km/hr
Time difference (Δt) = 10 min late + 15 min early = 25 min = 25 ÷ 60 hr

Formula Used:
Time = Distance ÷ Speed

Calculation:
Let distance be D km.
⇒ Time taken at 5 km/hr = D ÷ 5 hours
⇒ Time taken at 6 km/hr = D ÷ 6 hours
⇒ D ÷ 5 - D ÷ 6 = 25 ÷ 60
⇒ (6D - 5D) ÷ 30 = 5 ÷ 12
⇒ D ÷ 30 = 5 ÷ 12
⇒ D = (5 × 30) ÷ 12
⇒ D = 150 ÷ 12 = 12.5 km
∴ The correct answer is 12.5 km.

Additional Information
Average Speed

When a certain distance is covered at speed 'a' and the same distance is covered at speed 'b', the average speed for the whole journey is given by (2 × a × b) ÷ (a + b).

Relative Speed

If two objects move in the same direction at speeds S1 and S², their relative speed is |S1 - S2|. If they move in opposite directions, it is (S1 + S²).

Time & Distance Proportionality

If the distance is constant, speed and time are inversely proportional (S1 ÷ S² = T² ÷ T1). If speed is constant, distance and time are directly proportional.

questions.question: The diameter of a metallic sphere is 6 cm. The sphere is melted and drawn into a wire of uniform circular cross-section. If the length of the wire is 36 m, then what is its radius equal to?
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Equate the volumes directly: Volume of Sphere = Volume of cylindrical Wire.
⇒ 4/3 × π × R³ = π × r² × h
⇒ 4/3 × 33 = r² × 3600 (Converting 36 m to 3600 cm)
⇒ 36 = r² × 3600
⇒ r² = 1/100 ⇒ r = 0.1 cm
∴ The correct answer is 0.1 cm.

Alternate Method
Given:
Diameter of the metallic sphere = 6 cm
Radius of the sphere (R) = 6 ÷ 2 = 3 cm
Length of the uniform wire (h) = 36 m
Converting length to cm ⇒ h = 36 × 100 = 3600 cm
Let the radius of the circular cross - section of the wire be r cm.

Formula Used:
Volume of a Sphere = 4/3 × π × R³
Volume of a Cylinder (Wire) = π × r² × h

Calculations:
When an object is melted and recast into another shape, the total volume remains conserved.

⇒ Volume of the cylindrical wire = Volume of the metallic sphere
⇒ π × r² × h = 4/3 × π × R³
⇒ π × r² × 3600 = 4/3 × π × 33

Canceling π from both sides:

⇒ r² × 3600 = 4/3 × 27
⇒ r² × 3600 = 4 × 9
⇒ r² × 3600 = 36
⇒ r² = 36 ÷ 3600
⇒ r² = 1 / 100

Taking the square root on both sides:

⇒ r = √(1/100)
⇒ r = 1/10 = 0.1 cm
∴ The correct answer is 0.1 cm.

Additional Information
Principle of Recasting

When a 3D solid is melted and transformed into a completely different shape, its volume remains constant while the surface area may change.

Volume of a Sphere

The total 3D space occupied by a sphere of radius r is calculated using the standard formula V = 4/3 × π × r³.

Volume of a Cylinder

A circular wire is treated geometrically as a solid cylinder. Its volume is V = π × r² × h, where r is the radius of the circular base and h is the length or height of the wire.

questions.question: If \({\left( {\frac{3}{5}} \right)^x} \times {\left( {\frac{5}{3}} \right)^{2x}} = \;\frac{{625}}{{81}},\) then the value of x is:
questions.solution:
Solution

Given:
\((\frac{3}{5})^x \times (\frac{5}{3})^{2x} = \frac{625}{81}\)

Formula used:
(a/b)n = (b/a) - n
am × an = am + n

Calculations:
\((\frac{3}{5})^x \times (\frac{5}{3})^{2x} = \frac{625}{81}\)

⇒ \((\frac{5}{3})^{-x} \times (\frac{5}{3})^{2x} = (\frac{5}{3})^4\)
⇒ \((\frac{5}{3})^{-x + 2x} = (\frac{5}{3})^4\)
⇒ \((\frac{5}{3})^x = (\frac{5}{3})^4\)
⇒ x = 4
∴ The correct answer is option (2).

questions.question: P and Q enter into a partnership with investments of Rs. 1400 and Rs. 1800 respectively. They share half of the profit equally for running the business and the remaining profit in the ratio of their investments. If the difference in their shares of profits is Rs. 47, what is the total profit?
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Ratio of investments of P and Q = 1400 : 1800 = 7 : 9.

The first half of the profit is shared equally, so it creates zero difference in their total shares.

The difference of Rs. 47 comes entirely from the remaining half of the profit.

Difference in shares = (9 - 7) ÷ (9 + 7) of Half Profit = 2/16 × (Total Profit / 2) = Total Profit / 16.
⇒ Total Profit / 16 = 47 ⇒ Total Profit = 47 × 16 = 752.
∴ The correct answer is Rs. 752.

Alternate Method
Given:
Investment of P = Rs. 1400
Investment of Q = Rs. 1800
Difference in their profit shares = Rs. 47

Formula Used:
Profit Ratio = Investment of Partner 1 × Time : Investment of Partner 2 × Time

Calculations:
⇒ Ratio of investments = 1400 : 1800 = 7 : 9
⇒ Let the total profit be x.
⇒ First half of the profit = x/2 (divided equally)
⇒ P's share from first half = x/4, and Q's share from first half = x/4
⇒ Second half of the profit = x/2 (divided in investment ratio 7 : 9)
⇒ P's share from second half = (7/16) × (x/2) = 7x/32
⇒ Q's share from second half = (9/16) × (x/2) = 9x/32
⇒ Difference in their shares = Q's total share - P's total share
⇒ Difference = (x/4 + 9x/32) - (x/4 + 7x/32)
⇒ Difference = 9x/32 - 7x/32 = 2x/32 = x/16
⇒ Given difference = 47
⇒ x/16 = 47
⇒ x = 47 × 16 = 752
∴ The correct answer is Rs. 752.

Additional Information
Working and Sleeping Partners

When one partner actively manages the business (working partner), they typically receive a fixed percentage of the total profit as a salary before the remaining profit is divided according to the investments.

Compound Partnership

When partners invest money for different durations, the profit is shared based on the product of the capital invested and the time period. Profit Ratio = (C1 × T1) : (C² × T²).

Equally Shared Profit Component

Any portion of the total profit that is shared equally among partners does not affect the difference in their final profit shares. The net difference arises solely from the remaining profit distributed based on their investment ratios.

questions.question: A cube of side 15 cm is cut into 27 small cubes. Then find the ratio of the lateral surface area of the large cube to the total surface area of one of the small cubes.
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Number of small cubes = (A/a)³ = 27 ⇒ Ratio of sides (A/a) = 3.
Ratio of areas = (Lateral Surface Area of Large Cube) ÷ (Total Surface Area of Small Cube)
⇒ (4 × A²) ÷ (6 × a²)
⇒ (4/6) × (A/a)² = (2/3) × 32 = 6
∴ The correct answer is 6 : 1.

Alternate Method
Given:
Side of the large cube (A) = 15 cm
Number of small cubes formed = 27

Formula Used:
Volume of cube = (side)³
Lateral Surface Area of cube = 4 × (side)²
Total Surface Area of cube = 6 × (side)²

Calculations:
⇒ Volume of large cube = 27 × Volume of small cube
⇒ 153 = 27 × a³
⇒ 3375 = 27 × a³
⇒ a³ = 125 ⇒ a = 5 cm
⇒ Lateral Surface Area of large cube = 4 × 152 = 4 × 225 = 900 cm²
⇒ Total Surface Area of small cube = 6 × 52 = 6 × 25 = 150 cm²
⇒ Required Ratio = 900 / 150 = 6 / 1 = 6 : 1
∴ The correct answer is 6 : 1.

Additional Information
Total Surface Area of a Cube

It is the sum of the areas of all 6 faces of the cube. Formula: TSA = 6 × (side)²

Lateral Surface Area of a Cube

It is the sum of the areas of the 4 vertical side faces of the cube, excluding the top and bottom faces. Formula: LSA = 4 × (side)²

Volume of a Cube

It represents the total 3D space occupied by the cube. When a shape is cut or reshaped, the total volume remains conserved. Formula: Volume = (side)³

questions.question: With a 10% discount on the marked price, a seller earns a 5% profit. If the marked price is increased by 5% and two successive discounts of 5% each are offered, how much percentage profit does the seller earn?
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Ratio of Initial MP to CP = (100 + Profit%) ÷ (100 - Discount%) = 105 ÷ 90 = 7/6
New MP = Initial MP × 1.05 = (7/6) × 1.05 = 1.225 times of CP
Multiplier for two 5% successive discounts = 0.95 × 0.95 = 0.9025
Ratio of New SP to CP = 1.225 × 0.9025 = 1.10556
New Profit % = (1.10556 - 1) × 100 = 10.556% ≈ 10.5%
∴ The correct answer is 10.5%.

Alternate Method
Given:
⇒ Initial Discount (D) = 10%
⇒ Initial Profit (P) = 5%
⇒ Increase in Marked Price = 5%
⇒ Successive discounts on new MP = 5% and 5%

Formula Used:
⇒ MP = CP × (100 + P) ÷ (100 - D)
⇒ Equivalent Discount = d1 + d² - (d1 × d²) ÷ 100
CP = 100
MP1 = 116.67 + 5%
MP² = 122.5 - 9.75%
SP² = 110.56
Profit = + 10.56%

Markup

Calculations:
⇒ Let Cost Price (CP) = 100
⇒ Initial Selling Price (SP) = 100 + 5% of 100 = 105
⇒ Initial Marked Price (MP) = 105 ÷ (1 - 0.10) = 105 ÷ 0.90 = 116.67
⇒ New Marked Price = 116.67 × (1 + 0.05) = 116.67 × 1.05 = 122.5
⇒ Equivalent discount for two 5% discounts = 5 + 5 - (5 × 5) ÷ 100 = 10 - 0.25 = 9.75%
⇒ New Selling Price = 122.5 × (1 - 0.0975) = 122.5 × 0.9025 = 110.556
⇒ Overall Profit = New SP - CP = 110.556 - 100 = 10.556
⇒ Profit % = 10.556% ≈ 10.5%
∴ The correct answer is 10.5%.

Additional Information
Markup and Discount Relation

MP/CP = (100 + Profit%) ÷ (100 - Discount%). This direct ratio equation is highly useful for directly jumping between Marked Price and Cost Price without calculating the intermediate Selling Price.

Successive Discounts

Two successive discounts of x% and y% are structurally equivalent to a single effective discount of (x + y - xy ÷ 100)%.

Base of Calculations

Unless specified otherwise, Profit and Loss are always evaluated on the Cost Price (CP), whereas Discounts are strictly evaluated on the Marked Price (MP).

questions.question: If \(\frac{1}{3}A = 3B = \frac{3}{4}C\), then what is the value of \(A \∶ B \∶ C\)?
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Equate the given expression to 1: (1/3)A = 3B = (3/4)C = 1
⇒ A = 3, B = 1/3, C = 4/3
⇒ A : B : C = 3 : 1/3 : 4/3

Multiply by 3 to eliminate the denominators:

⇒ A : B : C = 9 : 1 : 4
∴ The correct answer is 9 : 1 : 4.

Alternate Method
Given:
⇒ (1/3)A = 3B = (3/4)C

Formula Used:
If xA = yB = zC = k, then A : B : C = (k/x) : (k/y) : (k/z)

Calculations:
Let (1/3)A = 3B = (3/4)C = k
⇒ A = 3k
⇒ B = k/3
⇒ C = 4k/3
Now, substitute the values of A, B, and C into the ratio form A : B : C:
⇒ A : B : C = 3k : k/3 : 4k/3

Divide the entire ratio by k:

⇒ A : B : C = 3 : 1/3 : 4/3

Multiply all terms by the least common multiple of the denominators (LCM of 3 is 3):

⇒ A : B : C = (3 × 3) : (1/3 × 3) : (4/3 × 3)
⇒ A : B : C = 9 : 1 : 4
∴ The correct answer is 9 : 1 : 4.

Additional Information
Compound Ratio

The compound ratio of two or more ratios is obtained by multiplying their antecedent and consequent terms respectively. For a : b and c : d, it is (a × c) : (b × d).

Inverse Ratio

The inverse ratio of a : b is b : a. If aA = bB, then the ratio A : B is equal to b : a.

Duplicate & Triplicate Ratios

The duplicate ratio of a : b is given as a² : b², and the triplicate ratio is a³ : b³.

questions.question: The ratio of the efficiencies of A, B and C is 4 \∶ 5 \∶ 3. Working together, they can complete that work in 25 days. A and C together will complete 35% of that work in:
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Efficiency ratio A : B : C = 4 : 5 : 3
Total efficiency = 4 + 5 + 3 = 12 units/day
Total work = 12 × 25 = 300 units
35% of work = 300 × 0.35 = 105 units
Efficiency of (A + C) = 4 + 3 = 7 units/day
Time taken = 105 ÷ 7 = 15 days
∴ The correct option is B.

Alternate Method
Given: Efficiency ratio of A, B and C is 4 : 5 : 3. They complete work in 25 days.
Formula Used: Total Work = (Combined Efficiency) × Time

Persons Time Work Efficiency

A - 300 / 4

B - 5

C - 3

A + B+C 25 12

Combined efficiency of A + B + C = 4 + 5 + 3 = 12 units/day
Total work = 12 × 25 = 300 units
⇒ Target work = 35% of 300
⇒ Target work = (35 ÷ 100) × 300 = 105 units
⇒ Combined efficiency of A and C = 4 + 3 = 7 units/day
⇒ Time taken by A and C = 105 ÷ 7 = 15 days
∴ The correct option is B.

Additional Information
Relationship between Efficiency and Time

Efficiency is inversely proportional to the time taken to complete a specific task (Efficiency ∝ 1 ÷ Time). If efficiency doubles, time taken is halved.

Total Work Calculation

Total work can be calculated by multiplying the combined efficiency of the group by the total number of days taken: Work = (Σ Efficiencies) × Total Days.

Work & Wages

Wages are generally distributed in the ratio of the work done by each individual, which is the product of their efficiency and the time for which they worked.

questions.question: A sum of ₹2,50,000 is invested for one and a half years at 12% per annum compound interest. What is the difference between the amounts received when the interest is compounded semi-annually and when it is compounded annually?
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Effective CI rate (annually) for 1.5 years at 12% = 12% + 6% + (12 × 6) ÷ 100 = 18.72%

Effective CI rate (semi - annually) for 3 half - years at 6% = 3(6) + 3(6)² ÷ 100 + (6)³ ÷ 10000 = 18 + 1.08 + 0.0216 = 19.1016%
Difference in effective rate = 19.1016% - 18.72% = 0.3816%
Difference in amount = 0.3816% of 2, 50, 000 = (0.3816 ÷ 100) × 250000 = ₹954
∴ The correct answer is ₹954.

Alternate Method
Given:
Principal (P) = ₹2, 50, 000
Rate (R) = 12% per annum
Time (T) = 1.5 years

Compounded Annually (1.5 years): ₹2, 50, 000 + 12% (1st yr)

₹2, 80, 000 + 6% (1⁄2 yr)

₹2, 96, 800

Compounded Semi - Annually (3 half - years): ₹2, 50, 000 + 6%

₹2, 65, 000 + 6%

₹2, 80, 900 + 6%

₹2, 97, 754

Difference = ₹2, 97, 754 - ₹2, 96, 800 = ₹954

Calculations:
⇒ Amount compounded annually (A1) = P × (1 + R/100)1 × (1 + (R/2)/100)
⇒ A1 = 250000 × (1 + 12/100) × (1 + 6/100)
⇒ A1 = 250000 × 1.12 × 1.06 = 250000 × 1.1872
⇒ A1 = ₹2, 96, 800
⇒ Amount compounded semi - annually (A²) = P × (1 + (R/2)/100)2T
⇒ A² = 250000 × (1 + 6/100)³
⇒ A² = 250000 × (1.06)³ = 250000 × 1.191016
⇒ A² = ₹2, 97, 754
⇒ Difference in amounts = A² - A1
⇒ Difference = 297754 - 296800 = ₹954
∴ The correct answer is ₹954.

Additional Information
Effective Rate Method

For 3 equal periods at rate R%, the effective compound interest rate is calculated as: 3R + 3R²/100 + R³/10000.

Half - Yearly Compounding

When interest is compounded semi - annually, the annual rate of interest is divided by 2 (R/2) and the number of years is multiplied by 2 (2T).

Fractional Year Compounding

If time is given in fractions like 1.5 years, the formula used for annual compounding is: A = P(1 + R/100)1 × (1 + (R/2)/100)1.

questions.question: A 10 feet long ladder leaning against a wall, reaches the wall at a point 8 feet high. By how much distance should the ladder be moved towards the wall so that its top reaches a point at 9.6 feet high?
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Initial base = √(10² - 8²) = √(100 - 64) = 6 ft
Final base = √(102 - 9.62) = √(100 - 92.16) = 2.8 ft
Distance moved towards the wall = 6 - 2.8 = 3.2 ft
∴ The correct answer is 3.2 ft.

Alternate Method
Given:
Length of the ladder (Hypotenuse) = 10 ft
Initial height of the wall (Perpendicular1) = 8 ft
Final height of the wall (Perpendicular²) = 9.6 ft

Formula Used:
Pythagoras Theorem: Hypotenuse² = Perpendicular² + Base²

Calculations:
Let the initial distance of the ladder from the wall be x ft.
⇒ 102 = 82 + x²
⇒ 100 = 64 + x²
⇒ x² = 36 ⇒ x = 6 ft
Let the final distance of the ladder from the wall be y ft.
⇒ 102 = 9.62 + y²
⇒ 100 = 92.16 + y²
⇒ y² = 7.84 ⇒ y = 2.8 ft
Distance the ladder moved towards the wall:
⇒ Distance = x - y
⇒ Distance = 6 - 2.8 = 3.2 ft
∴ The correct answer is 3.2 ft.

Additional Information
Pythagoras Theorem

In a right - angled triangle, the square of the hypotenuse is equal to the sum of the squares of the other two sides: a² + b² = c².

Pythagorean Triplets

Sets of three integers that satisfy the Pythagoras theorem. Common examples include (3, 4, 5), (5, 12, 13), and (8, 15, 17). The first part of this question directly scales the (3, 4, 5) triplet into (6, 8, 10).

Distance vs Displacement

While the ladder length remains constant, solving for the shifting horizontal and vertical distances requires treating the movement as two completely separate right - angled triangles.

questions.question: The difference between two numbers is 5. If 25 is subtracted from the smaller number and 20 is added to the greater number the ratio becomes 1 : 2. What is the greater number?
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Initial difference between the greater and smaller number = 5.

By adding 20 to the greater and subtracting 25 from the smaller, the new difference becomes: 5 + 20 - (-25) = 50.

The new ratio is 1 : 2, so the difference in ratio parts = 2 - 1 = 1 part.
Since 1 part = 50, the new greater number (which corresponds to 2 parts) = 2 × 50 = 100.
Original greater number = 100 - 20 = 80.
∴ The correct answer is 80.

Alternate Method
Given:
Difference between two numbers = 5

When 25 is subtracted from the smaller and 20 is added to the greater, the ratio becomes 1 : 2.

Formula Used:
Linear equations and ratio proportion concepts.

Calculations:
⇒ Let the smaller number be x.
⇒ Then, the greater number = x + 5
⇒ New smaller number = x - 25
⇒ New greater number = (x + 5) + 20 = x + 25
⇒ According to the question, the ratio becomes 1 : 2
⇒ (x - 25) / (x + 25) = 1 / 2
⇒ 2 × (x - 25) = 1 × (x + 25)
⇒ 2x - 50 = x + 25
⇒ 2x - x = 25 + 50
⇒ x = 75
⇒ The greater number = x + 5 = 75 + 5 = 80
∴ The correct answer is 80.

Additional Information
Ratio & Proportion Basics

When two quantities are in the ratio a : b, they can be represented as ax and bx, where x is a common multiplier.

Constant Difference Method

If the same value is added or subtracted to both parts of a ratio, the difference between the two numbers remains constant. This is highly useful in age - related problems.

Cross - Multiplication Method

For equations of the form a / b = c / d, the variables can be easily solved using cross - multiplication: a × d = b × c.

questions.question: Find the sum of the numbers between 400 and 600 such that when they are divided by 6, 12 and 16, there will be no remainder.
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Required numbers must be exactly divisible by the LCM of 6, 12, and 16, which is 48.

Multiples of 48 between 400 and 600 are 48 × 9, 48 × 10, 48 × 11, and 48 × 12.

Required Sum = 48 × (9 + 10 + 11 + 12)
Required Sum = 48 × 42 = 2016
∴ The correct answer is 2016.

Alternate Method
Given:
Divisors = 6, 12, and 16
Range = Numbers strictly between 400 and 600
Concept Used: A number is exactly divisible by a set of given numbers if it is a multiple of their Least Common Multiple (LCM).

Calculations:
⇒ Prime factorization of 6 = 2 × 3
⇒ Prime factorization of 12 = 22 × 3
⇒ Prime factorization of 16 = 24
⇒ LCM(6, 12, 16) = 24 × 3 = 16 × 3 = 48
⇒ We need to find all multiples of 48 that lie between 400 and 600.
⇒ Dividing 400 by 48, we get a quotient of 8.
⇒ The first multiple greater than 400 = 48 × 9 = 432
⇒ The maximum multiple less than 600 = 48 × 12 = 576
⇒ The valid numbers are: 432, 480, 528, 576
⇒ Sum of these numbers = 432 + 480 + 528 + 576 = 2016
∴ The correct answer is 2016.

Additional Information
Least Common Multiple (LCM)

The smallest positive integer that is uniformly divisible by two or more numbers. It is obtained by taking the highest power of each prime factor involved in the numbers.

Sum of Arithmetic Progression (A.P.)

Consecutive multiples of a number always form an Arithmetic Progression. The sum can also be calculated using the formula: Sn = n ÷ 2 × (first term + last term). Here, 4 ÷ 2 × (432 + 576) = 2 × 1008 = 2016.

Divisibility Rule

For a number to leave no remainder when divided by a group of divisors, it must be completely divisible by their LCM. If a remainder 'R' is specified, the general format of the number becomes (LCM × k) + R.

questions.question: A man and a woman can complete a task in 8 and 12 days respectively. In how many days will 2 men and 3 women be able to complete the task?
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Total Work = LCM(8, 12) = 24 units.
Efficiency of 1 man = 24 ÷ 8 = 3 units/day.
Efficiency of 1 woman = 24 ÷ 12 = 2 units/day.
Combined efficiency of 2 men and 3 women = (2 × 3) + (3 × 2) = 12 units/day.
Time required = Total Work ÷ Combined efficiency = 24 ÷ 12 = 2 days.
∴ The correct answer is 2 days.

Alternate Method
Given:
Time taken by 1 man = 8 days
Time taken by 1 woman = 12 days

Formula Used:
Total Work = LCM of given days

Calculations:
⇒ Efficiency of 2 men = 2 × 3 = 6 units/day
⇒ Efficiency of 3 women = 3 × 2 = 6 units/day
⇒ Total efficiency of 2 men and 3 women = 6 + 6 = 12 units/day
⇒ Time required = Total Work ÷ Total Efficiency
⇒ Time required = 24 ÷ 12 = 2 days
∴ The correct answer is 2 days.

Additional Information
Work and Wages

Wages are distributed in proportion to the total work done by each person. If people work for the same duration, wages are distributed in the ratio of their efficiencies.

MDH Rule

If M1 men do W1 work in D1 days for H1 hours per day, and M² men do W² work in D² days for H² hours per day, then: (M1 × D1 × H1) ÷ W1 = (M² × D² × H²) ÷ W².

Pipes and Cisterns

Calculations are the same as Time and Work. A pipe filling a tank has positive efficiency, while a leak or a pipe emptying the tank has negative efficiency.

questions.question: Sum of four consecutive multiples of 3 is 78. The largest of these number is:
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Average of 4 consecutive multiples of 3 = 78 ÷ 4 = 19.5

The average lies exactly between the 2nd and 3rd numbers in the sequence.

Since the gap between consecutive multiples is 3, the 3rd number = 19.5 + (3 ÷ 2) = 21

The 4th (largest) number will be the next multiple = 21 + 3 = 24
∴ The correct answer is 24.

Alternate Method
Given:
Sum of four consecutive multiples of 3 = 78

Calculations:
⇒ Let the four consecutive multiples of 3 be x, x + 3, x + 6, and x + 9.
⇒ According to the question, Sum = 78
⇒ x + (x + 3) + (x + 6) + (x + 9) = 78
⇒ 4x + 18 = 78
⇒ 4x = 78 - 18
⇒ 4x = 60
⇒ x = 60 ÷ 4 = 15
⇒ We need to find the largest of these numbers, which is x + 9.
⇒ Largest number = 15 + 9 = 24
∴ The correct answer is 24.

Additional Information
Consecutive Multiples

Consecutive multiples of any number n always maintain a constant common difference of n between them. They form an Arithmetic Progression (AP).

Average of an Arithmetic Progression

The average (mean) of any Arithmetic Progression is simply the average of its first and last terms. For an even number of terms, it lies exactly halfway between the two middle terms.

Sum of an AP

The sum of terms in an AP can be calculated as: Sum = Number of terms × Average. Therefore, finding the average first is often the fastest method to solve such series.

questions.question: In an office, 76% of the number of females is equal to the one-third of the number of males. What is the ratio of number of males to that of the females in the office?
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Given, 1/3 of Males = 76% of Females
⇒ M / 3 = (76 / 100) × F
⇒ M / 3 = (19 / 25) × F
⇒ M / F = (19 × 3) / 25 = 57 / 25
∴ The correct answer is 57 : 25.

Alternate Method
Given:
76% of the number of females is equal to^(1/3) of the number of males.

Formula Used:
Percentage value = (Rate ÷ 100) × Base value

Calculations:
Let the total number of males be M and the total number of females be F.
⇒ 76% of F = (1 / 3) × M
⇒ (76 ÷ 100) × F = M ÷ 3
⇒ (19 ÷ 25) × F = M ÷ 3

Rearranging the terms to find the ratio of M to F:

⇒ M ÷ F = (19 ÷ 25) × 3
⇒ M ÷ F = 57 ÷ 25
⇒ M : F = 57 : 25
∴ The correct answer is 57 : 25.

Additional Information
Ratio & Proportion Basics

A ratio compares two quantities of the same kind. The ratio of a to b is written as a : b or a ÷ b. The first term is called the antecedent, and the second term is the consequent.

Percentage to Fraction Conversion

To convert a percentage into a fraction, simply divide the percentage value by 100 and simplify. For example, 76% = 76 ÷ 100 = 19 ÷ 25.

Equivalent Ratios

Multiplying or dividing both terms of a ratio by the same non - zero number does not change the ratio. This property is highly useful to simplify complex fractional equations into simplest form.

questions.question: Find the value of $2 \operatorname{cosec}^2 23^\circ \cot^2 67^\circ - \sin^2 23^\circ - \sin^2 67^\circ - \cot^2 67^\circ$:
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Convert 67° angles to 23° using cot 67° = tan 23° and sin 67° = cos 23°.
⇒ 2 cosec² 23° tan² 23° - (sin² 23° + cos² 23°) - tan² 23°
⇒ 2(1 / sin² 23°) × (sin² 23° / cos² 23°) - 1 - tan² 23°
⇒ 2 sec² 23° - 1 - tan² 23° = sec² 23° + (sec² 23° - tan² 23°) - 1
⇒ sec² 23° + 1 - 1 = sec² 23°
∴ The correct answer is sec² 23°.

Alternate Method
Given:
2 cosec² 23° cot² 67° - sin² 23° - sin² 67° - cot² 67°

Formulas Used: sin(90° - θ) = cos θ
cot(90° - θ) = tan θ
sin²θ + cos²θ = 1
sec²θ - tan²θ = 1

Calculation:
⇒ 2 cosec² 23° cot2(90° - 23°) - sin² 23° - sin2(90° - 23°) - cot2(90° - 23°)
⇒ 2 cosec² 23° tan² 23° - sin² 23° - cos² 23° - tan² 23°
⇒ 2(1 / sin² 23°) × (sin² 23° / cos² 23°) - (sin² 23° + cos² 23°) - tan² 23°
⇒ 2(1 / cos² 23°) - 1 - tan² 23°
⇒ 2 sec² 23° - 1 - tan² 23°
⇒ sec² 23° + (sec² 23° - tan² 23°) - 1
⇒ sec² 23° + 1 - 1
⇒ sec² 23°
∴ The correct answer is sec² 23°.

Additional Information
Trigonometric Identities

The fundamental Pythagorean identities are sin²θ + cos²θ = 1, sec²θ - tan²θ = 1, and cosec²θ - cot²θ = 1.

Complementary Angles

Two angles are complementary if their sum is 90°. Key relations: sin(90° - θ) = cos θ, tan(90° - θ) = cot θ, and sec(90° - θ) = cosec θ.

Reciprocal Relations

Trigonometric ratios are related by reciprocal identities: cosec θ = 1 / sin θ, sec θ = 1 / cos θ, and cot θ = 1 / tan θ.

questions.question: The system of equations: 2x + 3y = 7 and (a - b)x + (a + b)y = 3a + b - 2 have infinitely many solutions:
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
For infinitely many solutions, the ratio of coefficients must be equal: a1/a² = b1/b².

⇒ 2 / (a - b) = 3 / (a + b)
⇒ 2a + 2b = 3a - 3b ⇒ a = 5b
Check options: Only Option 4 has a = 5 and b = 1, which perfectly satisfies a = 5b.
∴ The correct answer is a = 5, b = 1.

Alternate Method
Given:
2x + 3y = 7
(a - b)x + (a + b)y = 3a + b - 2

Formula Used:
For a system of equations to have infinitely many solutions, the ratio of their coefficients must be equal: a1 / a² = b1 / b² = c1 / c²

Calculations:
⇒ Here, a1 = 2, b1 = 3, c1 = 7
⇒ a² = (a - b), b² = (a + b), c² = (3a + b - 2)
⇒ 2 / (a - b) = 3 / (a + b) = 7 / (3a + b - 2)
⇒ Equating the first two parts:
⇒ 2 / (a - b) = 3 / (a + b)
⇒ 2(a + b) = 3(a - b)
⇒ 2a + 2b = 3a - 3b
⇒ a = 5b --- (Equation 1)
⇒ Equating the second and third parts:
⇒ 3 / (a + b) = 7 / (3a + b - 2)
⇒ 3(3a + b - 2) = 7(a + b)
⇒ 9a + 3b - 6 = 7a + 7b
⇒ 2a - 4b = 6
⇒ a - 2b = 3 --- (Equation 2)
⇒ Substituting a = 5b into Equation 2:
⇒ 5b - 2b = 3
⇒ 3b = 3 ⇒ b = 1
⇒ Substitute b = 1 back into Equation 1:
⇒ a = 5 × 1 = 5
∴ The correct answer is a = 5, b = 1.

Additional Information
Unique Solution

A system of linear equations has a unique solution if the lines intersect at exactly one point. The condition is a1 / a² = ̸ b1 / b².

No Solution

A system of equations has no solution if the lines are parallel and never intersect. The condition is a1 / a² = b1 / b² = ̸ c1 / c².

Infinitely Many Solutions

A system of equations has infinitely many solutions if the lines overlap entirely, meaning they represent the exact same line. The condition is a1 / a² = b1 / b² = c1 / c².

questions.question: A man sells 10 pens for ₹18 gaining 24%. How many pens should he sell for ₹1,530 to earn a profit of 55%?
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Using the proportional ratio: (Amount ÷ Quantity) ÷ (100 + Profit%) = Constant
⇒ (18 ÷ 10) ÷ 124 = (1530 ÷ N) ÷ 155
⇒ 1.8 ÷ 124 = 1530 ÷ (155 × N)
⇒ N = (1530 × 124) ÷ (1.8 × 155)
⇒ N = 680
∴ The correct answer is 680 pens.

Alternate Method
Given:
Selling Price (SP1) of 10 pens = ₹18
Initial Profit = 24%
Target Profit = 55%
Target Amount = ₹1530

Formula Used:
CP = SP × [100 ÷ (100 + Profit%)]
New SP = CP × [(100 + New Profit%) ÷ 100]

Calculations:
⇒ SP1 of 1 pen = 18 ÷ 10 = ₹1.80
⇒ CP of 1 pen = 1.80 × (100 ÷ 124) = ₹45/31
⇒ Target SP² of 1 pen for 55% profit = CP × (155 ÷ 100)
⇒ Target SP² = (45 ÷ 31) × (155 ÷ 100)
⇒ Target SP² = 45 × (5 ÷ 100) = ₹2.25
⇒ Number of pens = Total Amount ÷ Target SP²
⇒ Number of pens = 1530 ÷ 2.25
⇒ Number of pens = 680
∴ The correct answer is 680 pens.

Additional Information
Marked Price and Discount

Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price (MP). Formula: SP = MP × [1 - (Discount% ÷ 100)].

Successive Discounts

If two successive discounts of a% and b% are given, the effective single discount is (a + b - ab ÷ 100)%.

Dishonest Dealer

When a dealer sells goods at cost price but uses a false weight, the actual Profit% = [Error ÷ (True Value - Error)] × 100.
